### 1.1  Misc


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *In the payment landscape, payment processing is a complex process, where booking is just one of the steps. The Temenos Payments Hub (TPH) orchestrates the payment execution. The account status check, funds reservation and booking can take place at different stages of payment processing.*
> 
> **Applications:** `AC.ENTRY.PARAM`, `AC.INWARD.ENTRY`, `CATEG.ENTRY`, `EB.SYSTEM.ID`, `EXTERNAL.SEPA.DETAILS`, `GENERIC.ACCOUNTING.REQUEST`, `MS.PARAMETER`, `RE.CONSOL.SPEC.ENTRY` ... +1 more
> 
> **Key Fields:** *A*, *Attribute*, *Contra Acc*, *Contra Acct Categ*, *Contra Cr Txn Code*, *Contra Currency*, *Contra Dr Txn Code*, *Contra Entry* ... +25 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

Related topics:

- Temenos Transact Services

In the payment landscape, payment processing is a complex process, where booking is just one of the steps. The Temenos Payments Hub (TPH) orchestrates the payment execution. The account status check, funds reservation and booking can take place at different stages of payment processing.

TPH uses the internal Temenos Transact Deposit Demand Account interface to check the account status, reserve funds and raise bookings in an embedded manner. However, when a bank implements a third party payment system, these APIs must be invoked from that system or an ESB, and possibly from other solutions implemented by the bank like online channels, cards interfaces, and so on.

Depending on their enterprise architecture, banks can have multiple systems or interfaces to invoke the APIs for:

- Checking if a transaction can be applied on an account (cover request).
- Reserving funds on an account (reservation request).
- Booking an entry or entries on an account (booking request).

Temenos Generic Accounting Interface (GAI), also known as OFS clearing, accepts cover, reservation and booking requests sent by other banks’ systems to Temenos Transact.

Depending on the type of processing, a synchronous and/or asynchronous response(s) is sent by the GAI. Then, this response is forwarded by the Enterprise Service Bus (ESB) back to the request source system to take a decision on the payment processing.

The request messages are received through queues in the Temenos OFS Clearing proprietary format. The formatting to the Temenos request format, from the Temenos response format and routing are done in ESB.

The GENERIC.ACCOUNTING.REQUEST application allows the user to manually reverse a transaction that is successfully posted through GAI. This creates a booking reversal request, which is processed using the GAI mechanism.


##### Product Configuration

The main processing rules related to Generic Accounting Interface (GAI) messages are described in the AC.ENTRY.PARAM application and cover the following:

- System ID associated with the bookings
- Message layout – the header and the data items provided in the message
- Entry and fields separator
- Default transaction codes
- Contra-related options
- Accounting mode for exceptions handling
- Additional validations
- Duplicate check rule
- Suspense details
- Fund Transfer (FT) transaction type used in suspense posting
- Response options

A record must be created in the EB.SYSTEM.ID application for the System id indicated in AC.ENTRY.PARAM , AC.INWARD.ENTRY .

This appears in the accounting entries raised by GAI (populated in the STMT A dd D etail V alue field associated with the Add Detail Name PARENT.TXN.SYS.ID in STMT.ENTRY ) and indicates that the entries have been generated through GAI.

| Values in the Data Item field | Description |
|---|---|
| CONTROL TOTAL | Displays the total number of items in the request. If this is provided in the message, it is checked against the number of actual entries in the message. |
| SIGN | When the sign is not supplied in the request, the value in the header is used by default. |
| CURRENCY | When the currency is not supplied in the request, the value in the header is used by default. |
| LOCAL REF | Supplied at the header level and stored in the AC.INWARD.ENTRY record, which stores the header of the CSMBATCH message. |
| EXT.BATCH.REF | The batch reference provided in the batch message (if any) is not only populated in the batch entry in AC.INWARD.ENTRY , but also in the individual ones. For CSM and CSMBULK, this is populated in the accounting entries raised on the contra account and on the accounts specified in the request message; it will be stored in STMT.ENTRY / CATEG.ENTRY / RE.CONSOL.SPEC.ENTRY , in the ADD.DETAIL.VALUE field associated with the ADD.DETAIL.NAME field, which has the value “EXT.BATCH.REF”. |

The default entry delimiter is ‘_’ and the default field delimiter is ‘,’. In some markets or regions, these characters are included in the allowed character set and are used by customers when making payments. So, the banks must provide a different character than the default one.

The values can be specified in the Entry Delim iter and Field Delim fields in AC.ENTRY.PARAM . The characters used as delimiters are ` ! @ # $ % & * ( ) _ - + = [ ] { } ; / \ |

The Dr Txn Code and Cr Txn Code fields indicate the default transaction codes that are used if transaction code is not supplied in the request entry.

| Values in the Contra Entry field | Description |
|---|---|
| ENTRY | The balancing entry is raised for each entry indicated in the request. |
| CURRENCY.NET | Balance by currency, netting debit and credit entries, irrespective of the value date. If the entries that are part of an online posting message are netting for each currency to zero, a balancing entry is not raised. |
| CURRENCY | Balance by currency and sign, irrespective of the value date. A consolidated entry is created for all debit/credit entries, per each currency. |
| CCY.VAL.NET | Balance by value date and currency, irrespective of sign netting debits and credits. If the entries that are part of an online posting message are netting to zero per currency and per value date, a balancing entry is not raised. |
| CURRENCY.VAL.NET | Balance by currency, sign and value date. A consolidated entry is created for all debit/ credit entries, per each currency, sign and value date. |
| LOCAL | To raise balancing entries in the local currency irrespective of request currency. Balancing happens by value date, processing date, accounting date, and netting the debit and credit entries irrespective of sign. |
| CCY.PROC.NET | To allow balancing using currency, processing date, and netting debit and credit entries irrespective of sign. |

| Accounting Mode | In case of Error During Processing | In case of Override During Processing | No Error or Override During Processing |
|---|---|---|---|
| SAO | Posted to suspense account | Posted to target account or PL | Posted to target account or PL |
| SSS | Posted to suspense account | Posted to suspense account | Posted to target account or PL |
| SNP | No posting - rejected (Read Note | No posting –- rejected | Posted to target account or PL |

For CSM, CSMBULK and CSMBATCH, it is mandatory to be set as unique and implies that a record is created and stored for each entry in AC.INWARD.ENTRY .

The following type of responses are supported by GAI:

- Detail – Synchronous response, it returns the result and the type ID of the entry.
- Summary – Synchronous response, it returns the result only.
- ExtDetail – Asynchronous response through Integration Framework, it returns all the details available in the entry.
- ExtBatch – Asynchronous response through Integration Framework, it returns all the header details.

In AC.ENTRY.PARAM , the Interface Type field is set to Internal.


##### Business Events

When the Emit Business Event field in MS.PARAMETER is set as ‘Yes’, the business events representing the state change are emitted.

The following business events are emitted for Generic Accounting Interface tables.

| Business Event | Description |
|---|---|
| settlementService.checkFunds.fundAvailable | Event for a cover request when sufficient funds are available in the account |
| settlementService.checkFunds.fundNotAvailable | Event for a cover request when sufficient funds are not available in the account |
| settlementService.creditRequest.accountCredited | Event for a book request when the account is credited successfully |
| settlementService.creditRequest.creditFailed | Event for a book request when credit transaction to an account fails |
| settlementService.creditRequest.creditSubmittedForRetry | Event for a book request when credit transaction to an account submitted for a retry |
| settlementService.creditRequest.creditSuspended | Event for a book request when credit transaction to an account gets suspended |
| settlementService.debitRequest.accountDebited | Event for a book request when the account is debited successfully |
| settlementService.debitRequest.debitFailed | Event for a book request when debit transaction to an account fails |
| settlementService.debitRequest.debitSubmittedForRetry | Event for a book request when debit transaction to an account submitted for a retry |
| settlementService.debitRequest.debitSuspended | Event for a book request when debit transaction to an account gets suspended |
| settlementService.reserveRequest.fundReserved | Event for a reserve request when the funds are reserved successfully |
| settlementService.reserveRequest.reserveFundFailed | Event for a reserve request when the funds reserve fails |
| settlementService.transactionRetry.fundRecovered | Event for a transaction retry when the funds are recovered successfully |
| settlementService.transactionRetry.fundReserved | Event for a transaction retry when the funds are reserved successfully |

If this attribute is not set, all messages continue to update in existing way, that is, in the AC.INWARD.ENTRY table. |

### 1.2  Account Closure


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The banks can initiate account closure based on their requirement or on customer’s request. The Account Closure process enables the settlement of account balances and closure of the account.*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

The banks can initiate account closure based on their requirement or on customer’s request. The Account Closure process enables the settlement of account balances and closure of the account.

The banks can initiate closure in two ways:

- The banks can simulate account closure resulting in simulate closure bill, execute the simulation, and settle the account balance through any channel, thereby closing the account. Backdated closure can be done as long as the closure date is after the last schedule processing.
- The banks can close an account (without simulation) with a designated settlement account or beneficiary with payment order product as a single step. This could be either current or forward dated.

There are no specific differences for the closure of an account in the TBC, except the settlement of the balance. During a live or a scheduled closure, the system transfers the closure proceeds to another account within the TBC or publish an event for a settlement request to an account or beneficiary outside the TBC, which should be consumed by an external payments system, for further processing.

### 1.3  Account Creation


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Account Creation feature simplifies the long and tedious process of account opening. The banks can open current, savings, and notice accounts in any currency for single or multiple customers of different segments. Current, savings and notice accounts can be opened with or without passbook facili...*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | 🔧 Working With


#### 📖 Introduction

The Account Creation feature simplifies the long and tedious process of account opening. The banks can open current, savings, and notice accounts in any currency for single or multiple customers of different segments. Current, savings and notice accounts can be opened with or without passbook facility and it is possible to attach an overdraft facility to the accounts.

The system auto generates the account numbers for the accounts opened in the system. This account number can be used by the banks and the customer for all dealings. An account can have single ownership or multiple owners. The accounts can have more than one account number in multiple situations. Account nick names, legacy account numbers, IBAN numbers can be used as alternate account number in the system.

When the user tries to create an account using the interface, the system triggers the corresponding Activity in the TBC to complete the account creation process. During this process:

- The system evaluates the eligibility of the customer for this account product at the enterprise layer that is, the TEP (Temenos Enterprise Pricing).
- The user can attach an overdraft limit for the account only as a secondary limit .


#### 🔧 Working With

This section describes the process of creating different types of accounts, which are shown below:

- Customer Account - Retail and corporate account relationship with customer (Read Account Opening user guide for more information)
- Vostro Account - Client accounts
- Memo Accounts - Off balance sheet customer accounts that are opened in the system (Read Account Property Class user guide for more details)


##### Creating Accounts

While opening an account, the system defaults the customer from a new Arrangement Activity. The customers are added during account opening and can be added or removed anytime during the account life cycle.

An account can have single ownership or multiple owners. When there is a single owner, this owner is defaulted as the beneficial customer and for accounts with multiple owners, the customer role is mandatory. There can be other parties who play roles like power of attorney, authorised signatory.

Correspondence .

Document and image management features are not applicable to accounts opened in the TBC. The event released for account opening confirmation can be consumed by an external solution appropriate for Document and Image management.

### 1.4  Account Maintenance


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *In the life cycle of an account, the customer or the bank initiates the changes in the account related information. Following are some of the account maintenance activities:*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

In the life cycle of an account, the customer or the bank initiates the changes in the account related information. Following are some of the account maintenance activities:

- Changing the customer
- Changing the account officer
- Changing the product
- Updating the limit
- Changing debit or credit interest conditions
- Changing the capitalisation frequency
- Interim capitalisation of interest
- Interim make due of interest
- Applying or removing posting restrictions
- Resetting an inactive account
- Blocking or unblocking of funds
- Recording notice for withdrawal of funds
- Changing the statement frequency

When there is a request for any changes in an account through an API, the system updates the underlying account record in the TBC using the corresponding Activity.

- During a change customer or a change product, the system evaluates the eligibility of the customer for that account product at the enterprise layer, that is, TEP (Temenos Enterprise Pricing).
- The user can update any change in the limit for the account using the secondary limit .

### 1.5  Balances and Availability


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The system updates the account balances based on the booking, value and exposure dates of the financial transactions. This helps to maintain the future cash flows, ledger and available balances. The system performs a credit check based on the available balance.*
> 
> **Applications:** `AC.LOCKED.EVENTS`, `ACCOUNT`, `EB.AF.PARAM`, `EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Account Number*, *Av Auth Cr Mvmt*, *Av Auth Db Mvmt*, *Av Nau Cr Mvmt*, *Av Nau Db Mvmt*, *Avail Bal Upd*, *Available Bal*, *From Date* ... +9 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | 🔧 Working With


#### 📖 Introduction

The system updates the account balances based on the booking, value and exposure dates of the financial transactions. This helps to maintain the future cash flows, ledger and available balances. The system performs a credit check based on the available balance.

Based on the bank requirements, a specific amount in an account can be locked for a particular period. The user can record withdrawal notices for an account to ensure that funds are available for withdrawal.

The system updates the balances of an account in the TBC based on the booking date as it currently supports only trade dated accounting. However, the value date and the exposure date are still considered for interest calculation and availability respectively. It is possible to lock the funds including the secondary limit amount in TBC.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section deals with balances and the availability of funds.


##### Understanding Dates and Balances

When a transaction is posted in an account, different types of balances are updated based on the dates indicated in the transaction.

| Date | Description |
|---|---|
| Booking Date | Date on which the transaction is booked. |
| Value Date | Date from which the entry is included for calculation of interest. |
| Exposure Date | Date on which a credit entry is included in the cleared balance of an account. |

| Date | Lifecycle of Cheque |
|---|---|
| Value Date | The date on which the amount is credited to the account, hence, used only for interest calculation. This can be previous or same as the clearing date. |
| Exposure Date | The date on which the cheque is declared cleared by the bank and the funds are available for customers to withdraw. |
| Processing Date | If the bank is accepting a post-dated cheque, the processing date indicates the date on which the cheque clearing process began. |

The following table defines the field types of balances in an ACCOUNT record.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Open Actual Bal | This is the actual non-cleared or ledger balance of the account on the start of a day (SOD). |
| Open Cleared Bal | This is the cleared balance of an account on SOD, which includes the value of all entries (except any credit and reversal debit entries with exposure dates in the future). A future exposure date entry is updated on the particular day’s SOD. |
| Online Actual Bal | This is the actual balance of the account during the day and the value is same as the Open Actual Bal with authorised entries from SOD. Account balances are held in the EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES table. For an arrangement account, CURBALANCE holds the online actual balance. CURBALANCE - indicates the current or live value of property balance and indicates the account property name of a product in the model bank system. |
| Online Cleared Bal | This is the cleared balance of the account during the day. The value is same as the Open Cleared Bal with authorised entries from SOD (except any credit or reversal debit entries with exposure dates in the future). The Exposure Date Splitting feature helps to split a single amount to clear in separate periods. |
| Working Balance | This is the cleared balance of an account considering the unauthorised debits (but ignoring unauthorised credits and future authorised credits). This is the current balance of an account, which is used for checks done by the LIMITS system. During SOD, Working Balance is same as Open Cleared Bal and Online Cleared Bal If the cleared balance is USD 1000 and unauthorised debit is USD 100, then working balance is USD 900. |
| Available Bal | This helps to identify if any movements or transactions can generate a deficit of cash in client accounts, and anticipate the impact of a new transaction on pre-existing client commitments. |
| Open Available Bal | This is the SOD balance that consists of all authorised debits with value date before or same as the current date, along with all authorised credits with an exposure date before or same as the current date (excluding contract entries, such as the principal draw down of current loan value). |

The system updates the balances of an account in TBC based on the booking date as it currently supports only trade dated accounting. However, the value date and the exposure date are still considered for interest calculation and availability respectively.


##### Viewing Available Funds Ladder

This functionality provides the ability to view all forward and value dated account movements to the configured number of calendar days (forward from the current date). The available balance ladder is built by using the open available balance of that particular day.

The available balance can include unauthorised entries based on the configuration in the Balance Availability Property Class. The Available Bal attribute can be set to include unauthorised debit or credit (or) neither (or) both.

> **⚠️ Note:** As the authorised entries are always included, the Avail Bal Upd field is used to include unauthorised entries.

The EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES has all the movements as available balances in the below fields, unless a restriction is set in EB.AF.PARAM at transaction or application level:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Av Auth Db Mvmt | Authorised Debit Movements |
| Av Nau Db Mvmt | Unauthorised Debit Movements |
| Av Auth Cr Mvmt | Authorised Credit Movements |
| Av Nau Cr Mvmt | Unauthorised Credit Movements |

The system updates the balances of an account in TBC based on the booking date as it currently supports only trade dated accounting. However, the value date and the exposure date are still considered for interest calculation and availability respectively.


##### Balance Override Messages

The below messages are displayed when there is a shortfall or excess of funds in an account:

An account is linked to a limit, and there is an online debit transaction that results in overdrawn available balance on the value date of the transaction, to exceed its limit.

An account is neither linked to a limit nor shared balance pool, and there is an online debit transaction that results in the available balance to be negative on the value date of the transaction.

An account is linked to a limit and the available balances of all the accounts in limit falls short of the limit amount.

An account is linked to a limit and the transaction falls beyond the expiry date of the limit.

An account balance that has an AC.LOCKED.EVENTS record falls short on the level of the locked amount.

> **⚠️ Note:** Account parameter Locked With Limit field decides, if the locking of funds includes the limit available for the account.

The balance related override stated above is not applicable for an account in the TBC. The TBC has balances updated only based on the booking date as it currently supports only trade dated accounting. However, the value date and the exposure date are still considered for interest calculation and availability respectively.


##### Blocking Funds by UsingAC.LOCKED.EVENTS

The user can block the funds in a customer account by using AC.LOCKED.EVENTS .

> **⚠️ Note:** The Account Number , From Date and Locked Amount are mandatory fields.

When an account has a balance of USD 1000, overdraft limit of USD 500 and locked amount of USD1250, one of the following activity is performed:

- If Locked With Limit is set to Yes, a limit of USD 250 is available for the customer.
- If Locked With Limit is not set, a limit of USD 1000 is locked in which USD 500 is available for utilisation. Hence, any credit to the account up to USD 500 is locked automatically.

In TBC, the limit to overdraw an account can be updated as secondary limit only. Therefore, it is possible to lock the funds in those accounts including the secondary limit amount.


> **Related Applications:** `AC.LOCKED.EVENTS`, `ACCOUNT`, `EB.AF.PARAM`, `EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES`

### 1.6  Change Product


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The system uses Change Product activity to change the product of an account arrangement.*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.ARRANGEMENT`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Prod Eff Date,*, *Product Status*, *Product,*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | 🔧 Working With


#### 📖 Introduction

The system uses Change Product activity to change the product of an account arrangement.

The product of an arrangement can be changed , and this can be triggered manually or based on failed eligibility or as a scheduled event (either based on a set date or fixed period or relative to the customer’s date of birth).

When a customer requests for a Change Product, like an upgrade from a regular to a premium savings account in the TBC:

- The customer has to choose a product from the list of products available.
- The system evaluates the eligibility of the customer for the new product chosen through TEP (Temenos Enterprise Pricing).
- The system only evaluates if the new product is under the same product group and raises an error when not. There are no changes or limitations except the above stated items in the Change Product condition configuration or working.


#### 🔧 Working With

The arrangement accounts opened under a product, can be moved to another product by the bank. A few possible scenarios are listed below for easy understanding:

- Change of product because of failed eligibility. (For example, a staff account to a default account)
- Change of product due to the age of the customer. (For example, a child savings account to a regular savings account product)
- Change of product on customer's request. (For example, customers request to change their account from a notice savings account to a savings account)
- Change Product Activity (ACCOUNTS-CHANGE.PRODUCT-ARRANGEMENT) is used to change the product of the account.


##### Impact of Eligibility criteria

Failure in eligibility rule(s) due to changes in the demography of the customer, like attaining legal age or gaining employment or educational status. During such review failure, the system triggers a change product to the default product defined in the Eligibility condition.

The user can define the Eligibility condition for the account using the enterprise layer, that is, TEP (Temenos Enterprise Pricing). So the evaluation of the eligibility criteria and the trigger for the change product due to such reasons, take place outside TBC in the enterprise layer.


##### Bank Initiated Product change

The bank users initiate a Change Product activity on receiving customers' request for a changing the account product.

The Change Product Activity can be triggered manually or scheduled for a specific date or after a relative date (say birth date of customer).

It is possible to schedule the switch over product from one to another in advance by a specified number of days. This helps in intimating the customer in advance about the product change and gives way to negotiating with the customer before the actual change takes place.

The AA.ARRANGEMENT holds the product information of the arrangement. A set of multi-value fields namely Product, Prod Eff Date, Product Status are used to indicate the product status of arrangement.


> **Related Applications:** `AA.ARRANGEMENT`

### 1.7  Cooling Period


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *In certain regions, the legislation mandates that if customer prefers to close the account within a certain period from the account opening date, the bank should not charge the customer with any penalties like account closure charges. If any interest gets accrued so far, the bank waives the same if ...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Cooling Convention*, *Cooling Date Adj*, *Cooling Period*, *Cooling Waive Class*, *Cooling Waive Prop*, *Waive Bill Type*, *Waive Class*, *Waive Prop*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With


#### 📖 Introduction

In certain regions, the legislation mandates that if customer prefers to close the account within a certain period from the account opening date, the bank should not charge the customer with any penalties like account closure charges. If any interest gets accrued so far, the bank waives the same if the customer closes the account within the cooling period. This time is referred to as the cooling period.

There are no specific limitations with regards to the cooling period functionality for accounts in TBC.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The Cooling Period attribute defines a fixed length of time after arrangement creation. Within that time, the arrangement can be closed without incurring a penalty or by waiving accrued interest.

Banks can configure Cooling Period using the Closure property class. The Cooling Period , Cooling Date Adj , Cooling Convention , Waive Class , Waive Prop , Waive Bill Type attributes are related to the cooling period functionality.

- Banks specify the property class or property (Interest or Charge) for which a waiver or refund has to be done.
- By using the Cooling Convention attribute, the system calculates the cooling period in working days or calendar days.
- The Cooling Date Adj attribute can be used to adjust the cooling date to the next working day if the cooling date falls on a holiday.

When an account is pre-closed within the cooling period, only the Current Balance (CUR ) is considered and not the interest that is paid to the customer. Any Pay balances available in the arrangement are not reversed at the time of pre-closure. But the accruals from the last make due date are reversed at the time of pre-closure.


##### Product Condition – Closure

The Closure Property Class defines the cooling period for accounts product line. Within the cooling period date, if user is closing the account arrangement, then the system allows the account to be closed without interest and charges based on the configuration.

- The Cooling Period attribute defines the number of calendar days that the system considers to calculate the cooling period from arrangement creation date.
- The Cooling Date Adj attribute adjusts the cooling date to the next working day if it falls on a holiday.
- The user can configure the Cooling Convention attribute as 'Working Days' if the cooling period is calculated in working days 'Null' if cooling period is calculated on calendar days
- Property class level or property level choices are available for waiving or retaining the charge or interest applied during the cooling period using the Waive Class , Waive Prop and Waive Bill Type attributes.
- The user should configure the Waive Bill Type as ‘Current’ if the Interest property class or property is selected ‘All’ if the Charge property class or property is selected

Refer to the Closure section for more information.

- For Interest, only the current interest (accrued) can be waived. Interest which is already paid or capitalized cannot be waived or refunded.
- Due or Pay type of charges can be waived or refunded. Waiver or Refunded amount is adjusted against the account balance at the time of payoff.
- Credit or Debit Charges which are capitalized cannot be waived or refunded.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section orients the user to create cooling period.


##### Cooling Period using Closure

The cooling period allows the system to close the account within a stipulated time after the arrangement start date. The stipulated time is defined as the number of calendar days in the Closure property class.

When the customer chooses to close or cancel the account within the cooling period, the interest and charges are handled based on the attributes defined in the Closure property class.

The Closure product condition is defined as shown in the screenshot below for an account product. The cooling period is defined for seven days. The Interest property class is mentioned in the Cooling Waive Class field. Only the MAINTENANCEFEES property is defined in the Cooling Waive Prop field.

Arrangement was created on 15 Apr, 2022 and the cooling date for the arrangement is 22 Apr, 2022.

At the time of closure, account has below balances.

- Account Balance – USD 30,000
- ACCOPENINGFEE (Due Charge) – USD 250
- MAINTENANCEFEES (Due Charge) – USD 100
- Accrued Interest – USD 18.47

Account closure is triggered on 21 Apr, 2022 before the cooling date. During account closure, the system performs the following.

- Account Balance – Paid to the customer
- ACCOPENINGFEE – Capitalized against the account since the charge was not yet settled
- MAINTENANCEFEES – Refunded to the customer by creating an equivalent Pay bill. In this case, since the fee was not collected at the time of closure, the same got nullified by Pay bill (Since the MAINTENANCEFEES property is mentioned in the Closure condition for waiver)
- Interest Accrued – Reversed to the Banks PL account as the Interest property class is mentioned in the Closure condition for a waiver.

Since MAINTENANCEFEES is refunded, a pay-off bill is issued for the net amount of 29,750 USD (30,000 USD – 250 USD).

#### 📖 Introduction

Certain types of financial transactions require several account postings made to the same account, where the volume of these transactions is high and results in high number of postings across the account. This scenario occurs when the bank itself is on the one-side and the vostro or customer account on the other side of the transaction or when a bank has corporate or retail accounts that attract high volumes of transactions.

There are no specific differences in the TBC for handling of high-volume transactions.

### 1.9  Inactivity Dormancy


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Inactive or Dormant accounts are accounts without customer activity for a specified period. User-defined dormancy statuses are possible, based on the inactivity period. The banks can include any financial or non-financial activity in the check for last customer-initiated activity. The system can sen...*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS`, `AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY`, `AA.SCHEDULED.ACTIVITY`, `COMPANY`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Act Date*, *Dormancy Check Date*, *Dormancy Date*, *Dormant Check Date*, *Last Activity Date*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | 🔧 Working With


#### 📖 Introduction

Inactive or Dormant accounts are accounts without customer activity for a specified period. User-defined dormancy statuses are possible, based on the inactivity period. The banks can include any financial or non-financial activity in the check for last customer-initiated activity. The system can send alerts to customer periodically and levy charges at different stages of inactivity. A dormant account can be closed automatically after transferring the balance to an internal account.

The dormancy details of the arrangement can be handed off to the Customer Dormancy Monitor(CDM) system for customer level dormancy processing.

- In TBC, when the system has to generate an alert for a dormancy status, it generates an event that can be consumed by an external delivery system, used for handling alerts and notifications.
- Customer Dormancy Monitoring is not supported in Deposit TBC and must be handled through the external customer management solution. The dormancy information can be handed-off to the external customer capability as required to monitor the customer dormancy status.


#### 🔧 Working With

An account does not have a tenor based life cycle event and therefore remains active as long as there are qualified activities running on that account. When there are no such qualified activities running on the account for a certain period, the account is deemed as Dormant and there are certain system and business processes that have to be carried out on that account. Account inactivity can be set through Inactive marker in the Account Arrangement condition or the Dormancy Property Class. They are mutually exclusive. Read Account Inactivity Marker to know more about Inactivity marker in the COMPANY table.

The Dormancy Property Class works based on the theory that there are certain activities, which keep an account active. By monitoring them and keeping track of them, it is possible to evaluate the state of an account on a periodic basis during COB. The period is configurable at product level.

Dormancy processing comprises of system and business processes.

System processes

- Selecting the account as dormant
- Generating the reports of dormant accounts
- Automatically calculating dormancy charges

Business processes

- Banks trying to get in touch with customers (as part of KYC)
- Managing or monitoring such dormant accounts for fraudulent activities
- Closing the account

The definition of Account Dormancy is the absence of any customer-initiated transaction or activity on an account for a certain period, where the period can vary according to local regulations or a bank’s own internal policy. The system-driven transactions related to credit or debit interest application on the account and account maintenance fees (ledger fees), which are scheduled AA Activities, are not considered for dormancy purposes.

The Account Overview page displays the dormancy status.

The dormancy history is available as a drill down in the Overview page.

Currently the account's arrangement status is Inactive, now the user triggers the Manual activity “Set Dormancy” and moves the status of the account arrangement to Dormant. After authorisation the dormancy history for the arrangement is as below:

The user triggers another manual activity namely Reset Dormancy to move the status of the account to Active status. After authorising the activity manually, the overview screen is as below:

The system updates the Dormancy history for the account as Auto for the account after the status of the account arrangement is moved to Active.

> **⚠️ Note:** The process in the above enquiry states the way in which dormancy is monitored in this period. For example, when the account is manually moved to Dormant status, it requires a manual evaluation of its dormancy. This is indicated as Manual in the process. Likewise, when the account is manually moved to Active status, the system evaluates dormancy automatically as per the dormancy condition. This is indicated as Auto in the process.


##### Full-Fledged Dormancy Processing

- The definition of Inactivity or Dormancy evaluation includes financial and non-financial activities. The user can configure any AA Activity in the check for the last customer-initiated activity. No log Activities cannot be used for dormancy processing. However, Restrict Log Activity can be included as a qualifying Activity in dormancy processing. For a Nolog activity, the system does not record the transaction information in the activity log. On recording the activities in AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY , the system’s performance increases, and the size of activity history does not grow as well. However, there cannot be any activity charges or activity restrictions based on the transaction count and amount. Conversely, selecting Restrict Log allows the system to record the transaction count, amount, and initiation type in the cumulative fields of the AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY table. Thus, the user can configure dormancy condition that are dependent on the activity’s context details such as initiation type customer, while the size of the AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY table is kept manageable too. When a transaction is set as Restrict Log and it is a customer-initiated transaction type, then the context field stores it as a customer-initiated transaction in AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY . On the Dormancy evaluation date, the Last qualifying activity is verified against this Act Date in AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY and the system performs dormancy evaluation.
- Dormancy supports different statuses based on various Inactivity periods. The beginning of this Period is the account opening date. Subsequently, the beginning of this period is updated based on the Last Qualifying Transaction date. If there are multiple stages of dormancy configured in the system, then it schedules the next dormancy check based on the period of the next dormancy status.
- The system schedules an activity to run at the end of the monitoring period (user configured Dormancy Period) following the period start date. On the scheduled date, the system checks if the account has any qualifying activities.
- A Qualifying Transaction can be a customer initiated financial transaction (like a cash deposit or an ATM withdrawal) or such user activities as Change Product, Manual reset of a dormant account or manually transferring an account to dormant. It is fully configurable to specify which transactions are qualified to keep an account active.
- The system can run Exception Rules to exempt certain accounts from Dormancy processing. If the account has qualifying activities, then the system reschedules the next dormancy check based on the date of the last qualifying activity and the dormancy period. If the account does not have qualifying activities, the system runs the Exception rules (user configured) to get the final decision. Once confirmed, marks the account as dormant. If the Exception Rule returns a No, then the system does not mark the account as dormant. It reschedules the Check for Dormancy.
- The date of transferring an account to Dormancy (manually or automatically) is recorded in the Dormancy Date field
- The date of manual reset is treated as a Qualifying Activity.
- It is possible to attach charge component for each status of dormancy
- It is also possible to schedule a notification to be sent to customer for each stage of dormancy.
- On occurrence of a qualifying activity in a dormant account, the system resets the Accounts Dormancy status automatically. This option can be enabled for a specific dormancy status. A qualifying activity for dormancy need not qualify as a qualifying activity for reset dormancy and vice versa The dormancy status is reset only on authorisation of the activity. Auto reset is triggered only when the transaction is authorised by accepting all the overrides. INAO, INAU status activities do not reset dormancy status On authorisation of a back value dated qualifying activity, the dormancy status is reset effective the date of authorisation of transaction. During Auto Reset dormancy, the system finds the relevant Schedule Charge Activity related to any dormant status in AA.SCHEDULED.ACTIVITY and removes it. When an account is dormant, while trying to make a funds transfer (assume a qualifying dormancy auto reset) activity, the system raises an override highlighting that the account will be reset to active status if the activity is performed as funds transfer is a qualifying activity for dormancy auto reset. Upon authorisation of activity dormancy is reset by the system automatically.
- When there is a change in the Dormancy Period Product Condition (and proofed and published) It results in a re-scan of existing arrangements to reschedule Check for Dormancy or marks the account as dormant and schedules the next Check for Dormancy (if there are more than one Dormancy status configured) The dormancy date is either the date on which this change was done or a date in the past, depending on whether it was a new condition that was created or the prevailing condition was changed effective back dated. Any new arrangements created after this change picks the new Product Condition.


##### Customer Level Dormancy Processing

When customer level dormancy processing is configured for a particular dormancy status, the AA framework hands-off the value of Last Activity Date updated in AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS along with the dormancy status of the arrangement to Customer Dormancy Monitor (CDM).

- It is possible to notify the customer at various stages in lifecycle of a dormant account. The system generates an event to notify the customer on the dormancy status of the account on regular frequency.
- Customer Dormancy Monitoring is not supported in Deposit TBC and must be handled through an external customer management solution. The dormancy information can be handed-off to the external customer capability as required to monitor the customer dormancy status.


##### Dormancy Processing - Life Cycle

For example, Dormant: 12M

In all the stages mentioned below,

- The Last Activity Date is the date on which the latest qualifying activity happened and it is Effective Date of that Activity.
- Dormant Check Date is a test date arrived during run-time by calculating the latest date by which a qualifying activity should have happened. The system derives this date based on the current date and the dormancy period. This is not stored anywhere but used by the system during Check for Dormancy to determine if the account is required to be marked dormant. After this step, if it determines that the account has remained inactive, it runs the Exception rules (if any) to get the final decision. The date is derived from current system date to the extent of the dormancy period in the past. If today is 01 Mar 2015 and the Dormancy Period is 12M, then the Dormant Check Date is 01 Mar 2014.
- In all instances below, where it says Schedule Next Check for Dormancy, it means the system automatically schedules the Check for Dormancy.

- 01 Jan 2015 Create a new arrangement (account 1 and account 2): 01 Jan 2015 Schedule the next Check for Dormancy: 01 Jan 2016
- 01 Mar 2015 The customer makes a Cash Deposit (qualifying Activity) on both accounts Last Activity Date: 01 Mar 2015
- 01 Jan 2016 The system checks for dormancy during the COB of the scheduled date Dormant Check Date : 01 Jan 2015 Last Activity Date : 01 Mar 2015 Decision: Account is Active Schedule Next Check for Dormancy: 01 Mar 2016

- 01 Feb 2016 The customer makes a cash deposit on account 2
- 01 Mar 2016 The system checks for dormancy during the COB of the scheduled date Dormant Check Date : 01 Mar 2015 Account 1 Last Activity Date : 01 Mar 2015 Account 2 Last Activity Date : 01 Feb 2016 Decision: Account 1 is dormant Mark account 1 as dormant Update Account’s Dormancy status and status date Apply Activity Charge, if configured Schedule Dormancy Charge, if configured Schedule Next Evaluate Dormancy for next status (if configured) Decision: Account 2 is Active Schedule Next Check for Dormancy 01 Feb 2017

- 03 Mar 2016 Dormancy Criteria changed from 12M to 15M This results in a full scan of all arrangements under that product and the system reschedules the Evaluate Dormancy based on the new Product Condition In this example, Account 2’s Next Check for Dormancy becomes 01 May 2017 (15M from last qualified activity date of 01 Feb 2016) Account 1 which is already marked as dormant remains in that state but if there is a Next Check for Dormancy scheduled, it is recalculated based on the new Product condition. Dormancy Criteria changed from 12M to 9M This results in a full scan of all arrangements under that Product and the system reschedules the Evaluate Dormancy to the Activity Effective Date Activity Effective Date can be either today or in the past (if this was a back dated Product condition change). In the following COB, Evaluate Dormancy does its usual processing and mark the arrangement as Dormant, as appropriate.

- 03 Mar 2016 The user views the account 1 details and reset the dormancy Status. Run an Activity to Manual-Reset Dormancy Clear account 1’s dormancy status and status date Last Activity Date: Effective Date of the Reset Activity Apply Activity Charge if configured Remove any scheduled Dormancy Charge Re-Schedule Next Check for Dormancy for 03 Jun 2017 (15M)
- 01 Feb 2017 The system checks for Dormancy during the COB of the scheduled date Dormancy Check Date: 01 Nov 2015 Account 2 Last Activity Date : 01 Feb 2016 Decision: Account 2 is Active Schedule Next Check for Dormancy 01 May 2018 (15M)

- 02 Feb 2017 The user marks account 2 (which is Active as of use case above) as dormant. Run an Activity to Set Dormancy, in this case the system doesn’t check the number of days since the last qualified Activity date or account opening date (if no qualified activity is done). The system does the following: Run Exception rules. If the system returns No, an error appears to stop this Activity. Update the account’s dormancy status and status date Apply Activity Charge if configured Schedule Dormancy Charge if configured Schedule Next Evaluate Dormancy for next status (if configured) If this is the last status, then Next Check for Dormancy is not scheduled.

Based on Stage 4, account 1 is now active and Next check for Dormancy is 03 Jun 2017.

- 03 Jun 2017 The system checks for Dormancy during COB of the scheduled date Account 1 Dormancy Check Date : 03 Mar 2016 Last Activity Date : 03 Mar 2016 Account Balance: (50.00) (in Debit Balance Due to scheduled Ledger Fees) Decision: Account 1 is Dormant Run Exception Rule Decision Override: Account 1 is not Dormant Skip the Account Schedule Next check for Dormancy 03 Sep 2018 (15M)

- Scheduled Charges Ledger Fees: (Calculated) USD 10.00 Dormancy Fees: FLAT USD 5.00 Frequency: Monthly
- Account 2 is in Dormant Status as of 02 Feb 2017 (Use Case 5 above) Account Balance: USD 7.00
- 28 Feb 2017 Ledger Fees Capitalisation Issue Bill for USD 10.00 Invoke Charge Adjustment API Charge Adjustment API returns 7.00 Adjust Bill/Waive USD 3.00 Apply Ledger Fees: USD 7.00 Account Balance: USD 0.00 Dormancy Fees Capitalisation Issue Bill for USD 5.00 Invoke Charge Adjustment API Charge Adjustment API returns 0.00 Adjust Bill/Waive USD 5.00 Apply Dormancy Fees: USD 0.00

- 03 Mar 2017 The user views the account 2 details and resets the Dormancy Status. Run an Activity to Manual-Reset Dormancy Clear account 2’s Dormancy status & status date Last Activity Date : Effective Date of the Reset Activity Apply Activity Charge if configured Remove any scheduled Dormancy Charge Re-Schedule Next Check for Dormancy for 03 Jun 2017 (15M)
- 31 Mar 2017 Ledger Fees Capitalisation Issue Bill for USD 10.00 Invoke Charge Adjustment API No Adjustment since Account is Current/Active. Apply Ledger Fees: USD 10.00 Account Balance: USD (10.00) (In Debit Balance)

The TBC generates an event when the account is marked for closure due to dormancy.


##### Auto Closure of Dormant Accounts

Dormant Accounts can be closed automatically after the balances are transferred to the bank's internal account by the system on attaining a particular dormancy milestone.

The Dormancy condition is set in the Dormancy Property Class and Product Qualifiers can be used to configure auto closure of dormant accounts after the balance transfer automatically.

There are two stages of closure, while configuring a dormant account:

- A notice is sent to the customer when the arrangement is ready for closure.
- The unclaimed balance is moved and the arrangement is moved to closure. If the rules are satisfied then the system triggers closure activity otherwise the account is not to be closed. The new Activity is set as a trigger to run a certain set of rules defined under the Rule set. They are Account not in Debit No Posting Restrictions No Locked Funds The Rule set is configured in such a way that if all these Rules pass, then it results in a decision. The action to be taken upon the decision is to Close Account or ‘Not to Close Account’ As part of this Close Account, the system transfers all the balances of that account to the configured internal account and closes the account. The decision to send or not send a notice is made when the arrangement reaches the Dormancy Status of CLOSEREADY.

> **⚠️ Note:** As a result of force capitalisation at the time of auto closure or due to activity charges, the account having negative balances is not closed.

- The decision to send or not send a notice is made when the arrangement reaches the Dormancy Status of CLOSEREADY (configurable in Dormancy Product Conditions).
- Based on the setup of Dormancy conditions, the dormant account reaches the status of CLOSEREADY after the inactive period. This transition to CLOSEREADY happens by way of ACCOUNTS-SET-DORMANCY*CLOSEREADY event
- When this event happens, the system runs the rules defined under the Close.Ready.Notice Rule set The rule defined is to check if the account has a balance to send notification (bank defined activity charge) If it passes, then it arrives at the Decision.1result . Decision 1 results in a Send Advice Action Send Advice corresponds to SEND.NOTICE.DORMANT.ACCOUNT action. A Charge amount can be configured as Activity Charge for this named Activity.

In the TBC, it is possible to notify the customer when the account is marked for closure due to dormancy. The TBC generates an event for the same, which can be consumed by an external delivery system to send a notification.

- The ACCOUNTS-SET-DORMANCY*UNCLAIMED Activity is set as a trigger to run a certain set of rules defined under the Unclaimed.Close Rule set. The Rules are Account not in Debit No Posting Restrictions No Locked Funds
- The Rule set is configured in such a way that if all these rules pass, then it results in Decision.2.
- The Action to be taken upon Decision.2 is to Close Account, when the system transfers all the balances of that account to the configured internal account and closes the account.

The below screens display auto closure of current account with balance

As result of Force Capitalisation at the time of auto closure or due to activity charges, the account having negative balances or locked funds is not to be closed.

The below screens display auto closure of savings account with zero balance and locked funds


> **Related Applications:** `AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS`, `AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY`, `AA.SCHEDULED.ACTIVITY`, `COMPANY`

### 1.10  InitialFundingControl


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Banks can monitor the agreed initial funding on the account which is to be received by the agreed date.*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.ACTION`
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With


#### 📖 Introduction

Banks can monitor the agreed initial funding on the account which is to be received by the agreed date.

When the minimum funding requirement is not met:

- At the time of funding, decision can be made to restrict or raise a charge.
- At the end of monitoring period, decision can be made to settle the funds and close the arrangement.

This can be achieved by using appropriate set of configurations of Periodic Attributes and Product Qualifier Rules in Activity Restriction.

There are no differences for initial funding control and account cancellation feature in the TBC.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section describes the activity restriction definitions required to monitor the initial funding for an account along with its associated controls.


##### Monitoring Initial Funding

The account can be configured to accept the minimum balance allowed per account to be defined with a breakage action as error or to raise a charge.

This can be achieved by defining the activity restriction condition using the MINIMUM.INITIAL.BALANCE periodic attribute and INITIAL.BALANCE periodic attribute class.

As an example, consider the below activity restriction condition in which the account should be funded for an initial amount of USD 1000. In this case, the system is configured to raise an error when the customer credits the account for an initial amount that is lesser than USD 1000.

Additionally, it is also possible to levy a charge on the customer in case the initial funding rule is not satisfied.


##### Initial Funding Controls

The product qualifier rule definitions can use periodic attributes to monitor the agreed initial funding in the account. The frequency-based review rules for this evaluation can have a specific end of cycling counter.

If the account is not funded up to the minimum amount within the initial period, then the product qualifier rules in the Activity Restriction property condition can be defined to take a resultant action like sending a chaser to the customer for reminding the initial funding or triggering a settle payoff followed by an account closure at the end of the monitoring period.

Consider the minimum funding rule as configured with the MINIMUM.BALANCE periodic attribute to check if the minimum balance amount of USD 10,000 is maintained in the account.

The Product Qualifier Rules are configured in the Activity Restriction property condition as given below:

- Frequency based rule for initial funding is evaluated once in every seven days for two cycles. If the rule evaluation fails, then a resultant action is configured to inform the customer through a chaser.
- Frequency based rule for initial funding is evaluated once in every 14 days for one cycle. If the rule evaluation fails, then the resultant action is configured to settle payoff the account followed by an automatic closure based on the closure conditions. The resultant actions mentioned above can be a named activity defined in the AA.ACTION table.

In TBC, when the resultant action for the product qualifier rules defined in the Activity Restriction condition is to generate a chaser notice, the TBC generates an event that can be handed-off to an external delivery system to send a chaser.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section describes some illustrations for monitoring of initial funding in accounts along with its associated controls.


##### Monitoring Initial Funding

At the time of initial funding, if the minimum criteria configured by the bank is not met, then the initial funding itself can either be restricted or a charge can be raised for the same.

For example, when the initial funding criteria is set as USD 1000 as seen in the configuration page, if the customer makes the first credit to the account for USD 800, the system raises a validation indicating that the minimum funding requirement is not met.

On a case-to-case basis, the system can be configured to collect a charge as a penalty for not meeting the initial funding criteria.


##### Initial Funding Controls

Accounts that are not funded up to the minimum amount within the initial period can be closed automatically based on the Rule evaluations and the remaining funds can be credited to the settlement account.

The product qualifier rules in the Activity Restriction property condition can be defined for the end of period evaluations and the resultant action can be configured as mentioned here .

Consider the notice account is opened on April 5, 2021. The periodic evaluation for minimum initial funding is scheduled to run on the following dates:

- First periodic evaluation - April 12, 2021
- Second periodic evaluation - April 19, 2021

The notice account is defined with an initial funding rule to monitor if the account is funded up to a minimum initial amount of USD 10,000 within the initial period.

The account is not funded as on April 12, 2021. When the periodic evaluation is processed on April 12, 2021, an event is recorded as the rule fails and the resultant action is processed.

On April 19, since the account is not funded up to the minimum amount during the periodic evaluation, the account is automatically closed by triggering the ACCOUNTS-SETTLE-PAYOFF activity followed by an ACCOUNT-CLOSE-ARRANGEMENT.

The account is automatically closed during COB as the account is not funded up to the minimum initial amount.

The closure condition based on which the account is closed is given below.

- It is possible to define multiple rule sets to review and evaluate different conditions. For example, the third rule can be defined on top of the above illustration to monitor the minimum balance throughout the life of the arrangement. The rule can have resultant action to settle payoff the account followed by auto account closure according to closure property condition. This can be achieved without defining the number of cycles in the above example.
- If the auto-settlement instructions are configured along with closure type notice, then the system automatically settle payoff the account balance and closes the account based on the closure condition on the funds availability date.
- If there are any active notices when the notice account gets closed (as a result of any rule evaluation), they become obsolete.


> **Related Applications:** `AA.ACTION`

### 1.11  Interest Adjustments


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Retails Accounts are flexible and allows automatic recalculation and reposting of interest due to backdated activities. This is done on the next accrual or on the next capitalisation date.*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

Retails Accounts are flexible and allows automatic recalculation and reposting of interest due to backdated activities. This is done on the next accrual or on the next capitalisation date.

- For a correction performed during the next accrual, the system can also be configured to settle the revised amount to settlement account as a reversal and reposting.
- For correction performed on next capitalisation date, the interest adjustments are posted. If required, the correction can also be posted online by running a purpose built activity manually or by a service.
- When a back value dated interest correction is posted to an account, system can be configured not to result in unauthorised overdraft balance but create a new invoice bill for the difference .

There are no specific differences for interest adjustments in the TBC.

As mentioned in the Interest and Charges Posting feature in TBC, the settlement for current interest or back value dated interest correction can be,

- Capitalised to the same account or
- Collected from or paid to another account within the TBC or
- Forwarded as a settlement request to an account or beneficiary outside the TBC by publishing an event, which should be consumed by an external payments system for further processing.

---


### 1.12  InterestCharges Assessment


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The accounts can have fixed or floating rate of interest with different interest basis on different balance types. Negative rates are also supported.*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

The accounts can have fixed or floating rate of interest with different interest basis on different balance types. Negative rates are also supported.

Interest for the accounts can be calculated on tiered rates and, for overdraft accounts, the tiers can be based on the utilisation within and beyond the limit. When a temporary limit is sanctioned to the customer, the interest for the main , temporary and overdraft limits can be calculated on different tiered debit rates respectively. The interest tier amount thresholds are determined dynamically depending on the utilised and temporary limit amounts.

If a temporary limit is not set on the limit, any excess against the limit is interpreted as an unauthorised overdraft.

A deposit account can be linked to an overdraft account for arriving at the interest rate of this account based on the deposit rate.

For accounts with floating rate of interest, the customers can be notified, a certain number of days in advance about an upcoming floating interest rate change.

The banks can collect charges on a regular frequency. The charges can be triggered on occurrence of a specific Activity or if the terms and conditions of the product is breached. Charges can be collected immediately or on a periodic basis. Discounts and premiums can be selectively offered based on these charges.

The interest component in overdraft accounts can be based on the secondary limit feature updated from the external limit solution. The above described functionality related to temporary limit is not applicable for the TBC.

Linked rates feature, based on another deposit or account, is applicable in the TBC, only when the linked account or deposit is maintained in the same TBC.

Notifications for accounts are provided in the form of events which should be consumed by the appropriate external system for further processing.

---


### 1.13  InterestCharges Posting


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The accrued interest and charges are billed or invoiced at regular frequency to the customer.*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

The accrued interest and charges are billed or invoiced at regular frequency to the customer.

The billed amount is

- Capitalised to the same account or
- Collected from another account within the bank or
- Collected from another account outside the bank

It is possible to waive the calculated amount or defer the bill or offset bills as required.


##### Invoicing Capitalise Bills due to Insufficient Funds

If a back dated rate change results in over drawing the account, the system can be configured to utilise the account balance and the difference is raised as a new invoice bill. The system can also be configured to automatically settle this invoice (INV) balance from the settlement account for that back value date.


##### Interest Capitalisation Process with Restrictions

When interest is set as Pay in Payment Schedule, if the linked settlement account has a posting restriction (Post no Credits) applied, then the process can be handed-off to the Transaction Cycler.

In the TBC, the system bills or invoices the interests accrued, and charges levied to the customer at regular frequencies. The system combines the bills generated on the same day and the billed amount is:

- Capitalised to the same account
- Collected from another account within the TBC or
- Forwarded as a settlement request to an account or beneficiary outside the TBC

The features related to recycling the failed postings can be enabled using the Transaction Recycler configured at the GAI (Generic Accounting Interface) level.

> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

When the TBC replaces the existing system, live accounts in the legacy system must be migrated to the TBC. This procedure forms a part of the data migration process.
