##### Advance Payment of Instalments

The following section describes scenarios in advance payments.


##### Scenario 1 : Advance Payment Benefit from Principal and Interest Paid In Advance

Customers can make advance repayment of a bill ahead of the actual due date of the bill and get the benefit from both the principal and interest paid in advance. During an advance payment,

- The system settles the accrued interest till date, the remaining interest component paid by the customer is apportioned towards the principal.
- Thus, the principal is reduced both from the advance payment of principal and any interest component that is apportioned towards the principal.
- The interest accrual after the advance payment is on the reduced principal after the advance payment.

To achieve this, the Advance Payment Rule configuration is given in Configuration . It is possible to make advance payments with or without the bills generated in advance. However, periodic charges can be collected in advance only when bill is issued in advance. This kind of advance repayment is possible for all payment types excluding the payment types based on transaction amount and routines

It is possible to allow a payment in advance to settle the bills fully or partially by configuration of the Payment Rule Type. Banks can control the number of payments that can be made in advance using Advance Payment Restriction . When a bill in issued status is paid in advance, it is not treated as an advance payment. Hence, the value of Advance Payment Restriction configuration should be chosen accordingly.


###### Charges Settled in Advance

While advance payments are possible for all payment types except the payment types based on transaction amount and routines, it is recommended not to have calculated charges collected in advance.

When charges are part of the payment schedule, the customer can settle these charges in advance like any other advance payment. If the customer prefers to payoff the loan in this scenario, there is an option to refund the charge if it is an advance charge collected, or retain the charge if it is an obligatory charge. Only charges with the Advance Property Type are refunded to the customer during a payoff. Any other charge is understood as an obligatory charge and retained with the bank’s income.


###### Advance Repayment of the Last Bill

When the customer pays the last bill in advance, the periodic charges, charges, accrued interest till the advance repayment date and principal component are settled in the repayment order defined.

When customer pays the last bill based on the bill issued in advance, he would make the repayment for the full bill amount. The remaining amount after allocation of different components (difference between the interest component billed and the accrued interest) is parked in the Remainder Activity . As all other components are settled, the remaining amount is marked as UNC balance which is the final Remainder Activity .

In order to close the arrangement, the user must clear the unallocated credit balance using the adjust balance activity and the arrangement moves to Pending Closure status.


###### Amendments in Loan

Any modifications in the loan parameters such as rate change, disbursement, and so on after the bill is issued and before the advance payment, does not affect the issued bill and the changes are incorporated in the upcoming bills. During an advance settlement, the payment towards interest component settles the interest accrued till date of payment and the remaining amount paid towards interest is apportioned to the principal (irrespective of the bill holding an principal component). Some scenarios in interest only payments are described below. When a customer makes a payment to settle two bills in advance:

- The first bill’s repayment settles the interest accruals till date and the remaining amount is apportioned towards the principal.
- The second bill’s repayment is only towards the principal as there are no accruals for that cycle yet.
- The recalculation of interest amount happens after the payment transaction is completed and the loan term or repayment amount is recalculated based on payment schedule setup.
- The third bill after the advance payment carries the interest accruals from the advance payment date (of first bill) till the third bill due date. This bill contains the benefit from advance payment (The bill or repayment amount or term is recalculated due to the advance payment).

If there is a rate change in this loan after the advance payment, the difference in interest accruals from advance paid date till number of bills settled is accumulated and collected in the next bill.

When the customer makes an advance payment to settle one bill fully and the second bill partially:

- The first bill’s repayment settles the interest accruals till date and the remaining amount is apportioned towards the principal.
- The second bill is advanced, and the partial payment is apportioned towards that bill.
- The recalculation of interest amount happens after the payment transaction is completed, changing the term or amount based on payment schedule setup.
- The payment schedule projector displays the recalculated payment amount after the advance payment of bill. The bill settled partially in advance displays the actual settlement amount after recalculation only on the due date of the bill (or when the bill is settled in advance fully).

If there is a rate change in this loan after the advance payment, the difference in interest accruals from advance paid date till number of bills settled are accumulated and collected in the next bill. In this case, the second bill is partially settled, so schedule projector of the second bill includes the difference in accruals and the bill on due date (or another advance payment) includes the difference in interest accruals.


###### Changes in Arrangement post Advance Settlement

When there are changes in loan parameters such as rate change, disbursement etc., after the bill is settled in advance (irrespective of bill issued in advance) the settled bill is not changed.


###### Advance Payments in a Suspended Loan

When a loan is suspended, the accruals are not posted to PL. Instead, it is posted between the ACC SP balance and the ACC balance.

If the bill in this suspended loan is settled in advance, the repaid amount is settled against the accrued portion of interest and the remaining amount is settled against the outstanding principal. The upcoming bills are recalculated to accommodate for the customer benefits from both principal and interest paid in advance. The ACC SP balance is cleared and transferred to PL only after the loan moves to Performing status.

The accounting related features and processing are handled by an external GL system for loans in TBC. Therefore, to complete the accounting related to advance payments in a suspended loan, the TBC generates an event, which can be captured by the connected external GL (General Ledger) system.


###### Advance Payment in Charged Off Loan

Once a loan is charged off, the system does not allow advance payments to be processed.


###### Illustration - Advance Payments with Linear, Interest only, Charges and Periodic Charges bill

As Advance Payment is set to Full, partial settlement of bills in advance is not possible in this setup. Any funds remaining after the advance settlement is moved to unallocated credit as per Remainder Activity setup.

The advance payment settles the interest accruals as on the advance payment date and the remaining amount is settled against the outstanding principal, thus, benefitting the customer with a reduced payment which takes effect from the next bill onwards.

1,000,000 - 904.12 - 83,333.33 - 8287.68 - 83,333.33 = USD 824,141.54

- The remaining amount of USD 12114.61 apportioned towards the principal component which is USD 83,333.33.

As the bill is not settled fully, the system raises a due bill on the next due date 19 Jun (or on the next advance payment date) for the accruals from advance settlement date till that date and the remaining principal namely USD 804,241.54. The interest accrual after this advance payment is on this reduced balance. Thus the benefit from the advance payment of principal and interest is passed to the customer.

###### Amendments in Loan

The following is an example with rate change and partial settlements.

During an advance repayment, when the bill is settled in full, the current interest cycle is closed and the interest accruals for the next period is started from that day’s COB.

During a partial advance payment, the bill is not settled in full, and the remaining amount is made-due on the due date or collected during the next advance repayment.

| Column 1 | Column 2 | Column 3 |
|---|---|---|
| Interest | USD 250 | Interest accrued till July 15 |
| Principal | USD 9750 | Remaining amount is apportioned to principal |

| Column 1 | Column 2 | Column 3 |
|---|---|---|
| Interest | USD 251.39 | Interest accrued till July 15=(100,000*3.6/100*20/360)+(100,000*3.7/100*5/360) |
| Principal | USD 9,748.61 | Remaining amount is apportioned to principal |


##### Scenario 2: Advance Payment with Customer Benefit (Only from Principal)

When the bank wants the customer to pay in advance only one mortgage loan bill and receive a benefit only from the principal paid in advance, by settling the bill as-is billed, the setup as mentioned in the Configuration has to be in place.

The above-mentioned configuration is the recommended setup. With this setup, the customer can pay only the issued bill in advance. The interest period moves to the next billing date after this advance bill is repaid. The repayment amount is settled against the bill components as-is billed.


###### Advance Repayment of the Last Bill

When the customer pays the last bill in advance, the accrued interest till the advance repayment date is settled. The repaid unaccrued portion of the interest component in the bill is stored as a positive accrual balance in ACC and this is reflected in the Total Repay Amount (TOT.RPY.AMT) field in AA.INTEREST.ACCRUALS . The remaining amount is apportioned and settled against the outstanding principal. Thus, the issued bill is settled as-is billed.

To close the arrangement, the user must clear the positive ACC balance using the Adjust Balance activity and the arrangement moves to Pending Closure status.

> **⚠️ Note:** The system can have a positive balance in ACC at the time of regular maturity as a result of advance payments. In such scenarios, the positive ACC at the time of maturity should be cleared from the arrangement using an Adjust Balance activity effective the last advance payment date (or) last payment date.


###### Amendments in Loan

Any modifications in the loan parameters such as rate change, schedule change and so on, after the bill is issued and before the advance payment, does not affect the issued bill and the changes are incorporated in the upcoming bills. During an advance settlement, the payment towards the interest component settles the interest accrued till the advance payment date. The remaining amount is apportioned towards unaccrued component of interest and stored in the Total Repay Amount (TOT.RPY.AMT) field in AA.INTEREST.ACCRUALS . Thus, the accrued interest ends up having a positive balance after the repayment.

Consider the following scenario in interest only payments feature:

When the customer makes a payment to settle two bills in advance:

1. The first bill’s repayment settles the interest accruals till date and the remaining amount is apportioned towards the unaccrued portion of the interest component.
2. The second bill’s repayment also settles the unaccrued portion of the interest and updates the bill as settled. There is no recalculation as the complete repayment is towards the interest and is settled against the unaccrued portion of the interest.

If there is a rate change in this loan after the advance payment, the difference in interest accruals from advance paid date till number of bills settled is accumulated and collected in the next bill.


###### Changes in Arrangement post Advance Settlement

When there are changes in loan parameters such as rate change, schedule change and so on, after the bill is settled in advance (irrespective of bill issued in advance) the settled bill is not changed.


###### Advance Payments in Suspended Loan

When a loan is suspended, the interest accruals are not posted to PL. Instead, it is posted to the ACC SP balance against ACC balance.

When this bill is settled on the due date, the due balance is settled against the settlement account and the SP balance remains as such. The ACC SP balance is cleared only after the loan resumes the Performing Status and the amount in the SP balance is moved to PL.

In a similar scenario, if the bill is settled in advance, then the due interest amount is settled with the settlement account, but the SP balance is cleared only after the loan resumes the Performing status.

The accounting related features and processing are handled by an external GL system for loans in TBC. Therefore, to complete the accounting related to advance payments in a suspended loan, the TBC generates an event, which can be captured by the connected external GL (General Ledger) system.


###### Advance Payment in Charged-off loan

Once a loan is charged off, the system does not allow advance payments to be processed.


###### Illustration of Advance Payments with Progressive Payments, Charges and Periodic Charges Bill

The payment schedule as on Apr 16, 2021 is as shown below. The Apr 17, 2021 bill is issued on Apr 7, 2021.

The bills issued in advance with their bill details are given below.

The balances and interest accruals prior to the advance payment are:

Post an advance payment of USD 160,000, the bill is settled as-is.

The interest component is settled as billed, and the remaining amount is settled against the outstanding principal, thereby the customer benefits from a reduced principal.

The interest accruals are stored in ACC as positive accrual amount and the excess interest component is stored in the Total Repay Amount field of AA.INTEREST.ACCRUALS .

The bill details of the settled bills are as follows:

The bill details of the cancelled bills are as follows:

- One day ‘s interest accrual on the outstanding principal of USD 929,658.78 = USD 254.7

The bills settled in advance are moved from the Advance Repayments section to the Repayments section in the Bills tab of the Arrangement Overview page.

There is no change in the Payment Schedule and the bill details.

In this case, only the two bills issued in advance are settled because the Advance payment rule condition has Advance Payment Restriction set to BILLED.


##### Scenario 3: Advance Payment with No Customer Benefit

During an advance payment of a loan instalment, it is not mandatory that a benefit should be passed on to the customer. In such cases, the bills are treated as settled in advance, but the balances are updated on the actual due date of the bill. For this, the system must be setup as mentioned in the Configuring Advance Payment of Installments section.


###### Periodic Charges Settled in Advance

It is not possible to settle periodic charges in advance when the Advance Settle Date field is set as Due in AA.PAYMENT.RULE.TYPE . The system triggers an error when such a case arises.


###### Request Payment Holiday with Advance Settlement

When the customer has made an advance payment and requests a payment holiday after that, the user has to manually request for the payment holiday after the advance settled bills.

Inspite of the upcoming bill being settled, if the user requests the payment holiday effective upcoming bill, the system reverses the advance settlement (as part of the reverse replay process) and declares a holiday for the upcoming bills. The funds of the advance payment are used to settle the bills after this payment holiday.

> **⚠️ Note:** It is a rare scenario where the customer requests a payment holiday after an advance payment. In such cases, care must be taken to request the holiday from the desired date (either upcoming bills or after the advance settled bills).


###### Advance Repayment of the Last Bill

It is possible to do an advance payment towards the last bill of the loan contract when the system is configured with Advance Settle Date field set as Due. The system settles the bill components as-is and on the maturity date the arrangement moves to Pending Closure status.


###### Amendments in Loan after Advance Settlement

When the upcoming bill amounts are changed due to any life cycle event of the loan such as rate change, schedule change, term change, partial prepayment or principal decrease, disbursement, etc., the settlement of those bills in advance payment are also changed accordingly. The system reverses the advance settlement of the bills and replays the bill generation as well as the advance payments as applicable. The Bill Status and Settle Status are marked as per the revised advance settlements for the new bill amounts.

In this scenario, the system modifies the bill components differently based on whether the bill was issued in advance or not.

- When the bill is not issued in advance, but an advance payment is made to settle an upcoming bill and a rate change, schedule change, disbursement, etc. take place, the system reverse replays the payment made in advance and apportions the paid amount to the new bill amount. Thus, the total bill amount is modified.
- When the bill is issued in advance, but an advance payment is done to settle an upcoming bill and a rate change, schedule change, disbursement, etc. take place, the system reverse replays the payment made in advance and apportions the paid amount to the modified bill components. Thus, the total bill amount is not modified, however, the components of the bill gets adjusted.

The following section describes some scenarios in Constant payments where the first bill is issued in advance and the second bill is not yet issued.

When the customer makes a payment to settle two bills fully in advance:

1. The first bill’s amount settles the first bill’s interest and principal components as-is billed. The ADV balance holds the advance amount for the bill from the advance payment date till the due date.
2. The second bill’s amount settles the second bill’s interest and principal components as-is billed. The ADV balance holds the advance amount for the bill from the advance payment date till the due date.
3. Both the bills have bill status as Settled .

If there is a rate change in this loan after the advance payment, the system reverse replays the advance payment, and generates a new total bill amount to include the difference in interest accruals (due to the rate change) till the due date.

When the customer makes an advance payment to settle the first bill (which is issued in advance) fully and the second bill (which is not yet issued) partially:

1. The first bill’s amount settles the interest and principal components as-is billed. The ADV balance holds the advance amount for the bill from the advance payment date till the due date. The Bill status is Settled .
2. The second bill’s amount settles the interest and principal components to the extent of the amount paid in advance. The ADV balance holds the advance amount for the bill from the advance payment date till the due date. The Bill Status is Advanced . On the due date, the remaining portion of the bill which is still not settled is made-due and the Bill Status continues to be Advanced till the customer repays the full bill amount.

If there is a rate change in this loan after the advance payment, the system reverse replays the advance payment and generates a new total bill amount that includes the difference in interest accruals due to the rate change. Thus, the total bill amount is modified based on the rate change and the amount paid in advance is apportioned to this new bill amount.

The accounting related features and processing are handled by an external GL system for loans in TBC. Therefore, to complete the accounting due to amendments in loan after an advance payment is processed, the TBC generates an event which can be captured by the connected external GL (General Ledger) system.


###### Chargeoff

When the bank decides to chargeoff a loan, the system considers the advance payments also. It books the payment in advance to Account, Interest and Charge Chargeoff PL.

If the charged-off loan is configured with Advance Settle Date as Due in the payment rule type, the ADV CO and ADV CUST balance types hold the funds received in advance (till the due date) for the company and customer books respectively.

For the chargeoff accounting, the unaccrued portion of the interest paid in advance is stored in the ACC CO and ACC CUST balance types as a positive balance. These positive interest accruals in Cust and Co balances indicate the advance payment in the company and customer books respectively. As the loan accrues, the positive balance reduces till the due date of the loan.

On the due date there is no bill for the DUE CUST whilst the positive balance in the ACC CO is cleared.

However, If the loan is charged off, the system does not allow advance payments to be processed.

The accounting related features and processing are handled by an external GL system for loans in TBC. Therefore, to complete the accounting related to handling advance payments which were made before the loan was charged-off loan, the TBC generates an event, which can be captured by the connected external GL (General Ledger) system.


###### Advance Payments in a Suspended Loan

If the loan is in non-performing status (that is, the loan is suspended), then the system does not allow advance payments to be processed.

##### Tax on Advance Payment

When an advance payment is received but the payment rules direct it to be credited to unallocated credit (LENDING-CREDIT-ARRANGEMENT), then the UNCACCOUNT funds can be applied to the upcoming payments on the schedule date. To achieve this, the regular repayment activity of the LENDING-SETTLE-PAYMENT.RULES activity class should be configured in APPLY.PAYMENT (Repay from Credit Balance) field in Payment Schedule condition.

For an advance payment received through the repayment rules that trigger and settle the bills in advance, the repayment generates the bill in advance and settles them. This is achieved by Advance Payment field in Payment Rule Condition.

### 3.13  Change Product


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Change Product functionality allows the user to change the product of the live arrangement within the product group.*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS`, `AA.ARRANGEMENT`, `AA.PRODUCT.GROUP`
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With


#### 📖 Introduction

The Change Product functionality allows the user to change the product of the live arrangement within the product group.

When a customer requests a Change Product for a loan contract in the TBC:

- The customer chooses a product from the list of products available in the interface for example at the TPM (Temenos Product Manager) level.
- The eligibility of the customer for the new product chosen is evaluated at the Enterprise layer, for example, at the TEP (Temenos Enterprise Pricing) level.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The LENDING-CHANGE.PRODUCT-ARRANGEMENT Activity is triggered during Change Product. The Change Product Property Class allows the user to:

- Change the product of a live arrangement to another product within the same AA.PRODUCT.GROUP .
- Set the Change Product initiation type to manual or automatic.
- Set the Change Product Activity on a specific date or after a specific period (6M, 12M).
- Define the number of days by which the Change Activity must happen in advance to the scheduled date of change product, this is helpful to negotiate the terms of new product.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Change Product Activity can be triggered manually or automatically based on the Product Condition setup.


#### 🔧 Working With

In the below screenshot the change product is configured in next five months. The details are recorded in the AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS application.

The Change Product Activity is scheduled for the arrangement.

- The AA.ARRANGEMENT application specifies the status of the product. The status of the old and current products display as: PROCESSED - when the arrangement moves from old product to new product, the status of old product is updated. CURRENT - when the arrangement is running on the current product. SCHEDULED - when the product is scheduled for a future date status.

### 3.14  Chargeoff


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *For financial and regulatory reasons, a bank is required to charge-off the principal balance of a loan. This may be determined by the bank, or can occur after bank examiners determine a borrower to be high risk and/or the loan is considered under-collateralised. Also, the customer is unaware that hi...*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS`, `AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY`, `AA.BILL.DETAILS`, `AA.INTEREST.ACCRUALS`, `CATEG.ENTRY`, `RE.CONSOL.SPEC.ENTRY`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Bill Type*, *Charge Off Amount*, *Charge Off Percentage*, *Charge OffOrder*, *Charge off Amount*, *Charge off Percentage*, *Chargeoff Category*, *Chargeoff Special Income* ... +13 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With


#### 📖 Introduction

For financial and regulatory reasons, a bank is required to charge-off the principal balance of a loan. This may be determined by the bank, or can occur after bank examiners determine a borrower to be high risk and/or the loan is considered under-collateralised. Also, the customer is unaware that his loan has been charged off; the customer’s loan record remains intact and payments are processed accordingly.

Charge-off is not a loan default. Loan default is where the borrower has failed to make a payment for an extended period of time, whereas charge-off is when there is no longer a reasonable expectation of further payments. The customer is not aware of charge-off and related activities in his loan.

The bank may charge-off the principal balance of a loan due to reasons like loan is deemed doubtful. The loan may or may not be in non-accrual status during a charge-off. The pending receivable in the form of principal, charges and interest of a loan can be completely charged off in a single stroke or the loan principal alone can be can be charged off fully, partially or in a series of partial charge-off transactions on loan principal.

When the user triggers charge-off of a loan through an API, the system triggers the corresponding Activity in the TBC to complete the charge off process. The TBC generates an event, which can be captured by the connected external GL (General Ledger) system to complete the accounting related to charge off. The features related to handling charge-off under FASB regulations are not applicable for loans in TBC.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The key features of the charge-off functionality are as follows:

- The customer is unaware of the charge-off. The customer’s loan record remains intact and the payments are processed accordingly (described under shadow accounting)
- A shadow record holds the charged-off amounts, etc for the bank's books
- The charge-off is done in a single activity or it can also be done in parts.
- Multiple partial charge-off transactions are possible and they are recorded accordingly, for the bank's balances.
- The calculation of interest continues in the charge-off balance.
- A full or partial charge-off can be reversed and corresponding changes to the shadow record are updated.

Read the Chargeoff Property Class for more information on the configuration of an arrangement being charged off.


##### Accounting Condition for Charge-off

When a charge-off is triggered, the loan principal has to be moved from the assets of the bank and booked in the PL indicated in the Chargeoff Category for the Account Property or Property Class itself.

For a full charge-off, the billed and unbilled components (properties) are to be charged off. For such interest and charge property or Property class, the Chargeoff Category and Chargeoff Special Income are used. Read Partial Charge-off or Charge-off in Parts for more information on special income.

During a full charge-off, the charge properties in the form of activity charges, rule break charges, periodic charges are also charged off to the respective Chargeoff Category given.


##### Dual Accounting

All activities that affect the principal or an interest balance require dual accounting (that is, accounting on the customer and the bank balances). The following lists some of the key activities which require dual accounting:

- Make Due
- Apply Payment
- Age Bill
- Credit or Debit Arrangement


##### Make Due Accounting

Each time the principal or interest is made due, AA raises entries that credit current balances (that is, CUR and ACC ) and debit due balances (that is, DUE and DUE ). Once a charge-off has occurred, these debits and credits happen on the customer balances (that is, the CUST versions) and bank balances.


##### Apply Payment Accounting

Although dual accounting is required for applying a credit to the loan, a different order of payment is required and the charge-off balances need to be credited once the bank balances are exhausted.


##### Ageing Accounting

When the Overdue Property Class is configured, each time that principal or interest is aged, AA raises entries that credit the existing due or delinquent balances (for example, DUE or DEL ) and debit the next ageing balance (for example, DEL and DEL ). Because of this internal accounting (which many other banking systems do not do), the system raises bank entries as well as the customer entries.


##### Partial Charge-off or Charge-off in Parts

The banks require the ability to process full or partial charge-off of the loan principal. This is achieved using the Charge-off Property Class. The LENDING-CHARGEOFF-ACCOUNT Activity triggers the charge-off in parts. The Charge-off Property Class dictates the order in which the account balances are impacted (for example, current first vs. oldest aged balance first) and the application order to be observed when applying a principal or interest payment to the bank balances.

- Charge-Off increase or decrease
- Extraordinary Income (this can occur when a loan is repaid in its entirety but the book interest is less than the customer interest due to accelerated repayment of principal)

In case of the customer fully repaying the loan, there is a remainder on the loan due to the lesser bank interest that is accruing as a result of the charged-off principal. The remainder or difference, ends up in the ACC -CO balance and this amount has to be debited and then PL credited (as extraordinary income). This scenario occurs only when the calculation source for the INTEREST Property is defined as total outstanding principal that is, current + due and age principal. PL for extra-ordinary income should be defined in Chgoff Special Income attribute of the Accounting Property Class.

When a loan has been charged-off, there are certain situations where the Credit Arrangement Activity (which credits UNC ) can result in a credit accrual in the banks’ books and this leads to confusing accounting entries. To avoid this situation, a new restriction code is added to the Activity to prevent a credit to UNC if that credit results in a credit bank principal balance.

When the LENDING-CHARGE-OFF-ACCOUNT Activity is triggered, the charge-off amount is based on the charge-off order.

- If the charge-off order is set to NEWEST.FIRST, then the amount is allocated from CURACCOUNT balances first. If any remainder amount exists, then it is allocated for bills (new to old).
- If the charge-off order is set to OLDEST.FIRST, then the amount is allocated from bills (old to new). If any remainder amount exists even after allocating the account Property amounts from bills, then the charge-off amount is allocated from CURACCOUNT balance.

When the LENDING-CHARGE-OFF-ACCOUNT Activity is triggered and if the Txn Amount is greater than zero, then increase charge-off is triggered and if Txn Amount is less than zero, then decrease charge-off processing is triggered.

- If the charge-off order is set to NEWEST.FIRST, then the amount is allocated from due account charge-off balances (Old to New) first. If any remainder amount exists, then the account property balance is allocated from CURACCOUNT balance.
- If the charge-off order is set to OLDEST.FIRST, then the amount is allocated from CURACCOUNT charge-off balance. If any remainder amount exists even after allocating the account property amounts from CURACCOUNT balance, then charge-off amount is to be allocated from due or overdue charge-off bill balances (New to Old) balance.

> **⚠️ Note:** The order in which balances are to be impacted can be defined based on the status of the loan. This option is available in Chargeoff Property Class and Payment rules Property Class.

| Balance | Source |
|---|---|
| ACCINTEREST | CURACCOUNT |
| ACCINTERESTCO | CURACCOUNTCO |
| ACCINTERESTCUST | CURACCOUNTCUST |

- If a LENDING-CREDIT-ARRANGEMENT is processed, then the amount credited to UNC also credits UNC CUST.
- If a LENDING-DEBIT-ARRANGEMENT is processed, then the amount debited from UNC is also debited from UNC CUST.

To complete the accounting related to balance updates in a charged-off loan, the TBC generates an event, which can be captured by the connected external GL (General Ledger) system.


##### Handling Charge-off under FASB Regulations

For handling charge-off under certain specific regulations (FASB), the bank user uses the CHARGEOFF-REPORTING activity. The user can trigger the LENDING-CHARGEOFF-REPORTING activity and specify the required Charge off Amount or Charge off Percentage .Read Working with Handling Charge-off under FASB Regulations for more information.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Charge off Amount and Charge off Percentage fields can be updated only through the LENDING-CHARGEOFF-REPORTING activity.

The features related to handling charge-off under FASB regulations are not applicable for loans in TBC.


##### Write-Offs

During a negotiation with a borrower, the bank can agree to write off a portion or all of the principal balance of a loan. A write-down is a portion of the loan that the bank agrees and is not repaid by the borrower. The bills are not generated and interest is not calculated on the write-off balance. The loan may or may not be in non-accrual status when processing a write-down. The system can write-off the loan principal partially. The banks require the ability to process full or partial write-off. This is achieved using the balance maintenance activities. The key features of write-off are as follows:

- The write-off amount has been deemed as uncollectable or forgiven
- The customer is aware, that a portion of their loan has been removed or marked as uncollectable.
- The repayment schedule is adjusted based on the remaining principal balance after the write-down.
- Both the shadow and the customer records have the written-off amounts (if a charge-off is already performed).
- Multiple write-off transactions should be allowed and recorded accordingly for bank's and customer’s balances (if a charge-off is performed)
- The interest is not calculated on the written-off transaction and the written-off amount is treated as amount that cannot be recovered.

> **⚠️ Note:** Charge-offs and Write-downs are not mutually exclusive. There may be situations when both occur on the same loan.

Partial write-off of balances can be performed using the Write-Off Balance Maintenance Activity. In case if a part of a charged-off amount is to be written-off, then the order in which the write-off amount is to be allocated, is determined by the Writeoff Order attribute in the charge-off condition. The order can be defined as BANK FIRST or BANK LAST. In a partial charge-off scenario, the option can be chargeoff the BNK balances first or the chargeoff balances first using this option. In a partial write-off, the system ensures the write off amount mentioned is less than or equal to the value of the bank’s CUR balance.

> **⚠️ Note:** Partially writing off any DUE or AGE balances is done by writing off individual bills that contribute to those balances.


##### Different Repayment Order for Non-Accrual Loan

A different payment application order can be specified for a non-accruing loan. This option can be different for applying the payments to CUST and chargeoff balances. The choices are indicated in the Payment Rules and Charge off Property Classes respectively.


##### Applying Payment Received

The payment allocation in loans that have charge-off can be different. The payment rule is different for the bank and the customer balances. This is usually based upon the value of the book balances and the status of the loan (for example, partially charged-off, fully charged-off or non-accrual).

The payment allocation for customer balances is done based on the definition in Payment Rules. The bank and charge-off balances is appropriated based on the definition in Charge-off Property Class. Similar to the Payment Rules, the Charge-off Property Class also allows the user to define the order in which bank and charge-off balances need to be appropriated and the order can be defined differently based on status of the loan, that is, Performing or Suspended.

In addition to the above, the Charge OffOrder attribute in the Chargeoff Property Class allow the users to set the order in which the account balances is appropriated upon charging off a loan.

When there is a payment received in a loan that is charged off, the payment received is apportioned against the outstanding CUST balances as per the payment rules given in the Payment Rules Property Class. Likewise, for the bank recovery, the payment received is apportioned against the chargeoff balance thereby apportioning the CO balances as per the payment rules in the Chargeoff Property Class. Here both CUST and CO balances are contingent balances.

The actual non-contingent entry for the payment done by the customer, reduces the chargeoff PL. Read Extraordinary Income in Accounting Events section for more information on excess payment.

In TBC, when customer makes a repayment to a loan that is charged-off, the TBC generates an event, which can be captured by the connected external GL (General Ledger) system to complete the accounting.

Read Configuring Loan Charge-off for more information on how to configure Charge-off for a loan.


#### 🔧 Working With

Working with Loan Charge-off Key Features Charge-off is different from writing off the arrangement. The key features of charge-off are: A full or multiple partial charge-off transaction is possible. The interest on the charge-off balance should accrue, but is not passed to income. Reversal of charge-off transactions is possible Removal from charge-off or partial removal from charge-off (that is, a lessening of the charge-off amount) is possible as well. Dual accounting –that is, having two sets of books, the customer record vs. the bank record and applying payments independently to the two records. The charge-off feature is available for the Lending Product Line. The Charge-off Property has to be included in the product for charging off an account. Activity Class - Charge-off Full/Complete Charge-off The LENDING-CHARGEOFF-ARRANGEMENT Activity Class is used for charge-off of an arrangement. The complete outstanding in the loan is charged off. Partial Charge-off or Charge-off in Parts It is possible to charge off a loan, in parts. The LENDING-CHARGE-OFF-ACCOUNT Activity Class is used to charge-off the Account Property balance, based on the charge-off order. This is used to both charge-off an amount of principal (that is, increase charge-off amount) and to reduce the charge-off (that is, decrease the charge-off amount) if required. If a loan is being charged-off for the first time, this Activity is responsible for creating the charge-off balances as well as the customer’s shadow balances. Handling Charge-off under FASB Regulations For handling charge-off under certain specific regulations (FASB), the bank user uses the CHARGEOFF-REPORTING activity. Differences in TBC The features related to handling charge-off under FASB regulations are not applicable for loans in TBC. Dual Accounting For loan contracts, apart from the customer balances, it is possible to store two separate balances, the bank balances along with the charge-off balances. When a Lending Product with Charge-off Property is proofed and published, the system automatically creates the balance type records to maintain charge-off balances along with the customer and bank balances. For a loan that is charged off, for CUR , the balances prior to the Charge-off Activity is stored as a shadow CUR CUST. The charge-off amount is stored in CUR CO and the amount under banks book is stored as CUR . The CUR CO charge-off balance, is the contingent balance and CUR CUST is a balance used for internal purpose and CUR is only non-contingent in nature. When the LENDING-CREDIT-ARRANGEMENT activity is processed, the amount credited to UNC is also credited to UNC CUST. When the LENDING-DEBIT-ARRANGEMENT activity is processed, the amount debited from UNC is also be debited from UNC CUST. Differences in TBC To complete the accounting to update the balances in a charged-off loan, the TBC generates an event, which can be captured by the connected external GL (General Ledger) system. Shadow Balances When a loan is charged-off, the borrower is unaware of this action, and continues to receive regular billing notices. As a result, when a loan is fully or partially charged off there is a situation to maintain two sets of books: A customer record (that is, the customer’s view of the balances and bills) A bank record (that is, the bank’s view of the balances). Prior to the charge-off, the customer and the bank records are the same (and therefore there is only one set of books). However once a loan is partially or fully charged off, the views are different. Customer Record Banks generally don’t communicate charge-off decision to the customers. So, a customer is unaware of a charge-off. Copying the balances prior to the Charge-off Activity creates a shadow record. This now becomes the customer record and does not include any of the effects of the charge-off. The bills and payments continue to be processed normally against this customer record. The payments received have to be apportioned as per the Payment Rules according to the customer. The customer balances are apportioned in this repayment order. Bank Record Full/Complete Charge-off For a full or complete charge-off using the LENDING-CHARGEOFF-ARRANGEMENT activity, there are no bank balances. The BNK balances are zero in this case. Charge-off in Parts/Partial Charge-off A charge-off creates the shadow balances for the customer record that do not include the effects of the charge-off (that is, the customer is completely unaware). As a result, the existing balances (customer balance less charge-off amount) continue to be referred to as the bank record and includes the effects of the charge-off (for example, the charged-off balance). As the arrangement advances, it also contains the interest accrual on the bank balance and charged-off balance separately. Additionally payments to the loan are allocated in a different manner on the bank record than on the customer record. This is based upon the value of the book balances and the status of the loan (for example, partially charged-off, fully charged-off or non-accrual). Internal inquiry screens display both the customer and the bank record, once a loan is partially or fully charged off. Reports breakdown the information this way as well – including both the bank balances and the customer balances. Charge-Off Balances The CUR CO and each ACC CO balance corresponds to the charge-off balance for the principal and the interest respectively. The system creates these balances by appending a CO at the end of each balance type. Differences in TBC To complete the accounting to update the balances in a charged-off loan, the TBC generates an event, which can be captured by the connected external GL (General Ledger) system. Multiple Interest Accruals For a full charge-off, the system accrues interest for charge-off and the customer balances namely CO and CUST balances. There is no bank balance to accrue interest for the BNK balances. For a partial charge-off (charge-off in parts), the system accrues interest for bank balance (for example, CUR ), charge-off and the customer balances. The system also accrues interest for the chargeoff and customer balances namely CO and CUST balances. It is necessary to accrue both charge-off and customer interest on the corresponding balances separately. Differences in TBC When a loan contract in TBC is charged-off, the TBC generates an event, which can be captured by the connected external GL (General Ledger) system to complete the accounting and balance updates. Full/Complete Charge-off During a full charge-off, the arrangement balances are moved to the Chargeoff PL. As part of shadow accounting, CUR CUST and CUR CO balances are maintained during a full Chargeoff. This results in the accrual of balances per Interest Property for each of this principal balance. Each of them accrues interest at the same rate but based upon their balance. ACC CUST is accrued on CUR CUST and ACC CO is accrued on CUR CO. Though multiple interest accruals are done based on different balances, definition of source balance for each type of accrual is not required. Product configuration contains: Property Source INTEREST CURACCOUNT Corresponding Accruals in a full charge-off loan are: Balance Source ACCINTERESTCO CURACCOUNTCO ACCINTERESTCUST CURACCOUNTCUST Partial Charge-off or Charge-off in Parts In a partial charge-off, there are three balances: CUR , CUR CUST, CUR CO. Hence, there are three accrual balances per Interest Property and each accrues interest at the same rate but based upon their balance. ACC is accrued on CUR then ACC CUST is accrued on CUR CUST. Though multiple interest accruals are done based on different balances, definition of source balance for each type of accrual is not required. The interest is calculated on: Property Source INTEREST CURACCOUNT Corresponding accruals in a partial charge-off loan are: Balance Source ACCINTEREST CURACCOUNT ACCINTERESTCO CURACCOUNTCO ACCINTERESTCUST CURACCOUNTCUST Product Setup and Charge-off Balances When a Lending Product with Charge-off Property is proofed and published, the system automatically creates the below balance type records to maintain customer, bank and charge-off balances. Except bank balances, other balance type records which are created by system are contingent in nature. Bank Balances Charge-off Balances Customer Balances CUR CUR CO CUR CUST DUE DUE CUST CUST UNC UNC CUST ACC ACC CO ACC CUST DUE DUE CUST CUST CUR CO balance type holds the cumulative amount that’s been charged-off against an account. ACC CO balance type is used for posting the accrued interest on charged-off balances namely CUR CO. Dual Billing In the case where a loan is in Charge-Off status, AA.BILL.DETAILS is updated with both the customer and the bank due amounts. For a complete charge-off, the reflection of the charge-off billing is found in the billed balances. The bank amount is zero For a partial charge-off, two sets of figures (the customer and bank amounts) are calculated and stored on the bill. The customer and the bank amounts differ due to the effect of the charged-off principal as well as the alternate way of applying credits to the arrangement. Bill Generated Before/After Charge-off On bill generation, AA.BILL.DETAILS is updated with both the customer and the bank due amounts for each of these accruals. AA.BILL.DETAILS stores the bank related fields that get updated on and after the charge-off of an arrangement. Once the charge-off is done, then the customer balances are stored in existing amount related fields and bank balances are stored in the BNK (bank) fields. Overdue processing is triggered based on the bills getting aged. The Os Prop Amt and Or Prop Amt fields of the bill are based on the customer balances(original amount) and regular overdue processing is triggered for the same. After a complete charge-off is made in the arrangement, the Full Chargeoff field in the AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS application displays Yes. During charge-off, the loan principal is charged off to the PL Category assigned to the Account property class. The interest is charged off to the PL Category assigned to the Interest property class. Any tax is charged-off to the PL Category assigned to the Tax property class. Validations During a Complete Charge-off When this activity is executed, the system performs the below validations and results in error in below scenarios: The bank performs the charge off after clearing any outstanding credit balances of the loan (like UNC/INV/AVL). Hence if there are any credit balances available during a charge-off, the system raises the following error. When there is a charge with outstanding pay balance, the arrangement cannot be charged off. The pay balance must be cleared and then charge-off should be triggered in the system. Post charge-off, the banks do not prefer to disburse any further loans or increase the loan commitment further. Hence, the disbursement activity is not allowed after the charge off. During the cooling and cancel period, the loan charge-off is not allowed. Any income to the arrangement is booked to the Chargeoff PL of that Property An arrangement that has undergone partial charge-off can undergo full charge-off, but an arrangement that is completely charged off cannot be charged off further. Loans cannot go to negative rate when loan is in charge-off. Dormant loans cannot be charged off. When an arrangement has a charge set to amortise, the charge cannot be charged off. The system raises an error when the user tries to do a full charge-off when there is a charge amortisation in progress. During charge-off, the system calculates the penalty interest if this has been configured and this helps the bank to access the real charge-off amount for all the property. In a business situation where the bank user must capture a bill in a loan that has undergone charge-off, the user can do so with the capture bill (LENDING-CAPTURE.BILL-BALANCE.MAINTENANCE) activity on such a loan. This activity can be used only for the arrangement that has undergone a full charge-off (LENDING-CHARGEOFF-ARRANGEMENT). As a result of this bill capture activity, the system releases the bill and balances in the customer books and the charge-off books.

Consider a scenario of dispute with the customer and the contract is charged off. The bank prefers to collect some charges or re-raise a bill that was previously paid, due to a customer dispute. In this case, the bank user can capture the bill and record it as an outstanding amount with the customer.

Consider a loan that is fully charged off using the LENDING-CHARGEOFF-ARRANGEMENT activity. The balances charged-off include the principal and interest as highlighted below.

- Charge-off principal - 46,369.61 (Outstanding principal).
- Charge- off interest - 31.62 (Accrued interest amount after the first installment).

This loan has only one installment bill which is already settled.

In this example, the client has raised a dispute with the bank on the 3871.49 bill dated Apr 12, 2023. So, the bank decides to refund the bill. At a later date, the claim is proved false and the bank wanted to raise the bill with the same amount for the customer.

The user captures the bill in this charged-off loan using the LENDING-CAPTURE.BILL-BALANCE.MAINTENANCE activity. The details of Bill Type , Payment Type , Payment Method , Payment amount , Property , Original Property Amount , and New Property Amount are entered based on the first installment bill details.

Though the bill is to claim the dues that were refunded earlier, the capture bill can be raised only for the current value date (not forward or back-valued) for the required payment type, bill type, and the bill amount for the components required. The bill date must also be the current date (not forward or back-valued).

Post capture bill activity, a due bill is created, and the system automatically updates the respective charge-off balances and customer balances in ECB.

Post capture bill activity:

- The charge-off principal is updated as 50000 (46169.61 + 3830.39)
- The charge-off interest is updated as 72.72 (31.62 + 41.10).

When an activity is triggered back-valued after this capture bill activity, the capture bill activity is also effectively reversed and replayed. As the bill is a manually created bill, the components of the bill do not undergo a change but the bill is reversed and replayed staying unaffected.

When a loan contract in TBC is charged-off, the TBC generates an event, which can be captured by the connected external GL (General Ledger) system to complete the accounting and balance updates.

The following section provides examples of using SUSPEND.STATUS and CHARGEOFF.STATUS periodic attributes

The SUSPEND.STATUS periodic attribute allows the user to evaluate if loan is suspended or not and suitably configures any activity restrictions based on the suspense status of the loan. The evaluation is done based the suspend information stored in AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS and allows the bank user to configure an error/override in the Activity Restriction condition.

Consider an example in which user needs to restrict a charge-off operation on a performing loan which is not suspended. If this periodic attribute is configured at product or arrangement level, then a user cannot trigger the charge off activity on a loan which is not suspended.

A rule is configured to check if the loan is in suspended status or not.

The rule is evaluated when an activity (charge off activity is considered in the case below) is triggered and based on the evaluation result an override (or error) is raised. Additionally, a rule break charge is applied if necessary.

This periodic attribute allows the user to evaluate and place activity restrictions based on the charge off status of the loan. This evaluates the charge off information in AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS and allows the bank user to configure an error/override in Activity Restriction condition, based on the charge off status of the loan.

Consider an example in which user needs to restrict a resume operation on a charged-off loan. If this periodic is configured at product or arrangement level, then the user cannot trigger resume on a loan which is fully and/or partially charged-off.

A rule is configured to check if the contract is in suspended status or not. The rule can be configured to evaluate if loan is fully or partially charged-off.

The rule is evaluated when an activity (resume activity is considered in the case below) is triggered and based on the evaluation result an override (or error) is raised. Additionally, a rule break charge is applied if necessary.

The features related to handling charge-off under FASB regulations are not applicable for loans in TBC.

### 3.15  Charges


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Charges can be scheduled on a regular frequency on occurrence of a specific activity or on breaching the terms and conditions of the product features. These charges can be fixed or calculated amount or combination of both of them and these can be calculated on tiered amounts.*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.ACCRUAL.DETAILS.HANDOFF`, `AA.ACCRUAL.FREQUENCY`, `AA.PRD.DES.ACCOUNTING`, `AA.PROPERTY`, `AC.ALLOCATION.RULE`, `AC.BALANCE.TYPE`, `AC.EVENT`, `EB.ACCRUAL` ... +2 more
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Accrue*, *Accrue Amort*, *Accrue Period*, *Amort Period*, *Booking.Cm*, *Effective Phase*, *Event Type*, *Mvmt Cr Txn* ... +4 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With


#### 📖 Introduction

Charges can be scheduled on a regular frequency on occurrence of a specific activity or on breaching the terms and conditions of the product features. These charges can be fixed or calculated amount or combination of both of them and these can be calculated on tiered amounts.

- Discounts can be given on the calculated charge before applying the predefined cap and floor amount.
- It is possible to accrue or amortise the charges over a period. It is also possible to stop and resume the amortisation of the charges over a period after the loan moves into non-performing status. Realisation of income is as follows: Suspend mode functionality - When the suspended loan is resumed, the realisation of income/expense which was suspended is booked to P/L immediately. Stop mode functionality – When the suspended loan is resumed, the realisation of income/expense which was stopped is resumed with a new straight line amount based on the residual tenure of the loan.
- The charge amount can be in a currency, which is different from the currency of account based on product requirements.
- The charges applied on certain activities can be grouped and collected in regular frequencies.
- The charges calculated can be waived fully or partially on charge assessment. The waived amount can be accounted to a separate profit and loss category.
- The charges can be paid to the customer as a bonus amount on occurrence of specific activities or on certain conditions. It is also possible to suspend or resume the accrual or amortisation of a ‘Credit’ type charge.

The accounting related features and processing are handled by an external GL system for loans in TBC. Therefore, to complete the accounting related to charges (such as for suspension, accrual and amortisation of charges and so on), the TBC generates an event which can be captured by the connected external GL (General Ledger) system.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The following section describes the configuration of charges.


##### Opt Currency Charge

The Charge Property Class is dated and optionally currency specific. It can be forward dated and more than one instance can be added in the same product. It supports variation and is available for External Products. Charges can be used in the Inheritance Property Class and can be set to tracking, non-tracking or custom tracking. Optionally, delayed tracking is also possible.

For loans in TBC, the Inheritance property class is not applicable as it is used only for the purpose of balance netting. Therefore, it is not possible to use a charge in the inheritance property class for loans in TBC.

The user can define and the system can evaluate the variations in the charge amounts (that is, preferential pricing) based on factors such as customer details, channel and so on, at the enterprise layer that is, TEP (Temenos Enterprise Pricing).

The features related to usage of charges in external products are not applicable for loans in TBC.


##### Charge Override

The Charge Override Property is visible in the arrangement only after the charge is triggered and validated. It is used to make any discounts on the Property.

The features related to charge override are not applicable for loans in TBC.


##### Charge Currency Different From Arrangement Currency

If the currency defined in the arrangement and the currency of the arrangement fee are different, then the system raises an override.

If the requesting currency and the currency defined in this field are different, then the system converts the base amount to charge currency equivalent and calculates the charge amount. The final charge amount is again converted to the requesting currency equivalent. The system calculates the converted amount using the mid-rate. The Tier Groups field defines the calculation method of charge amount for the currency. This field accepts two values namely, BANDS and LEVELS.


##### Rule Break Charges

The user can specify periodic rules in specific Product Conditions. For example, in a Term Amount Product Condition, the user can attach a periodic rule, which can be set to increase the commitment amount over a period of one year, but it cannot exceed 10% of the original commitment. When the user links such periodic rules in a Product Condition, it is possible to link a Charge Property to collect it when the rule is broken. The charge can be a fixed amount or calculated on a base amount.


##### Amortisation of Charges

Charges can be amortised by setting the Accrue Amort field as AMORT and the Accrue Period as MATURITY or defining a valid period (such as 1M, 1Y, etc.) in the AA.PRD.DES.ACCOUNTING record. Booking of charge to income (PL) is amortised and the income is distributed to numerous period based on the amortisation term set in the AA.PRD.DES.ACCOUNTING record and the accrual frequency set in the AA.ACCRUAL.FREQUENCY for the specific Charge Property.

If the Accrue Amort field is set to AMORT and the Accrue Period is set to 1Y, then the system amortises the charge till the end of the defined Accrue Period and the accrual depends on the frequency set for the Charge Property. The Mvmt Cr Txn and Mvmt Dr Txn fields need to be specified for the accrual of the charge amortised.

The EB.ACCRUAL record is created when a charge is amortised and holds the details of amortisation of charges such as amount of charge, charge property, start or end date of amortisation, frequency, and accrual particulars.

In AA.ACCRUAL.FREQUENCY , the frequency of accrual for the specified charge has to be added.

The below screenshot displays the AA.ACCRUAL.FREQUENCY record.

For a suspended loan, in order to define a charge for which amortisation needs to be stopped, the charge Property Type has to be set to Stop Suspend.

##### Preferential Pricing

Preferential pricing refers to the use of any of the available methods (such as, Product Variations, Relationship Pricing and Promotional Pricing) to provide customers with interest rates or charges, which are better than the standard product.

The below screenshot displays the Preferential Pricing.

It is possible to define pricing benefits (that is, preferential pricing) for certain loan contracts based on factors such as customer age, rating, channel and so on. The user can define preferential pricing for loans in TBC and the system can evaluate at the enterprise layer that is, TEP (Temenos Enterprise Pricing).


##### Rebate Processing

A rebate is the ability to create and credit the customer a payable charge. This rebate (as a credit to the customer) can happen at the point of arrangement creation or during the life of the arrangement.

The rebate canbe paid out to the customer by using the Payout Rules Property.

For credit charges (rebates), Property Type is selected as Credit in AA.PROPERTY . This indicates that this property is a payable charge to the customer and not a due charge from the customer.

As it is possible to credit the charge or rebate to the customer, PAY balance type is available for loan products.

Once this is set, the bank can calculate the credit charge in the same way as a debit charge. It can be configured:

- As an activity charge, credit to be given when a certain activity occurs
- In the Payment Schedule, on a pre-defined frequency or on a certain date
- Using the rules defined in Activity Restriction

Rebates can be applied to the customer with the following options:

- Capitalised – In this method, the amount is credited to the customer's current balance and thus reducing the outstanding amount.
- Pay (Made Due) – In this method, the amount is credited to a pay balance that can be settled either automatically or manually.
- Deferred – In this method, the activity is deferred to a later stage and eventually made due or capitalized from the payment.

The following accounting events are added to the existing allocation rules used for charges and settlement in loan products.

- CHARGE-ACT.MAKE.DUE-PAY
- CHARGE-ACT.CAPITALISE-DUE
- CHARGE-PAY-PAY
- CHARGE-ADJUST.BILL-PAY-OS.ADJ
- CHARGE-CAPTURE.BILL-PAY
- SETTLEMENT-SETTLE-PAY

The below screenshot displays SETTLEMENT-SETTLE-PAY in LOAN-SETTLE.

It defines the charges that need to be applied when an activity is triggered on the arrangement. The event triggers the rebate charge defined at the product level. On triggering this event, the rebate is credited to the customer.

The rebate can be paid to the customer by using the Payout Rules definition. The below screenshot displays LENDING.PAYOUT record in Payout Rules Product Condition.

##### Phase Based Charge Conditions

The system provides an option to define charges for a product. The charges can be different at various life cycle of the product, based on the requirement of the banks or financial institutions. The bank can set up charges by configuring the Effective Phase field in the Product Phases tab of the Product Designer. Read Product Phase to set up charges and read Overpayment section for a detailed example for phase based charges.


##### Pre-Closure and Dues Settlement

In an arrangement, it is possible to generate the schedules before the cooling period expires. In such a scenario, any interest, charges or principal amount that is due, has to be settled by the customer before the user can close the arrangement.


##### Tax on Charges

The Tax Property is currency based, dated and can be multiple. It is possible to define the Property on which the tax is to be calculated and the corresponding Tax code and Tax type condition for the corresponding Tax property. The Tax Property can be Property specific and Property Class specific. The bill is updated with the Tax amount and the Tax property for the corresponding Charge Property. Tax cannot be scheduled when a scheduled property has tax to be calculated for that property, tax property, and the amount is displayed in the enquiry.


##### Pre-Closure of a Loan and Rebate Processing

When a loan is pre-closed, the bank rebates the insurance amount pertaining to the residual term. At the time of pre-closing, the closure charges along with the rebate amount are considered to compensate for the calculated outstanding amount. When the insurance contract is for a specific period, the unamortised amount for a certain period (that is, from the pre-closure date to the actual maturity date) is rebated.

##### Rebate Processing

The below screenshot displays the rebate processing.

For some loan products, the customers protect their loan commitment with the help of insurance covers against risks such as death and disability. The insurance policy can be for the entire loan term or particular period such as yearly and then it is renewed at the end of every period. Rebate processing provides a facility to rebate the outstanding amount of premium for loan insurance on pre-closure or on cancellation at a later stage or cancellation within a certain grace period.

The aim of the rebate processing feature is, to render the ability to use a local routine for certain types of amortisation calculation. However, in AA, the generic accrual processing mechanism allows the user to amortise or accrue fixed amounts supplied by applications through a direct API or accounting entries. The standard method of processing is to straight line the amount on a daily basis.

It is possible to post to an internal account category (instead of PL) in the Accounting version.

The user can define the start date of accrual calculation. From that day, the accrual and account postings begin. On the first day, the calculation is based on the beginning of the accrual period – Start Date in the EB.ACCRUAL record. The changes to the grace period is considered only if the record is reversed, and if the record is reversed, no accounting activity takes place.

This feature provides an option to rebate the outstanding amount of premium for loan insurance on pre-closure or on cancellation at a later stage or cancellation within a certain grace period.

Home loan insurance, or any mortgage redemption insurance plan, is part of a banker's sales pitch when extending sizable long-term credit, such as a home loan. These plans hedge the risk of loss in case the borrower dies or becomes disabled during the loan term, especially an unsecured loan. The banks fund the insurance portion as part of the loan amount, which is repaid by the customers as part of the loan. The insurance policy can be done for the entire loan term or particular period.

The solution deals with the option to define the grace period, rebate on cancellation of an insurance contract and insurance rebate on pre-closure of a loan.

The accounting related features and processing are handled by an external GL system for loans in TBC. Therefore, to complete the accounting related to charges (such as for suspension, accrual and amortisation of charges and so on), the TBC generates an event, which can be captured by the connected external GL (General Ledger) system.

Unless the dues are either settled or waived, the system does not allow the user to close the arrangement.

### 3.16  Creating Lending Arrangements


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Lending is part of the Retail Banking AA suite of products and it supports the following Product Groups,*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.PRODUCT.MANAGER`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Currency*, *Customer*, *Product*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With


#### 📖 Introduction

Lending is part of the Retail Banking AA suite of products and it supports the following Product Groups,

- Home Equity
- Lines of Credit
- Mortgages
- Personal Loans
- Small Business Loans

A loan arrangement helps the bank to record the terms and conditions of the agreement, between the bank and its customers, relating to the loan sanctioned. The Lending module allows the creation and servicing of arrangements. Activities such as new arrangement, early closure, take over, loan cancellation, charge off, interest reset, and so on can be performed on arrangements.

There are no specific limitations in creating lending arrangements in the TBC.

When the user requests the creation of a loan contract, the system triggers the corresponding Activity in the TBC to complete the process of loan creation. The loan contract is created under the product selected, from the list of products available.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section orients the user on configuring different kinds of lending products.


##### Defining a Lending Product

- The AA Product Builder allows the user to build or modify a product. Read the Product Builder user guide for more information.
- The user must associate the appropriate Product Conditions to the (loan) product to define the attributes (tenor, interest type, repayment frequency, charges and so on) of the loan product.


##### Proof and Publish

A product must be proofed and published via the AA.PRODUCT.MANAGER application to see the product in Product Catalog. Read the Product Builder user guide for more information.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section allows the user to create different kinds of lending arrangements.

- While creating a loan, the user inputs the customers for the loan contract.
- The Customer and Currency attributes are mandatorily used to create (via Product Catalog) a loan.
- The system assigns the role of the customer as Beneficial Owner by default. It is possible to add multiple owners to an arrangement. When a loan is created via the command line, the user must manually designate the loan product from the Product attribute.


> **Related Applications:** `AA.PRODUCT.MANAGER`

### 3.17  Customer and Eligibility


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The banks offer different loan products to its customers. There can be a single owner or multiple owners for a loan arrangement and multiple other parties involved in the loan, for example, Power of Attorney or Authorised Signatory. These customers are not the owners (borrowers) but are important an...*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.ARR.CUSTOMER`, `AA.CUSTOMER.ROLE`, `AA.PARTY.ROLE`, `CUSTOMER`, `EB.LOOKUP`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Customer*, *Limit Id*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With


#### 📖 Introduction

The banks offer different loan products to its customers. There can be a single owner or multiple owners for a loan arrangement and multiple other parties involved in the loan, for example, Power of Attorney or Authorised Signatory. These customers are not the owners (borrowers) but are important and are recorded on the loan arrangement.

Loan products can be tailored to specific sets of customers, for example, the banks can offer mortgage loan products with different terms and conditions for regular customers, staff and non-residents. To enable this functionality the bank can define the criteria to define which customers are eligible to use the bank’s lending products. It is possible to set up different eligibility rules based on the role of the customer of the arrangement.

The eligibility evaluation happens on all involved parties of the arrangement and are reviewed periodically, according to the product configuration or re-evaluated when there is change in the customer information (customer static changes).

In the TBC, the configuration and evaluation of eligibility is performed only when TEP (Temenos Enterprise Pricing) is used.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section orients the user to configure loan ownership and understand the eligibility criteria.


##### Ownership and Other Party

The Customer Property Class is used by all products to specify the involved parties of an arrangement and their respective roles. The Customer Property Class is primarily an arrangement level class, that is, the values are input at arrangement-level, and is typically configured at the product level as fully negotiable. Each arrangement should have atleast one customer who is the legal owner of the loan.

Each involved party should be recorded along with the respective role, at the arrangement level. The customer roles are configured in AA.CUSTOMER.ROLE .

Read the Customer Property Class user guide for more information on customer roles.

Additionally, other parties can be added to an arrangement with a designated role (Guarantor, authorised signatory). Roles of other parties can be defined in the AA.PARTY.ROLE virtual table, in the EB.LOOKUP file. All owners and any other involved parties need to exist in the CUSTOMER application.

The parties should be existing entries in Party TBC, rather than CUSTOMER application.


##### Eligibility

Eligibility rules for a customer to get a loan in a particular product are configured in the Eligibility Property Class. The banks can create or configure the rules using the Rules Engine. These rules can be used to set up the eligibility conditions. The eligibility rules can be evaluated at the time of loan creation at regular intervals and whenever there is a change in customer static information. Read the Eligibility Property Class user guide for more information.

Eligibility rules set is applied on all the involved parties of the arrangement. The banks can set different eligibility rules based on the role they play in the loan. If the party does not satisfy the eligibility condition, the system displays an error or an override based on the configuration.

An eligibility condition for a loan product based on the customer’s age is shown below.

In the TBC, the configuration and evaluation of eligibility is performed only when TEP (Temenos Enterprise Pricing) is used.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section orients the user on working with new loan arrangements.


##### Ownership and Other Party

At the time of opening a new loan arrangement, a bank user can define:

- The owners of the arrangement
- Add any number of other involved parties
- Along with the role of each party. The system ensures there is at least one beneficial owner for the loan. The user can perform tax split for each customer and the system defaults the values from AA.CUSTOMER.ROLE .

The AA.ARR.CUSTOMER table, stores the parties involved in the arrangement, along with the tax liability percentage, limit allocation percentage and GL allocation percentage at arrangement level.

Under certain circumstances, the parties involved in the arrangement may be altered. It is possible to,

- Add or remove a party to the arrangement.
- Change the ownership of the arrangement, to another party.

The Change Customer Activity (LENDING-CHANGE-CUSTOMER) can be used to change the customer or to add other parties to the loan. These parties are evaluated against the configured eligibility rules, during the Change Activity. When the ownership of the loan is changed, it impacts any limit provided to the loan. The Activity triggers a change in the limit details required for the new owners.

- In the TBC, the configuration and evaluation of eligibility is performed only when TEP (Temenos Enterprise Pricing) is used.
- When the customer for a loan contract is updated, the limit condition is also opened for the user to edit. Any change in the limit attached to the loan can be updated using the Limit Id field in the Limit condition at this point in time. The TBC generates an event to the external limit system in order to delink the old limit from the loan and link the new limit to the loan contract. The external limit system must approve the sanctioned limit for the loan and an event for the approval is received from the external limit solution. In case the external limit system has rejected the new sanctioned limit for the loan, the TBC reverses the activity for updating the customer on receiving an event stating the rejection of the limit from the external limit system.

With the Lending TBC, the parties should be existing entries in Party TBC.


##### Eligibility

The customer’s eligibility for availing the product can be checked during the creation of a loan, at regular intervals and when there is a change in the Customer attribute or static changes have happened at a party.

In the following example, while creating an arrangement for a student loan product, the customer’s age is validated for eligibility of the loan. The customer’s age has to be between 15 and 25. As it is found to be outside the limits for a student loan an error is raised as shown below.

In the TBC, the configuration and evaluation of eligibility is performed only when TEP (Temenos Enterprise Pricing) is used.


> **Related Applications:** `AA.ARR.CUSTOMER`, `AA.CUSTOMER.ROLE`, `AA.PARTY.ROLE`, `CUSTOMER`, `EB.LOOKUP`
