### 3.29  Loan Topup


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The banks can offer its customers, an additional loan amount on the existing loan as loan top-up. Loan top-ups are cost effective to the banks as it need not invest time and money acquiring and assessing new customers. In AA, the loan top-up is an addition to the loan commitment on live arrangements...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Amount*, *Change Amount*, *Commitment Drawdown*, *Include Future Disb*, *Percentage*, *Status*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With


#### 📖 Introduction

The banks can offer its customers, an additional loan amount on the existing loan as loan top-up. Loan top-ups are cost effective to the banks as it need not invest time and money acquiring and assessing new customers. In AA, the loan top-up is an addition to the loan commitment on live arrangements. The system allows to increase the commitment amount of a lending arrangement to provide the loan top-up.The topped up loans can be automatically disbursed and the disbursed amount appears as a line item in the payment schedule projection.

The new payment amount including the future scheduled increase commitment can be projected in the payment schedule on the effective date itself.

The features related to automatic disbursement of the top up amount are not applicable for loans in TBC.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The Term Amount Property Class is used to define the maximum commitment amount for a Product. This is defined in the Amount attribute. The Amount attribute can be fully negotiable or be set as negotiable for a maximum amount which is the cap. It is also possible to increase the commitment of this cap amount. The user can use the LENDING-INCREASE-TERM.AMOUNT Activity Class to increase the commitment amount.

The disbursement of the top-up amount can be set to automatic as per configuration in the Settlement Property Class. While performing the Activity, the user can also schedule the disbursement of this loan to the same or any future date. It is also possible to perform the disbursement using FT, TT or Payment Order.

The Commitment Drawdown attribute in the Term Amount Property Conditions should be set as Auto (as shown below) to achieve automatic disbursement of both new and top up loans respecting the given settlement instructions.

The features related to automatic disbursement of the top up amount are not applicable for loans in TBC.


##### Including Future Scheduled Disbursements

The repayment amount with respect to future scheduled disbursements can be known on the effective scheduled date itself when the Include Future Disb attribute in Payment Schedule property conditions is set to Progressive.

| Column 1 | Column 2 |
|---|---|
| Commitment Amount | 100,000 |
| Start | 50% (50,000) |
| START + 6M |  |


#### 🔧 Working With

A loan top-up can be achieved by increasing the loan commitment amount and disbursing it. The Change Amount attribute can be used to indicate the top-up amount while performing the LENDING-INCREASE-TERM.AMOUNT Activity.

If the arrangement is set for single disbursement, then the user cannot disburse the increased amount. Hence, any disbursements setting should be configured accordingly.

In the below arrangement, USD 87,165 is disbursed and the Status field set to Current.

In this arrangement, the initial commitment is 900,000 and disbursed.

The below screenshot displays the account details.

This loan is topped using the Increase Commitment Activity, and the commitment is increased by another 15,000 USD.

In this case, an automatic disbursement is not set for increased commitment.

The below screenshots display the financial summary and the ECB balances. It shows that the TOTCOMMITMENT and CURCOMMITMENT are increased and the amount is ready for disbursal.


##### Increase Commitment Simulation

The user can simulate the increased commitment activity and view the schedule projection in the simulated overview screen to know the payment amount of the contract based on the increased loan amount. The simulated activity when converted to live facilitates automatic disbursement to the given settlement instructions when the Commitment Drawdown is set to Auto.

Customer A buys a loan for 5000 USD for a term of two years(2Y) and later he requests the bank for an additional loan of 1000 USD. The disbursement of loan happens via Payment order. The Commitment Drawdown is chosen as Auto. The bank simulates the Increased Commitment activity and agrees with the customer to pay the top up amount. After the customer agrees, the top up activity gets converted to live for automatic disbursement of top up amount for the given settlement instructions. The projection of schedules after the increased commitment disbursement is based on the increased amount plus the remaining principal outstanding.

The features related to automatic disbursement of the top up amount are not applicable for loans in TBC.

### 3.30  Loan WriteOff


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *A bank writes off a loan when the borrower becomes insolvent due to various reasons and the underlying loan, or an asset is no more recoverable from the customer. The bank may book such loans as bad loans and eliminate a portion or a whole amount of such loan from its balance sheet.*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY`, `AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY`, `EB.CONTRACT.BALANCE.BALANCES`, `STMT.ENTRY`
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With


#### 📖 Introduction

A bank writes off a loan when the borrower becomes insolvent due to various reasons and the underlying loan, or an asset is no more recoverable from the customer. The bank may book such loans as bad loans and eliminate a portion or a whole amount of such loan from its balance sheet.

There are no specific limitations related to writing off loan contracts in TBC.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

There is no separate configuration for write off of loans. The Balance Maintenance Property Class has to be available in the product.


##### Accounting for Write-off Arrangement

When the LENDING-WRITE.OFF-BALANCE.MAINTENANCE (arrangement write-off) activity is triggered, the system triggers the LENDING-ADJUST.BALANCE-BALANCE.MAINTENANCE activity for adjusting the balances.

The accounting entries are posted according to the accounting and the soft accounting allocation rule configurations. In the illustration used for write-off arrangement activity, the accounting condition for this product has an allocation rule that is, the LOAN.ACCOUNT allocation rule is attached on the ADJUST.BILL action. Accounting set up and allocation rules can be seen in the below screenshot:

For the ADJUST.BILL action, the contra entry is captured in the internal account (U-AAWOF). This is categorised in ACCOUNT.CLASS as AA Write-off.

To complete the accounting related to write-off of loans in TBC, the TBC generates an event, which can be captured by the connected external GL (General Ledger) system.


#### 🔧 Working With

A write-off can be performed at three levels of an arrangement:

- Write-off Bills – Reduces liability on due bills
- Write-off Balances – Reduces outstanding principal balance
- Write-off Arrangement – Reduces all the loan bills and balances

When the loan principal is written off, the CUR (Outstanding Principal Balance) and UTL (Utilisation Balance) are updated. When the outstanding bills are written off, the corresponding due and overdue balances in the loan are updated.

| Pre Bill Write-Off | Post Bill Write-Off |
|---|---|
|  |  |

| Pre Balance Write-Off | Post Balance Write-Off |
|---|---|
|  |  |

| Pre Write-Off | Post Write-Off |
|---|---|
|  |  |

### 3.31  Migration of LendingArrangements


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Existing contracts are most likely to be present when the Temenos' system replaces the existing legacy system. Therefore, these contracts need to be transferred to our system, which is referred as Takeover.*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.ACTIVITY.CLASS`, `AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY`, `AA.CONTEXT TYPE`, `ACCOUNT`, `CUSTOMER`, `EB.CASHFLOW`, `LIMIT`, `PERIODIC.RATE`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *AMC*, *Activity*, *Advance Payment*, *Advance Payment Restriction*, *Advance Settle Date*, *Arrangement*, *Context Name*, *Context Value* ... +30 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With


#### 📖 Introduction

Existing contracts are most likely to be present when the Temenos' system replaces the existing legacy system. Therefore, these contracts need to be transferred to our system, which is referred as Takeover.

As the situation at each new implementation is different, a general approach is adopted when planning and executing the takeover of existing retail loans into the retail lending product line. Read the Working with section for more information.

When the user migrates a loan through a front-end API, the system triggers the corresponding Activity in the TBC to complete the migration process. During takeover, the user can update the details of the limit associated with the loan using the limit condition.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

Takeover of live contracts uses the Balance Maintenance Property Class. For more information on configuration, read the Balance Maintenance Property Class.

During the migration of data from the legacy system to Temenos' system, it is possible to improve the performance of the takeover process by updating certain AA tables through a background service. Read Customer Arrangement Offline Update for more information.


##### Migration Consideration for Advance Payment Setup

The following are some migration scenarios for advance payments.


###### Bills Issued In Advance

During the migration of a loan contract from legacy system to AA, it is possible that the loan product has a facility to settle the bills in advance.

For loans that have the bills generated in advance but are not yet settled, the Temenos' system allows the takeover of the bill in the issued status (that is, the bill is made due during the advance repayment or the bill due date). To accommodate this, the capture bill activity allows bill date/issue date to be back dated and settle date/due date to be future dated.

It is possible to takeover a bill in Issued status only when Bill Produced field is set and the advance payment feature is enabled for the loan contract.


###### Bills Issued and Settled In Advance

The following section describes scenarios in advance payments for bills issued and settled in advance.


##### Scenario 1: Advance Payment Benefit from both Principal and Interest Paid In Advance

For loans that have the bills generated in advance but are already settled, during the takeover:

- The principal outstanding is the remaining balance after the bill is settled in advance.
- The accruals from the advance settlement date till the takeover date are captured.
- The next due date is updated explicitly in the system, so that AA doesn’t generate another bill (since it has already been settled).

If the bill for a conventional loan is settled in advance, before the due date, then the interest period is cycled to the next due date of the bill during takeover. Thus, the system starts accruing interest on the principal balance after the last advance payment. The next bill is generated as per the configuration, that is, based on the next due date and the number of days mentioned in the advance payment setup.


##### Scenario 2: Advance Payment with Customer Benefit (Only from Principal)

Consider a conventional loan product with the following configuration:

- Advance Payment is set as FULL.
- Advance Payment Restriction set as BILLED (as part of recommended setup).
- Settle Unearned Interest set as YES.

It has an advance bill which is taken over as a settled bill (that is, the bill is issued in advance and settled prior to the due date), the interest accrual for that period is a positive balance considering the interest accruals paid in advance. In this case, the user has to trigger a Capture Balance activity to capture and store the accrued interest as a positive balance.

The user can also trigger the Adjust Balance activity to adjust the interest accruals to a positive amount during takeover.

The above-mentioned configuration is the recommended setup for advance payment with interest benefit for customer only from the principal amount paid in advance. With this setup, the customer can pay only the issued bill in advance.

- Takeover of interest accruals (that is, ACC ) as a positive balance can be made possible only when Settle Unearned Interest is set to YES.
- If Settle Unearned Interest is set for a conventional loan, then the Advance Payment field can only be set to FULL. Else, the system raises proofing errors.
- When a bill is issued in advance, then it is considered as a current bill. For example, if the bank has set Advance Payment Restriction to 1 and the loan has bill a (invoiced to the customer) in advance, then the customer can settle the issued bill and one more bill in advance.


##### Scenario 3: Advance Payment with no Customer Benefit

During an upgrade or migration, the product can be configured with an advance payment rule. The Advance Payment Rule should have the payment rule type setup with Advance Settle Date (ADVANCE.SETTLE.DATE) set as DUE. This ensures that no benefit is passed to the customer for any advance payment. If the loan has any advance payments in the legacy system, then the advance payments should be triggered after the takeover activity .

During the takeover activity, the user closes the legacy contracts and moves the accrued balances to a control account. The balance under the advance payment is also moved to the control account and the outstanding principal and the accruals till date are captured. In this scenario the sequence of steps involved during migration are:

- Take over contract
- Capture principal balance
- Capture accruals

Similar to accruals, the advance payment is also moved from the legacy system to Temenos' system.

- Once the takeover is completed, the user must trigger a capture balance to capture the ADV balance. Now, the user can see the Forward Apply Payment activities triggered by the system to settle the bills for the respective future date.

When the system moves to the actual due date, it is evident that the settlement process is suppressed as the bill is already settled. The system clears the DUE , DUE and DUE effective on the bill due date with the advance balance type. If the advance payment has a principal repayment component, the system updates the GL only on the due date of the bill for the reduced CUR .

In TBC, during the takeover of a loan that has an advance payment processed for an upcoming instalment, the TBC generates an event, which can be captured by the connected external GL (General Ledger) system to complete the accounting and balance updates.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section deals with the migration of lending arrangements.


##### General Approach

The following general approach is recommended:

- Analyse existing products and create equivalent products using the AL module.
- Determine requirements for historic data in Temenos' system.
- Prepare extract of legacy loan contract data and balances.
- Create new arrangements from the legacy loan contract data.
- Create the outstanding legacy bills.
- Update the penalty balances.

To takeover legacy loans to AL, the following activities must already have taken place before creating the arrangements:

Each loan arrangement has to be linked to a customer in the CUSTOMER application. Every loan has to be captured in the Temenos' Lending module to ensure that the associated client data is made available in our system and the legacy loan data can be associated with the customer number in the Temenos' system.

In TBC, during migration of a loan contract, the information related to owners and other parties can be input from an external system such as Party TBC. The system evaluates this customer information against the records found in the external system.

For each customer in a loan arrangement, a corresponding LIMIT record is created in our system before creating the arrangement.

In TBC, during the takeover of a loan, the user can update the sanctioned limit amount for the loan using the Limit Id field in the Limit condition.

A loan can be a long-term contract in the legacy system, which can be ongoing for several years. The usual practice for the takeover of financial contracts is for the contract to be takeover to take place with an effective date that is equal to a scheduled date (for example, interest or principal due date).

The contract is created with principal balance and interest rates at the selected event date as a new contract. Interest rate and principal changes after the event date are loaded into our system as future-dated activities. Details of previous history and balances are not used in the contract processing in our system.

The date chosen can be the last payment date, which can be a past date.

> **⚠️ Note:** It is possible to takeover a contract in the middle of an interest period, but this adds additional complexity to the process. Interest calculations are split in the two systems with associated profit and loss being accrued partly in the legacy system and Temenos' system.

Existing contracts are analysed to identify the earliest date that can be used to create an arrangement.

The existing products in the legacy system has to be analysed and products have to be created for the Lending Product Line that provides the same functionality.

The legacy system is unlikely to provide functionality in exactly the same way as Temenos' system and data may not map directly from the legacy system to our system.

Properties, Product Property Conditions and Products have to be created with an effective date that is on or earlier than the earliest contract date for takeover identified in the legacy data.

Products have to be published, including any known future conditions and made available for sale before arrangements can be created.

It is unlikely that the legacy system has the concepts of product inheritance and negotiable attributes as our system so the legacy products are likely to be supported best by:

- Not using any inheritance in the product structure.
- Making the majority of attributes negotiable for arrangements.

In TBC, the loan contracts are migrated to products which are designed and defined using a product management system like the TPM (Temenos Product Manager).

The AA module supports the ability to record arrangement level conditions for information purposes only. Once the arrangement is created, it is possible to load historic conditions if required. Any data loaded prior to the creation date in our system are not used for processing and is not a mandatory requirement.

Temenos' system cannot process the adjustment to loan contracts with an effective date prior to the takeover date. The usual approach is to make the amendment in the legacy system if still available, or manually calculate the adjustment. The adjustment can then be applied to the arrangement in our system effective the takeover date.

The value of outstanding bills have to be taken over into Temenos' system with an effective date equal to the start date of the arrangement in our system or the takeover date. Data has to be made available for overdue bills.

The value of penalty interest and charges calculated (accrued) by the legacy system has to be made available at the takeover date (that is, effective date of arrangement creation in our system). It provides the ability to take these balances over.

The following data should be made available (or be able to be derived) in Temenos' system:

- Customer number.
- Product name.
- Effective Date for the takeover of the contract.
- Currency of Arrangement.
- Outstanding principal balance as at the Effective Date.

> **⚠️ Note:** A possible scenario is that a contract that has passed its maturity date in the legacy system but has outstanding bills and has a current principal of zero at the effective date of takeover.

A separate extract of overdue bills for existing arrangements has to be prepared. It includes,

- The bill due date.
- The breakdown of properties and outstanding amount for the bill.
- A legacy contract identifier that should be possible to link to the created arrangement number after takeover.

Any outstanding penalty interest or charge accrual balances for loans should be prepared and should identify

- The Property name (for example, PENALTYINT)
- The balance amount for the Property.

During migration or takeover activity the TAKEOVER.CASHFLOW-REPORTING Cashflow type activity class allows the user to specify the EIR or carry cost which is handed off to the Cashflow engine.

Read Capturing EIR/AMC during Migration in Reporting Property Class for further information.

- It is possible to configure the reporting condition to hand off the required information to an external system for calculating the annual percentage rate for loans in TBC. The TBC generates a business event to hand off the cashflows to an external system for further processing to take place. All other features related to Reporting condition are not applicable for TBC.
- The features pertaining to EIR as well as AMC are not applicable for loans in TBC and can be enabled using external solutions.

The following section describes the methods used in triggering TAKEOVER CASH FLOW REPORTING Activity


###### Using AMC Method

1. The following screenshot is Lending Arrangement overview after Takeover is completed
2. The TAKEOVER CASHFLOW REPORTING activity is triggered .The Takeover method is “AMC” and EIR is input as 5.
3. EB.CASHFLOW is updated with the following details Event Type updated as TAKEOVER-PERFORMING for the performing loan


###### Using EIR Method

1. The following screenshot is Lending Arrangement overview after the takeover activity. This loan is in Suspend Status.
2. The TAKEOVER CASHFLOW REPORTING activity is triggered .The Takeover method is “EIR” and AMC is input as 70.
3. EB.CASHFLOW is updated with the following details AMC value is updated in the Takeover Npv field. Event Type is updated as “TAKEOVER-SUSPEND” for the suspended loan


###### Takeover Sequence

The following section describes the takeover sequence in detail.


###### Takeover process – AA Contract with Reporting PC (in IFRS standard)

This process is for existing bank with AA loans & IFRS reporting in their system but switching to FASB standards (from IFRS).

1. Update Reporting condition for the loan product.
2. Proof and Publish the product.
3. Trigger IFRS activity.
4. Update EIR or AMC as required and commit.
5. EB Cashflow gets updated.


###### Takeover process – AA Contract without Reporting PC (without IFRS standard)

This process is for existing bank with AA loans without IFRS module initially but later comply.

1. Add Reporting condition for the loan product.
2. Proof and Publish the product.
3. Trigger IFRS activity.
4. Update EIR or AMC as required and commit.
5. EB Cashflow gets updated.


###### Full Takeover from legacy (Non AA, Non IFRS case)

This process involves migration of loans from legacy system into Temenos' solution with AA & IFRS functionality.

1. Create Loan product with Reporting condition
2. Complete loan Takeover sequence to migrate the outstanding loan bills and balances.
3. Trigger IFRS activity.
4. Update EIR or AMC as required and commit.
5. EB Cashflow gets updated.


> **Related Applications:** `AA.ACTIVITY.CLASS`, `AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY`, `AA.CONTEXT TYPE`, `ACCOUNT`, `CUSTOMER`, `EB.CASHFLOW`, `LIMIT`, `PERIODIC.RATE`

### 3.32  Misc


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Lending Temenos Banking Capability (TBC) provides various lending functionalities that a financial institution can offer to its customer.*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

The Lending Temenos Banking Capability (TBC) provides various lending functionalities that a financial institution can offer to its customer.

It supports an entire range of lending features with flexible configurable conditions, with which, new lending products can be added, to meet the bank’s ongoing requirements.

It supports the complete life cycle of loan accounts, from creation of loan, disbursements, maintenance such as amendment of interest rate, capitalise interest to principal amount, change product, repayment and closure of loans at maturity.

Regulatory requirements, such as, tax on interest and restriction of operations, are also covered in the Lending TBC.

The features that Lending Temenos Banking Capability (TBC) provides are summarised below:

- Loan Creation - Creation of any type of loan contract fetching details from other TBCs like Party, Reference data and so on. It is possible to create both call and term loan contracts for single or multiple borrowers using the Lending TBC.
- Loan Simulation – Simulation of loan contracts at every stage of the loan life cycle such as creation of loan contracts, prepayment of loan amount, renewal of loan contract, request for payment holiday, calculation of payoff amount to pre-close the loan and so on.
- Loan Commitment and top-up – In the TBC, it is possible to define and store the terms and conditions of the sanctioned loan (such as the loan amount, the tenure of the loan and so on) as agreed with the customer. Also, banks can offer their customers, an additional loan amount on the existing loan as a loan top-up using the Lending TBC.
- Loan Disbursements – Lending TBC supports manual disbursement of the sanctioned amount for a loan contract. The disbursement can be initiated from an external payment system. Lending TBC generates an event for the disbursement, which can be consumed by an external General Ledger system for accounting and bookkeeping purposes.
- Loan Limit – The sanctioning, management and monitoring of limits is handled by an external limit solution. This sanctioned limit can be attached to the loan, in the Lending TBC, by populating the limit key from the external limit solution.
- Interest on Loan - Lending TBC supports multiple interest rate types, such as fixed, floating and periodic interest rate - with different interest basis and accrual method. The interest can be calculated on different balance types. It is also possible to calculate interest on loans, using the Rule of 78 method. When the loan amount is disbursed in tranches, the interest for the loan can be calculated as a weighted average rate.
- Loan Charges – With Lending TBC, it is possible to levy charges at regular frequencies or on triggering an activity or when a rule is broken.
- Tax – Tax can be collected on interest and charges, based on tax rules and considering the customer’s demographic details.
- Scheduling of Payments – The repayment of a loan can be scheduled at regular intervals, so that the accrued interest and charges are billed to the borrower, along with the principal at the defined frequency. Also, it is possible to amend the repayment terms of an existing loan, such as changing the loan repayment date, defining repayment holiday, delaying the due dates of the repayments and so on.
- Overpayments – It is possible for the borrower of a loan contract to deposit an overpayment amount. This additional amount can be collected on top of the scheduled instalment or as a lump sum ad-hoc payment.
- Restrictions on Loans - The bank can configure and apply restrictions on transactions or activities, such as pre-closure or prepayments to loans.
- Settlement of Bills - Interest and charges that are billed on loans can be capitalised to the same account or forwarded as a settlement request by publishing an event to an account or beneficiary outside the Lending TBC. The settlement is done as per payment rules applied to the contract.
- Payment Holiday – Lending TBC provides the ability to define payment holiday for a loan contract, to modify or skip some of the scheduled payments, based on certain rules configured by the bank.
- Advance Payment of Instalments – Lending TBC provides the ability to a borrower, to pay some of the upcoming instalments, in advance.
- Delinquency – Lending TBC is enabled to automatically age overdue (past due) the bills, based on configured rules and supports calculation of overdue fees or penalty interest rates, production of chasers and so on.
- Renegotiation – Provides the ability to re-negotiate and modify the terms and conditions of an existing loan.
- Interest Adjustments - Back-valued changes – transactions or rate changes – result in automatic recalculation of interest, through reverse-and-replay.
- Loan Rollover – Lending TBC supports the manual or scheduled renewal or rollover of a loan contract, based on certain conditions.
- Change Product - Provides the ability to change the product of a loan contract, as an upgrade or downgrade based on the customer eligibility and/or rating or as decided by the bank.
- Loan Prepayments – Provides the ability to the customer to prepay a certain portion of the loan principle in advance. Based on the configuration, the customer can be optionally charged or even restricted from making these prepayments.
- Loan Pre-closure – Provides the ability for early full repayment of a loan, before its contractual maturity. Based on the configuration, the customer can be optionally charged or even restricted from pre-closing the loan contract.
- Loan Closure - TBC supports the closure of the loan based on the customer’s request.
- Loan Charge-off - Lending TBC provides the ability to, fully or partially, charge-off a loan contract, without impacting the customer balances. The system is capable of maintaining the charge-off balances, remaining bank book and the actual customer balances. Repayments can be apportioned to bank balances and customer balances as per the configuration. Charge-off can be performed for various reasons, such as a high-risk borrower, loan being under-collateralised and so on.
- Loan Write-off – When the borrower becomes insolvent, banks can write off loans in the Lending TBC, to eliminate a portion or the full loan amount from its balance sheet.
- Migration of Lending Arrangements – Loan contracts can be migrated from an external legacy system to the Lending TBC, through the functionality provided.
- Alerts – Provides the ability to configure alerts on loan contracts and when an alert is triggered, the system publishes an event that should be consumed by the appropriate external system to deliver the alert to the customer or bank’s staff, as required.

The below-described features are not provided by the Lending TBC:

- Eligibility - The eligibility conditions and checking for a loan should be handled by an external component, either a Temenos’ solution, such as Temenos Enterprise Pricing, or a third-party solution, such as the Bank’s onboarding or origination solution.
- Accounting - An external accounting solution should handle the bookkeeping and accounting entries. Lending TBC uses soft accounting to update the balances from the disbursements, repayments and so on and, publishes events that should be consumed by the external system for taking care of the bookkeeping.
- Limit - An external limit system should handle the limit sanctioning, management, monitoring, and other related features.
- Delivery – The delivery and activity messaging are not supported by Lending TBC and should be handled by an external system, which will consume the events published by the Lending TBC.
- Alerts – An external system handles the delivery of alerts to the customer based on the events consumed from Lending TBC based on the setup in the alert condition. Once the alert is successfully processed in the external solution, the external system sends an event to the Lending TBC.
- Loan securitisation – The features related to loan securitisation is not currently applicable in Lending TBC.

### 3.33  New Loan Simulation


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *AA provides a simulation tool for decision making for prospects and existing customers. The simulation engine performs real time activities - without creating or updating the live records and producing outputs for the activities. These outputs help in comparison and decision making. These simulated ...*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY`, `AA.SIMULATION.CAPTURE`, `AA.SIMULATION.MONITOR`, `AA.SIMULATION.RUNNER`, `BNK/AA.SIMULATION.SERVICE`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Auto Run*, *Date*, *Execute Simulation*, *Include Future Disb*, *Interest Rate*, *Number of Payments*, *Payment Account*, *Principal Amount* ... +3 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With


#### 📖 Introduction

AA provides a simulation tool for decision making for prospects and existing customers. The simulation engine performs real time activities - without creating or updating the live records and producing outputs for the activities. These outputs help in comparison and decision making. These simulated activities can be retained for user-defined days and if the customers opt for the same, the simulated activities can be executed into a live transaction. During simulation of increase commitment, the new repayment amount can be projected in Payment Schedule upfront to the customer.

There are no specific limitations for simulation of loans in the TBC.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

Simulation in business terms refers to the ability to perform a single or a series of business operations in the system and obtaining the outcome without actually applying these changes to the live system. The simulations are performed for every stage of the loan life cycle such as new loan illustrations, renewal of exiting loans, and payoff calculations.


##### Simulation Capture

The AA.SIMULATION.CAPTURE application is used to capture this information. The simulation capture process is similar to the process used when creating a new arrangement using the AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY .


##### Simulation Runner

Once the information for simulation is captured, the AA.SIMULATION.RUNNER application is used to run the simulation.Further information such as the simulation end date, simulation currency, simulation run date, simulation date and the simulation reference value are added.


##### Simulation Results

The AA.SIMULATION.MONITOR enquiry displays the status of a service. This enquiry considers the simulation runner ID as input and returns the status of the service (whether the service has completed processing or not).


##### Product Conditions

The user can edit the simulation run date to turn a simulation live on the current date instead of the capture date and retain the same terms as of the capture date. Thus, the date on the simulation runner could be a date after the simulation capture date and future dates as well, subject to the product availability.

- For non-tracking product conditions that occur between the AA.SIMULATION.CAPTURE date and the actual run date of simulation, and when the Run Activity field of AA.SIMULATION.RUNNER is set to Yes, the system turns the simulation live as per the date manually modified on Date field. However all the conditions, terms and financials associated with the application, are retained as is on the live arrangements/activities, regardless of any changes on product conditions applied at product level between the simulation date (on AA.SIMULATION.CAPTURE ) and the actual booking date (modified on AA.SIMULATION.RUNNER ). The non-tracking and custom tracking conditions are retained as is, as stored in the individual SIM files.
- For tracking property changes between AA.SIMULATION.CAPTURE and AA.SIMULATION.RUNNER execution, the system tracks the updated product conditions while turning the activity/arrangement live.


##### New Loan Simulation

It allows the user to calculate simulation scenarios by combining variable and fixed values and pass them into the system. In Lending, the user has to enter the required details in the mandatory fields of the loan such as Principal Amount , Term , Interest Rate , Number of Payments and Payment Account .


##### Increase Commitment Simulation

The new repayment amount with respect to increased commitment is updated in Payment Schedule projection during simulation when the respective activity is set to recalculate in the Payment Schedule Property Conditions.

For future scheduled increased commitment, the new repayment amount in conjunction with the increased commitment can be projected when the Include Future Disb attribute in Payment Schedule conditions is set to Progressive.


##### Simulation Comparison

It is based on the list of simulation available within the existing arrangement. This workflow allows the banks to compare two or more simulated arrangements to an existing contract and choose the best one. Additionally, the user can also print the comparison overview screen if required.

The comparison window is available under the Additional details of the Lending Arrangement overview screen.

> **⚠️ Note:** For simulation comparison, a minimum of two simulation references should be selected for an existing arrangement.

The features related to comparison of simulations are not applicable for loans in the TBC. However, the user can create multiple simulations of the loan for different conditions separately and manually compare the simulated results.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section details on how simulation can be captured, amended and executed for loans.


##### Amend Simulation Capture

The user can amend the simulation capture. The Update Prod Condition attribute in AA.SIMULATION.CAPTURE defines whether or not to refresh the property conditions in the simulation capture record using the latest product conditions.

Additionally, while amending the simulation capture, the effective date can be changed to the required date and the Update Prod Condition attribute can be defined to use the product condition or the SIM records for the new effective date.

If the effective date needs to be changed, the Auto Run attribute needs to be manually set to Simulate.

Read Amend the Simulation Capture for more information.


##### Amend Simulation

The user can amend a simulated record for further simulation by inserting or adding activities, such as Pre-payment, Payment Rules Change, and so on, to be run on the respective dates. To achieve this, the date on which the Activity is to be run should be specified, and the Run Activity attribute should be set to Yes in the AA.SIMULATION.RUNNER application.


##### Information Storage and Retrieval

Once the AA.SIMULATION.RUNNER record has been authorised, the TSA.SERVICE agent and BNK/AA.SIMULATION.SERVICE record need to run. This action stores the required data in different files for retrieval later. After the service run has been completed, the $SIM files for information retrieval are updated.


##### Execute Simulation

After the storage of information onto different files, the user can opt to have a LIVE arrangement in the system depending on the customer’s final decision. This can be achieved by setting the Execute Simulation attribute to Yes in the AA.SIMULATION.RUNNER application.

Read the AA user guide on Simulations for more information.


> **Related Applications:** `AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY`, `AA.SIMULATION.CAPTURE`, `AA.SIMULATION.MONITOR`, `AA.SIMULATION.RUNNER`, `BNK/AA.SIMULATION.SERVICE`

### 3.34  Overpayment


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Overpayment allows the borrower to pay an additional amount on top of the monthly instalment. It is an additional amount paid regularly or one lump sum adhoc repayment. Overpayment is a common feature in the mortgage business. A mortgage product can allow overpayments and the mortgage loan contract ...*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.BILL.DETAILS`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Actual Amt*, *Bill Type*, *Bills Combined*, *Calc Type*, *Combine Bill*, *End Date*, *Frequency*, *Mand Prop Class* ... +12 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With


#### 📖 Introduction

Overpayment allows the borrower to pay an additional amount on top of the monthly instalment. It is an additional amount paid regularly or one lump sum adhoc repayment. Overpayment is a common feature in the mortgage business. A mortgage product can allow overpayments and the mortgage loan contract can record the details of overpayment permissible with its terms and conditions. For example, the bank can define a limit for the overpayment and it does not accept overpayments breaching the limit. It can also optionally levy an early repayment charge on the overpayment amount.

The features related to automatic settlement of the overpayment amount is are not applicable for loans in TBC.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

Mortgage Overpayments is a provision where the banks allow the customer or borrower to make additional payments over the agreed contractual mortgage payment. The borrower can make these overpayments as:

- A lump sum, where the borrower pays an adhoc lump sum amount
- Regular overpayments, where the borrower pays a monthly regular payment on top of the standard contractual mortgage monthly repayment.

In some mortgage products, the lender does not allow the borrower to pay the lump sum overpayment amount. In certain cases, the lender permits overpayments with some restriction like allowing the overpayments after a certain period. In such cases, any overpayment during the restricted period is allowed by collecting a fee.

Similarly, there are mortgage products where the lenders can either allow regular overpayments with some restrictions or not allow regular overpayment.

AA allows the user to configure a lump sum or regular overpayment in the product with or without charges and limits for overpayment. The products can have a cap amount defined for the overpayment. The overpayment breaching this cap amount incurs charges or the overpayment can be blocked. The periodic attribute in Payment Rules controls whether the overpayment is allowed for the mortgage product.


##### Overpayment Payment Schedules

The user can schedule an overpayment using a payment type, for example Overpay, where the user can set the following values for fields:

- Type - Manual
- Calc Type - Actual
- Bill Type - INFO

The loan principal (which is the account property) can only be scheduled using an overpayment. The Refer Schedule field defines the payment frequency and payment method that the overpayment schedule should follow. For example, the overpayment schedule follows the constant repayment schedule as shown below.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Refer Schedule attribute is not mandatory for scheduling the Overpayment Payment Schedule


##### Limiting Overpayments

The user can define a limit on the overpayment using the overpayment limit type. The limit type defines the overpayment limit as a fixed amount or percentage of the total loan amount or the outstanding loan amount. The user can define periodic attributes in the repayment rules to limit overpayments in the loan by either:

- Defining a fixed overpayment limit amount
- Calculating the overpayment limit amount based on the total loan amount
- Calculating the overpayment limit amount based on the outstanding loan amount

The table below lists the Periodic Attribute Classes that define the overpayment limits.

| Periodic Attribute Class | Description |
|---|---|
| ADHOC.PREPAY.CURRENT | Calculates the lump sum overpayment limit amount as a percentage of outstanding loan amount. |
| ADHOC.PREPAY.TOTAL | Calculates the lump sum overpayment limit amount as a percentage of total loan amount. |
| ADHOC.PREPAY.VALUE | Defines the lump sum overpayment limit as a fixed amount. |
| REGULAR.PREPAY.CURRENT | Calculates the regular overpayment limit amount as a percentage of outstanding loan amount. |
| REGULAR.PREPAY.TOTAL | Calculates the regular overpayment limit amount as a percentage of total loan amount. |
| REGULAR.PREPAY.VALUE | Defines the regular overpayment limit as a fixed amount. |

The user can create a periodic attribute under the Periodic Attribute class to control the overpayment limit effective period.

The overpayment limit can be monitored periodically, say for a repeating period of one year from the loan disbursement or from the loan creation date. Thus the limit reset period can be defined using the Period Type , Period and Rule Start accordingly.

The screenshot below is an example of periodic attributes that control the overpayment limit from the start date of the arrangement or loan opening date.

The user has to define this periodic attribute as a rule in the Payment Rule condition to define the overpayment limit is applicable for a product.


##### Repayment Configuration for Overpayments

The flowchart below depicts the recommended Payment Rule configuration in a loan product with a configured overpayment. When the loan receives a repayment, the system evaluates and settles the repayments as,

- Repayments for overdue bills
- Repayments for due bills
- Scheduled overpayment
- Lumpsum overpayment
- Overpayment with a penalty
- Principal decrease
- Unallocated credit.

Thus the payment rule evaluates the amount to be allocated to the overpayment activity for both regular and adhoc overpayments.

> **⚠️ Note:** The allocation of funds received during an overpayment can be configured using the Remainder Activity in the payment rules condition. Banks can choose to allocate these funds as a principal decrease (regular overpayment, lumpsum overpayment, overpayment with penalty) or unallocated credit balance.

The user can pass the excess amount after settling the current outstanding due to the regular overpayments’ payment rule. The workflow below is an illustration for such repayment rule configurations.

The regular overpayments have a periodic attribute that evaluates the limit as a fixed amount. Similarly, the periodic attribute can evaluate the limit as a % against the current outstanding amount or total loan amount.

The period that is considered by the periodic attribute while evaluating the limit is based on the calendar or arrangement start date.

In the loan product, the user can pass the excess amount after settling the regular overpayments to adhoc or lump sum overpayments payment rule.

The workflow below is an illustration for lump sum overpayments where the periodic attribute evaluates the limit as a loan amount. Similarly, the periodic attribute can evaluate the limit as a percentage against the current outstanding amount or total loan amount.

The period that is by the periodic attribute while evaluating the limit is based on the calendar or arrangement start.


#### 🔧 Working With

Mortgage overpayment is a provision where banks allow the customer or borrower to make additional payments over the agreed contractual mortgage payment. The borrower can make overpayment in two ways:

- Lumpsum Overpayment - When the borrower makes an adhoc payment and it can be made when the borrower affords. A mortgage loan of EUR 200,000 with tenor of ten years at an interest rate of 4%. The borrower can make a lump sum payment of EUR 15,000 in a year.
- Regular Overpayment - When the borrower agrees with the bank to make an additional amount on top of the regular agreed contractual monthly payment. A mortgage loan of EUR 200,000 with a tenor of ten years at an interest rate of 4% with the monthly regular payment of EUR 1000. The borrower can opt to pay an additional amount of EUR 500 monthly.

Overpayment has the following benefits:

- Payoff the mortgage earlier
- Reduce the amount of interest payable

The overpayment feature in mortgage loans in AA has the ability to:

- Define a regular overpayment in the loan
- Accept a lumpsum overpayment in the loan
- Place a control on the amount of overpayment received over a period


##### Controlling Overpayment Amount and Related Charges

The banks can control the amount of overpayment in a loan. It can specify the amount of overpayment allowed to be a:

- Percentage of a total loan amount or
- Percentage of the outstanding loan amount (at that overpayment date) or
- A fixed amount allowed to be overpaid.

This allowed overpayment amount is recalculated on a regular basis (like yearly or quarterly) or can be for the life of the loan (using the PERIOD.TYPE and PERIOD periodic attribute fields).

For limiting the overpayment based on the total loan amount (total commitment) and fixed amount , the allowed overpayment is constant throughout the loan life cycle or for the specified cycle. (This allowed overpayment amount might change only in extreme situations like an increase in total loan sanctioned to the customer or an increase or decrease in the allowed overpayment amount due to the modification in the terms and conditions).

In the case where the overpayment amount is controlled as a percentage on the outstanding loan amount (CUR ), the overpayment limit amount is updated on a regular basis as the outstanding loan amount (CUR ) varies throughout the life of the loan.


###### Regular Overpayment

For a regular overpayment, the Payment Schedule condition can be used to define a scheduled overpayment and it can be set to have the same schedule date as regular scheduled installment. When the customer requests a scheduled overpayment, the user adds a schedule in the loan with:

- Payment Type as Overpay. This Payment Type should have: Type as Manual Calc Type as Actual Mand Prop Class as Account

- Actual Amt to specify the overpayment amount that should be scheduled
- Refer Schedule to specify the installment payment type (for example CONSTANT) so that Frequency and Method of installment payment type is reused
- Bill Type should be Info.
- Num to specify the number of overpayments

When the user defines the Num field as three, then there are only three overpayments scheduled. If End Date or Num is not specified, the overpayments are scheduled, until they are manually removed or simply open-ended.

The overpayment should generate a Bill Type as INFO and Payment Method should be set as Due. Thus, the overpayment amount is not considered for ageing/overdue and Accrual by bill process.

> **⚠️ Note:** When a regular overpayment bill is scheduled and configured for settlement, the overpayment bill gets automatically settled like any other obligatory payment.

The below screenshot displays an Info bill raised for an overpayment. The Or Total Amount and Or Prop Amount are set as 200, while the Os Total Amount is not updated since it is not considered for Info Type Bill. This implies that the overpayment does not generate an outstanding item with pending settlement (not an obligatory payment for customer and therefore not aged due to pending settlement).

The system currently allows to schedule the overpayments in same frequency as the scheduled repayment using the Refer Schedule with or without number of overpayments. It is possible to combine an overpayment schedule with a regular repayment schedule bill using the Combine Bill Option. In the above screenshot, the Combine Bill option is not set. Hence a separate bill is raised for the overpayment updating only the overpayment fields in the AA.BILL.DETAILS .

The features related to automatic settlement of the overpayment amount are not applicable for loans in TBC.

Consider a scenario where the regular overpayment is set as 10% of the total loan amount (TOTCOMMITMENT) applicable from the arrangement start date with the overpayment limit resetting yearly. The lump sum overpayment is restricted.

Consider a mortgage loan for USD 100,000. The Payment schedule for this product has a regular overpayment of USD 200 scheduled for three instalments, Bill Type is set as Info, the Refer Schedule field is set as CONSTANT and Bills Combined as Yes.

In the below screenshot it is evident that a bill is generated and it contains the total due of USD 2977.84 to be settled. It has also generated the Info pay details that contain the overpayment of USD 200, which is not an obligatory payment by the customer.

The funds are settled using the Payment Rules. A payment of USD 5000 is made, out of which:

- The outstanding due bill of USD 2977.84 and New Arrangement Fee of USD 999, which makes up to a total of USD 3976.84, is settled first, using the LENDING-APPLYPAYMENT-PR.REPAYMENT activity
- Then, USD 200 is allocated to Regular overpayment using the LENDING-APPLYPAYMENT-PR.REGULAR.OVERPAY activity

The Overpayment enquiry (AA.DETAILS.OVERPAY) in the Arrangement Overview page provides a summary of the overpayment, as shown in the screenshot below.

This loan has an allowed overpayment limit of USD 1000 where USD 200 is used and USD 800 is remaining.


###### Lumpsum Overpayment

A lump sum overpayment refers to an excess payment received from the customer as an adhoc overpayment (and not against any outstanding bills in the loan).

Consider a scenario where the regular overpayment is restricted by setting zero as the cap value in the repayment rule. The adhoc overpayment has a 10% limit on the total loan amount (TOTCOMMITMENT) applicable from the arrangement date with the overpayment limit resetting yearly. Read Limiting Overpayment section for more information on the overpayment limit.

Consider a mortgage loan for USD 10000. As regular overpayment is restricted, the payment schedule is setup only for the regular installment. In this case, the setup is for constant repayment of principal and interest.In the example, the calculated installment amount is USD 83.16.

When the repayment received is more than the due amount of USD 83.16, the reminder activity for adhoc overpayment is triggered for the excess amount received.

- Here it is evident that a repayment USD 283.16 is received and allocated to the regular repayment
- No amount is allocated to the scheduled or regular overpayment
- USD 200 is allocated to adhoc overpayment

In the screenshot below, the Arrangement Overview enquiry (AA.DETAILS.OVERPAY) displays that the regular overpayment is restricted, and the lump sum overpayment has a limit of USD 1000, where USD 200 is only utilised in the life of the arrangement.


###### Regular and Lumpsum Overpayment

A loan can have regular and adhoc repayments received as a single payment. Both regular and adhoc overpayments can be enabled for a loan and a charge can be configured, if the customer breaches the said overpayment limit agreed by the bank or financial institutions, using Activity Charges Product Condition.

This product has a repayment rule that triggers:

- Overdue payments
- Regular payments
- Regular overpayments
- Ad hoc overpayments
- Principal decrease

The user can set limit for regular and lumpsum overpayment separately as 10% of the total loan amount with the limit reset period as arrangement start date.

When the customer requests a scheduled overpayment, the user adds a schedule in the loan with

- Payment Type as Overpay. This Payment Type should have: Type as Manual Calc Type as Actual Mand Prop Class as ACCOUNT
- Actual Amt has to specify the overpayment amount that should be scheduled
- Refer Schedule as installment payment type (for example, CONSTANT) so that the Frequency and Method of installment payment type is reused.
- Bill Type should be Info.

A prepay charge is configured such that, whenever the overpayment limit is breached, a charge is applied on the excess payment. Here a prepay charge of 5% is levied when the LENDING-APPLYPAYMENT-PR.PRINCIPAL.DECREASE activity is triggered, which indicates that the overpayment limit is breached, hence the activity is triggered and the charge is applied.

Consider a mortgage loan created for USD 10000 and it is effective from 01 April, 2022. Based on the setup the overpayment limit is calculated as USD 1000 for regular and lumpsum overpayment.

The Payment Schedule for this product has a Regular Overpayment of USD 500 scheduled, the Bill Type is set as Info, the Refer Schedule is set as CONSTANT and Bills Combined set as Yes.

In the screenshot below it is evident that a bill is generated that contains the total due of USD 171.98 to be settled. It also generated the info pay details that contains the overpayment of USD 500, which is not an obligatory payment by the customer.

A payment of USD 4000 is made.

The funds are settled using the Payment Rule conditions attached to the product. A Payment of USD 4000 is made and the funds are apportioned as:

- The outstanding due bill of USD 171.98 and New Arrangement Fee of USD 999, which makes up to a total of USD 1170.98, is settled first, using the LENDING-APPLYPAYMENT-PR.REPAYMENT activity.
- Then USD 500 is allocated towards Regular Overpayment using the LENDING-APPLYPAYMENT-PR.REGULAR.OVERPAY activity.
- USD 500 is allocated towards Lumpsum Overpay using the LENDING-APPLYPAYMENT-PR.ADHOC.OVERPAY activity.
- Upon breaching the overpay limit, USD 1828.32 is applied as Principal Decrease using the LENDING-APPLYPAYMENT-PR.PRINCIPAL.DECREASE activity.
- Then a prepay charge is triggered on the excess repayment using the LENDING-ISSUEBILL-PREPAYFEE activity.

As the overpayment limit is breached, the excess amount of USD 1828.32 is apportioned towards pprincipal decrease and a PREPAYFEE is raised against excess amount and charged as per the applicable conditions.

5% of PREPYAFEE charge is applied on the excess repayment amount of USD 1828.32

The Overpayment enquiry (AA.DETAILS.OVERPAY) in the Arrangement Overview page provides a summary of the overpayment, as shown in the screenshot below. This loan has an allowed overpayment limit of USD 1000 where USD 500 is against Regular Overpayment and USD 500 is used against Lumpsum as per the applicable conditions, hence exhausting the limit amount for the current period.


> **Related Applications:** `AA.BILL.DETAILS`
