### 3.41  Tax


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Tax is applied either on financial properties of an arrangement or on specific transactions. Financial properties include interest, charge, periodic charge, and account.*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY`, `CUSTOMER.CHARGE`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Actual Group*, *Context Tax Code*, *Context Tax Condition*, *Make Due*, *Prop Payment Method*, *Prop Tax Code*, *Prop Tax Cond*, *Prop Tax Context* ... +11 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With


#### 📖 Introduction

Tax is applied either on financial properties of an arrangement or on specific transactions. Financial properties include interest, charge, periodic charge, and account.

Tax can be applied on any charge or interest of a loan product. If the value of a bank's intermediation services can be measured by the difference between its loan and deposit interest, then the loans are considered as the bank's output, on which a Value Added Tax can be imposed. Hence, the Tax Property Class is optional at the Product Line level for lending.

For loans in TBC, the tax related assessments are generally performed based on the customer attributes and these attributes are part of an external Party system like the Party TBC. Hence, the tax group that the customer belongs to can be updated using an API in the Actual Group attribute of the CUSTOMER.CHARGE application in TBC.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The system enables tax calculation during issue bills, make due and capitalise for the respective interests, charges, periodic charges, account property and activities when configured in the tax condition. The calculated tax is updated against the TAX Property in the bill.

At the AA product level, the tax can be defined either at Property Class level or at Property level. At the arrangement level, it is possible to remove the values of TAX or TAX.TYPE.CONDITION that default from the product level allowing for zero or no tax calculation.

When calculating the annuity payment, tax can be both included and excluded. This calculation is performed based on the settings indicated in the Tax Inclusive field in Payment Type. If this field is set to Yes, then the annuity is calculated including the principal, interest and tax.

The Accounting Property Class captures whether net or itemised accounting has to be performed on the tax calculated on the amount.

To complete the tax related accounting, the TBC generates an event, which can be captured by the connected external GL (General Ledger) system.


##### Tax on Activities

Tax can be calculated on the transaction amount, bill amount or any balance when specific activities with activity class Type Process.tax are triggered. The user can configure the Trans Activity , Trans Bill Type , Trans Source Type , Trans Payment Type , and Trans Source Balance fields in the AA Tax property to define the activity on which the tax is to be calculated.

For Lending product line, tax can be calculated for the following activities:

- Disbursement of a loan from a payment system
- Loan Repayment, Principal Decrease and other transactions triggered from a payment system (i.e., LENDING-APPLYPAYMENT-PAYMENT.RULES and LENDING-APPLYPAYMENT-PAYOUT.RULES)
- Issue Bill for Charge, Periodic charges, and Payment schedule.


##### Tax on Account Property Made-Due or Paid

The user can define the tax condition to calculate tax on ACCOUNT property that is made-due or paid. For example, during maturity of the loan, the residual principal amount is made-due and a tax amount can be collected on this residual amount by setting the Property field to the Account property defined in the loan product. The Prop Tax Code or Prop Tax Cond field should be defined to specify the details (rate) for tax calculation.

For Lending product line, tax is calculated on ACCOUNT property during:

- Auto disbursement of loan amount
- Loan Maturity (Tax on the residual principal amount that is made-due)
- Loan pre-closure or payoff (Tax on the DUE balance created during loan closure)
- Scheduled Make-Due of ACCOUNT properties (that is, Tax on DUE balance created during scheduled make-due based on the payment schedule definition).


##### Overriding Default Tax Conditions using Context Types

For tax on activities, it is possible that the user can pass overriding tax rate/amount at the AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY level by using the context fields. This can be done by defining the Prop Tax Context , Tax Context , Context Tax Code , and Context Tax Condition fields in the Tax condition.

Read Overriding Default Tax Conditions using Context Types for more information.


#### 🔧 Working With

Tax can be applied on the interest and charge amount levied on the account. Different types of tax can be calculated. The tax amounts can be displayed separately or after netting off with the interest or charge, on customer statements. It is possible to split the tax liability between different owners of the account.

Tax can be calculated on interest and charges and this component is included as part of the bill amount.


##### Tax on Accrued Interest

At any point in the life cycle of the contract like advance payment, partial pre-closure, etc., tax can be calculated and collected proportionately for the accrued interest collected. The system can be configured to calculate the tax on accrued interest (both principal interest and penalty interest) at the time of collection of that interest when Tax Inclusive is set as Yes in the corresponding Payment Rule Type used at the time of repayment.

When tax is collected on the accrued interest (both principal interest and penalty interest) it is mandatory that the interest and the tax are made due and settled. This implies, the account statement would include the information about accrued interest collected in advance and the corresponding tax amount collected. This is achieved by setting the Make Due field as Yes in the corresponding Payment Rule Type used at the time of repayment.

> **⚠️ Note:** If Tax Inclusive is set as Yes, then Make Due should also be set as Yes. Else, the system raises an error when the Payment Rule Type is committed.


##### Tax on Activities

Tax can be calculated on the transaction amount, bill amount or any balance for specific activities. The AA Tax property can be defined to mention the activity for which tax is to be calculated, the source balance, and other details for calculating the tax amount. Consider,

- Transaction amount – USD 10,000
- Federal tax rate – 10%
- State tax rate – 15%

| Net | Gross |
|---|---|
| Federal tax amount = 10%*10,000=1000 State tax rate = 15%*10,000=1500 Total tax amount = 1000+1500=2500 | Federal tax amount =(10,000/(100-15)*10)=1333.33 State tax rate = (10,000/(100-15)*15)=2000 Total tax amount = 1333.33+2000=3333.33 |

##### Tax on Account Property Made-Due or Paid

The user can define the Tax condition to calculate tax on ACCOUNT property that is made-due or paid by setting the Property field to the Account property defined in the loan product. Consider,

##### Overriding Default Tax Conditions using Context Types

The tax rate that is configured at the tax condition level can be overridden at the arrangement activity level for tax on activities. The user can pass overriding tax rate/amount at the AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY level using the context fields.

Read Overriding Default Tax Conditions using Context Types for more information.


##### Recovery Order for Tax

In an overdue loan scenario, the banks prefer to settle the tax component first, before collecting the other components of the loan. This enables banks to collect the tax (either fully or partially) when there is a partial payment on the loan.

Banks can prioritise the repayment amount to settle the tax component first. To enable this feature, the Tax Settlement field in the Payment Rule Property Class is used. The allowed values of this field are:

- Separated – Sequences the Tax Property in the Property field in Payment Rule product condition. The Tax Settlement in Payment Rule cannot have the option set as Separated when the corresponding Payment Rule Type has Tax Inclusive set as Yes. That means recovery order to collect tax first cannot be set on prepayments, payoff and advance payment of interest. When the penalty interest is set to accrue by bills and tax has to be collected, order recovery cannot be separated. For a contract when tax must be recovered first and tax is applied on both principal interest and penalty interest (where penalty interest is accrue by bills), there must be two payment rules configured as shown below:
- Prorate - Indicates that Tax should be calculated and collected on a pro-rated method based on the repaid amount. This is the default value.

To know further click here .

### 3.42  Types of Loan

> **Purpose:** *The banks offer loan products to their customers to meet different financial requirements. Some of the loans may have a defined maturity date, while others may have the capability to be renewed or rolled over upon reaching the maturity date. Further, some loans have a short term (for example, 3 mont...*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Change Date*, *Change Period*, *Change Product*, *Maturity  date*, *Maturity Date*, *Report End Date*, *Term*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With


#### 📖 Introduction

The banks offer loan products to their customers to meet different financial requirements. Some of the loans may have a defined maturity date, while others may have the capability to be renewed or rolled over upon reaching the maturity date. Further, some loans have a short term (for example, 3 months) or a much longer term (for example, 25 years). It is also possible to offer loans that have no term or maturity date associated with the arrangement, which are referred to as Call loans. The banks can also customise the conditions based on which these loans are offered to the customers; for example, a high priority customer can get a loan at a lesser rate of interest.

There are no specific limitations for handling different types of loans (such as term loans, call loans and so on) in the TBC.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The Term Amount Property Class is used to configure the tenure of the loan. The Term or Maturity Date attribute can be used to indicate the loan tenure.


##### Term Loan

A term loan can range from a short-term loan, for example, with a term up to 18 months to a long-term loan, for example, with a repayment period of up to 25 years. It is also possible to offer the customers an intermediate term loan with a repayment period extending up to three years. It is evident that there is either a Term or Maturity Date that is associated with term loan. Further, it is also possible to assign the Change Product attribute to a term loan.

The rate of interest can be fixed for the term or it can be a floating rate based on an internal or a marked index rate like LIBOR with or without a spread. It is possible to change the term or the rate of interest in case of a long-term loan. Though it is also possible to do the same for a short or an intermediate term loan as well.

The charges and fees that are associated with the term loan can be fixed for all customers, but it is also possible to have a preferential pricing in case of priority customers.

The user can define and evaluate the features related to preferential pricing for a loan, using TEP (Temenos Enterprise Pricing).


##### Call Loan

A call loan is characterised by:

- Term and Maturity date are not specified in Term Amount Property
- Change Product Property is not configured If Change Product Property is configured with a value specified in either Change Period or Change Date , it is considered as Fixed Term.


#### 🔧 Working With

The following section shows examples of types of loans.


##### Term Loan

The below screenshot shows an overview of a long-term loan with a floating rate of interest. The AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS table reflects the Report End Date which is calculated based on the term defined during the arrangement creation.


##### Call Loan

The below screenshot shows an example of a call loan. In the Arrangement Overview screen, there is no term or maturity date defined for this arrangement. Further, the AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS table does not reflect the Report End Date .

For contract maturity reports, Report End Date in AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS is referred instead of Maturity Date . The Report End Date field is updated thus: The next renewal date if it precedes the maturity date The maturity date if there is no renewal scheduled before the maturity date Null if it is a call contract and there is no renewal scheduled


> **Related Applications:** `AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS`

### 3.43  Weighted Average Rate


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *When loans are being disbursed in multiple tranches, each having its own interest rate a Weighted Average Rate (WAR) for the arrangement has to be calculated and applied to the contract after each disbursement .*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Include Prin Amount*, *On Activity*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With


#### 📖 Introduction

When loans are being disbursed in multiple tranches, each having its own interest rate a Weighted Average Rate (WAR) for the arrangement has to be calculated and applied to the contract after each disbursement .

A weighted average interest rate is an average that is adjusted to reflect the contribution of each loan to the total debt. The weighted average multiplies each loan’s disbursement interest rate by the loan balance and divides the sum by the total loan balance. Each loan’s disbursement interest rate contributes to the weighted average in proportion to the loan’s percentage of the total debt.

The Weighted Average Rate Type of Interest condition enables the calculation of the weighted average rate, which determines the actual effective rate of the arrangement.

There are no specific limitations with regards to calculating and processing of weighted average rates for loans in TBC. It is not possible to automatically disburse the commitment amount for loans in TBC.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

Each disbursement has its own interest rate when loans are being disbursed in multiple tranches and the system can calculate a Weighted Average Rate (WAR) or Effective Rate for the arrangement, that needs to be re-calculated after each disbursement.

The calculated effective rate is used by the arrangement account to generate the instalments of the customer depending on the amount outstanding derived by multiple tranches being used or payments applied to the loan.

Whenever a change of interest or rate reset happens, the WAR or effective rate calculated during the last disbursement has to be replaced considering the new rate given.

The Weighted Average Rate Type of Interest condition in interest product condition should be selected as shown below.

Read the WAR section in Interest Property Class for further information on configuration of WAR.


##### Recalculation of WAR

While defining the interest details the WAR gets recalculated each time a disbursement happens, a rate reset event is scheduled or when there is repayments. On Activity should be set to (RECALCULATE) Rate for disbursement and rate reset activities .

> **⚠️ Note:** Change of interest/ Repayments is considered only when new disbursement is triggered WAR is not calculated for future projected disbursement schedules when Include Prin Amount is defined in Payment Schedule condition. Whereas WAR calculation happens when an actual process takes place.


#### 🔧 Working With

The following section provides an illustration of the Weighted Average Rate calculation.

Assume that a commitment of 29,000 is approved on 02 Jan 2020 for the customer and the drawings happen in multiple disbursements:

| Disbursement No | Disbursement Amount (USD) | Int. Rate/Disbursement | Interest Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 9,000.00 | 7.25 | - |
| 2 | 10,000.00 | 7.25 | 7.75 |
| 3 | 10,000.00 | 7.75 | - |


###### After First Disbursement


###### After Second Disbursement

Considering the same example,

- Loan outstanding is 9000
- New disbursed amount 10000
- Current WAR = 7.25%
- WAR Rate Periodic rate = 7.5% Margin = +0.25%
- Effective rate is updated to 7.75%


###### Subsequent Disbursements (Until Full Disbursement)

Considering the same example, the values are calculated as:

- Loan outstanding is 19,000 (@ 7.51)
- Customer takes another disbursement for 10,000
- Current interest rate Periodic Rate = 7.50% Margin = +0.25%
- Disbursement event is set to recalculate interest rate

The system recalculates the weighted rate considering the current loan outstanding, weighted rate and the amount disbursed & its corresponding rate.

| Disbursement No | Disbursement Amount (EUR) | Int. Rate/Disbursement | Interest Change | WAR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 9,000.00 | 7.25 | - | 7.25 |
| 2 | 10,000.00 | 7.50 | 7.75 | 7.51 |
| 3 | 10,000.00 | 7.75 | - | 7.59 |


###### Rate Reset

Considering the same example, the calculation is as follows:

- Loan outstanding is 29000
- Current WAR = 7.59%
- Rate reset on 17/10/2020 Periodic rate = 7.50% Margin = +0.50%
- Rate reset event is set to recalculate interest rate
- Effective rate is updated to 8%

WAR is not calculated further, the reset rate is applied.

### 3.44  Misc


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Transaction Recycler provides the ability to retry failed financial transactions again at regular intervals. This is a generic retry mechanism which can be consumed by any Temenos Transact application. The Transaction Recycler is available for Arrangement Architecture (AA) and Interest and Charg...*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.PARAMETER`, `MS.PARAMETER`, `RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Aa Product*, *Aa Product Group*, *Attribute Type*, *Attribute Value*, *Create Retry Trigger*, *Custom Priority Rank*, *Date Convention*, *Def Prev Settle* ... +33 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

Related topics:

- Temenos Transact Services

The Transaction Recycler provides the ability to retry failed financial transactions again at regular intervals. This is a generic retry mechanism which can be consumed by any Temenos Transact application. The Transaction Recycler is available for Arrangement Architecture (AA) and Interest and Charged (IC) modules (R13 release and above). Read Transaction Cycler section under Settlement Property Class for more information related to Arrangement Architecture.

The Transaction Recycler service handles the retry of failed transactions. This service will run as a COB job at a specific stage during both End of Day (EOD) and online phases. This job will retry the transactions on scheduled dates until the transaction is settled or number of retry attempts allowed have been exhausted or retry end date is reached.

During each retry, the Transaction Recycler will take the amount available in the settlement account for settling the transaction amount in full or partial, based on the Transaction Recycler retry configuration. The RC can retry the settlement based on pre-defined priority order as defined by the bank. In case of an AA loan repayment, the RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY application allows the user to define sorting priority criteria based on custom values - the bill type or the aging status of bill.

The transactions handed over to Recycler (RC), if settled outside the RC framework are not excluded from further processing by RC and is marked with a specific status.

The following chart shows the transaction recycler process:

The Transaction Recycler acts as a framework and the processing required for retrying an AA payment or IC charges is built as a plug-in. In the above flow chart, the core plug-ins are generally represented as the payment processor, and the RC processes further, when there is an AA payment or an IC payment pending. The Transaction Recycler recognises that two different types of payments should be processed and the respective payment processor invoked is parameterised. This design enables the addition of new activity types (including any client-specific local activities) to be retried while using the same Transaction Recycler framework to orchestrate the recycling.


##### Product Configuration

The following chart shows the Transaction Recycler module components:

| Core Routine Fields | Description | Routine Name |
|---|---|---|
| Pre processor | Used to define whether a message specific core routine needs to be called to pre-process a message. | RC.PREP.RC.TYPE – For example, RC.PREP.IC.CHARGE |
| Prioritise | Used to define the message-specific core routine called by the Transaction Recycler to perform transaction grouping and sorting. | RC.PRTY.RC.TYPE – For example, RC.PRTY.IC.CHARGE |
| Processor | Used to define the message-specific core routine called by the Transaction Recycler to process the Transaction Recycler transaction, or transactions if they are grouped. | RC.PROC.RC.TYPE – For example, RC.PROCE.IC.CHARGE |
| Post process | Defines the message-specific API routine called by the Transaction Recycler to perform processing after the transaction has been completed. | RC.POST.RC.TYPE – For example, RC.POST.IC.CHARGE |

The RC.PRIORITY application is a highest level prioritisation parameter that allows to setup priority of transactions at the company level by EB.SYSTEM.ID or AA.PRODUCT.GROUP . This application is used in conjunction with RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY and RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY to create the rules regarding which type of transaction takes priority when there is more than one outstanding transaction against a settlement account. It ranks by EB.SYSTEM.ID , by AA.PRODUCT.GROUP or by a custom RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY record and the ID to this application can be either a master or a lead company.

In the RC.PRIORITY application, the order of priorities are defined in the descending order (for example, the first definition has the highest priority and so on).

- In the above screenshot, the system is set up to consider the transactions in the following order, if multiple retry requests are posted against the same account:First: Products defined in the RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY application in the PRIORITY+ONE record (direct debits sent by TPH with transaction code 125).

- Second: Products defined in the RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY application in the MORTAGES record (MORTGAGE AA Product and then MORTGAGE.CASHBACK AA Product).

- Third: Products defined in the RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY application in the PRIORITY +TPH record (direct debits sent by TPH with transaction code 213).

- Fourth: Request posted by the PAYMENT.ORDER application, irrespective of the request type.

When using as a priority, either a System ID (an EB.SYSTEM.ID record), the system does not require a correspondent RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY record. If the RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY record is not defined, it will process all retry transaction requests posted by the application in a default order, considering the oldest one received by the recycler first.

> **⚠️ Note:** The system allows only one option for each priority to be entered. This can either be an EB.SYSTEM.ID, an AA.PRODUCT.GROUP or a Product Priority (custom RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY ID ).

Def Prev Settle is a filtering rule that means if, out of a list of ‘n’ pending transactions, one of transactions could not be settled (during retry), then all subsequent pending transactions in that list will be abandoned. It could be set to either Yes or No or left blank. If selected, it is applicable for EB.SYSTEM.ID , AA.PRODUCT.GROUP or Product Priority. This field is mutually exclusive with Prev Settle field.

The Prev Settle field can be set as Yes or No. If set to Yes, during retry of ‘n’ transactions, all transactions must be settled. Even if one of the transactions fail for some reason, then none of the remaining transactions will be considered for settlement.

The RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY application is used in conjunction with RC.PRIORITY and RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY to create the rules regarding the type of transaction that takes priority when there is more than one outstanding transaction against a settlement account. The RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY is used to set the ranks at transaction level for the same type of retry request. It is used to set priority by value date, transaction amount or by a custom setting, for example by bills overdue status sent to Recycler by Arrangement Architecture (AA).

For example, if there are several transactions for the same product type against the settlement account, then the transactions have to be prioritised.

- The oldest transactions are processed first.
- If there are more than one transaction due for the same date and type, then prioritise by the largest amount first.

The RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY application allows the user to define sorting priority criteria based on custom values. For example, based on the bills’ status issued by AA in case of loans repayments. To perform this, set:

- Due Type - Sort By Priority Attribute
- Due Rule - Custom

The Priority Rank Type field in RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY accepts the following three options:

- Aging Status - Enables prioritisation based on the aging status of bills generated for each arrangement.
- Bill Type - Enables prioritisation of bill ( RC.DETAIL ) records based on the bill type of the arrangements.
- Blank – The value is used if the prioritization is by Aging Status of the bills.

It is not possible to set the prioritization by both Aging Status /Blank and Bill Type in the same record.

The multi-valued Custom Priority Rank field must contain custom values in the order which they must be sorted. Based on the Custom Priority Rank the Custom Priority Rank field must contain valid EB.LOOKUP record values from AA.OVERDUE.STATUS or from AA.BILL.TYPE .

In the example below, the custom values represent the overdue bill’s status based on aging / bill type as they are sent by AA to Recycler, to process the retry requests.

> **⚠️ Note:** It is not possible to set the prioritization by both Aging Status / Blank and Bill Type in the same record.

The overdue status is shown in the RC.DETAIL record after the request is settled.

> **⚠️ Note:** The AA Payment Rules setup must be in sync with the setup done in the Recycler priority setup tables. For example, if the oldest bill setup is done in AA Payment Rules, the same setup must be done in the recycler.

For example, if the Payment Rules are setup to consider the oldest bill first for an AA Product, and for the same AA Product, the contract priority rule is setup to consider the largest amount first (different setup than in Payment Rules), the system works as follows:

- If two bills are issued for the same contract on the same date, the system settles the bills by date (oldest one first) ignoring the ‘By amount’ setup in the recycler.
- If two bills are issued for the same contract on different dates, the system settles the bills considering the ‘By amount’ setup in the recycler.
- If two bills are issued for different contracts on different dates, the system settles the bills considering the ‘By amount’ setup in the recycler.
- If two bills are issued for different contracts on the same date, the system settles the bills by date (oldest one first) ignoring the ‘By amount’ setup in the recycler.

The user can define product priorities based on contract custom criteria using the RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY application. If the user wants to define such priority, the Rank Based Priority field must be defined with the RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY custom name. If this is set, the order defined in RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY is applied to all products setup in RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY . For example, it is possible to define custom priority criteria based on bills overdue status and based on product type. The bills overdue status should be setup first in the RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY application as a custom record (read the RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY for more details).

In order to sort the retry request based on the setup in RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY and the one in the product order defined in RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY , Priority Execution field must be defined. The values in this field are ’Rank Then Product’ and ’Product Then Rank’.

If the value ’Rank Then Product’ is selected, if more than one retry request is posted against the same account, the system orders requests based on the rank (status) defined in RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY first and then by the product as defined in RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY . If the value ’Product Then Rank’ is selected, the system orders the requests by product first and then by their rank from the RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY application.

The following screenshot shows the RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY is created with the value ’Rank Then Product’.

The RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY custom record ‘MORTGAGELOANS’ has the setup as shown in the below screenshot.

The RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY record is setup to order the requests according to the rank (status) first and then according to the product order (MORTGAGE.LOANS.USD and then MORTGAGE.LOANS.1Y), if more than one request has the same rank (status).

In case the RC.PRODUCT.PRIORITY record has a custom ID and if the Priority Execution field is defined with the value ’Rank Then Product’, the Aa Product Group field will become multivalued, allowing the definition of priorities based on products which are part of different AA PRODUCT GROUPS in the same record.

The input of Aa Product Group field is mandatory in case any Aa Product are defined. The Aa Product definition is not mandatory if the Aa Product Group is entered. If only the Aa Product Group is defined, the system considers all the retry requests posted by any product type within the product group and orders them by date (the oldest one is considered first). It is not possible to define a duplicate combination of Aa Product Group and Aa Product of the same type in the same record.

The online recycler checks for the following:

- New triggers on the accounts with active retry requests.
- Retry request for which the cut off time has passed.

The RC.PARAMETER application controls the retry trigger and the Create Retry Trigger field can have one of the following options:

- Any Credit – The system creates a retry trigger ( RC.RETRY.TRIGGER table application) for any credit posted on the account.
- Credit Balance – The system creates a retry trigger only if the new credit makes the account balance positive.

In the OVERRIDE record, ACCT.UNAUTH.OD, the Susp Appln field and Fwd Acct Mode should to be configured, as shown in the example below:

| Scenario 1 Schedule Initiation on Holiday parameter is configured | Scenario 2 Schedule Initiation on Holiday parameter is not configured |
|---|---|
| Transaction Recycler retries the transaction to settle the bill. System checks the value date when the settlement account received the funds. As it is backdated, RC settles the bill with value date on Saturday. Penalty interest accrued for Saturday and Sunday is reversed, and only one day of penalty interest is applied to the contract. Bill is settled & Contract status = Current, as of Saturday. | Transaction Recycler retries the transaction to settle the bill. System checks the value date when the settlement account received the funds. As it is backdated, RC settles the bill with the value date on Saturday. Age Overdue activity is reversed and not replayed. Total amount for which the customer is charged = Instalment amount + One day’s penalty. Due to the reversal of the ageing activities, the penalty interest is posted to UNC/remainder activity. |


##### Business Events

When the Emit Business Event field in MS.PARAMETER is set as ‘Yes’, the business events representing the state change are emitted.

The following business events are emitted for Transaction Recycler.

| Business Event | Description |
|---|---|
| settlementService.transactionRetry.currentRetry | Event to be emitted when the transaction retry is moved to current status |
| settlementService.transactionRetry.fundRecovered | Event to be emitted for a transaction retry when the funds are recovered successfully |
| settlementService.transactionRetry.fundReserved | Event to be emitted for a transaction retry when the funds are reserved successfully |
| settlementService.transactionRetry.manuallyApproved | Event to be emitted when a transaction is manually approved |
| settlementService.transactionRetry.retryCancelled | Event to be emitted when the transaction retry is cancelled |
| settlementService.transactionRetry.retryCompleted | Event to be emitted when the transaction retry is completed |
| settlementService.transactionRetry.retryCreated | Event to be emitted when the transaction retry is created |


> **Related Applications:** `AA.PARAMETER`, `MS.PARAMETER`, `RC.CONTRACT.PRIORITY`

### 4.1  ChangeProduct


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Banks can change the product of a multi-currency structure, thereby, performing an upgrade or downgrade of the multi-currency structure.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Allowed Product*, *Default Attribute Option*, *Product*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With


#### 📖 Introduction

Banks can change the product of a multi-currency structure, thereby, performing an upgrade or downgrade of the multi-currency structure.

When the user triggers a change product at the multi-currency account, the sub-accounts also undergo a product change to the sub-account product specified in sub-arrangement rules of the new MCY product.

In addition to the above-mentioned validations and features, during a Change Product activity, like an upgrade or downgrade of the multi-currency structure in the TBC:

- The customer chooses a product from the list of products available.
- The eligibility of the customer for the new product chosen is evaluated by the TEP (Temenos Enterprise Pricing) or another external system.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

During the life cycle of a multi-currency account, the bank can change the product of the MCY account by triggering the Change Product Activity (MULTI.CCY.ACCOUNT-CHANGE.PRODUCT-ARRANGEMENT) at the MCY account level.

When the bank changes the multi-currency account product, the system automatically changes the product for the underlying sub-accounts in the MCY structure. The underlying sub-accounts are changed to the product configured in the Allowed Product field of the sub- arrangement rules condition for the new MCY product (MCY account product to which the multi-currency account is changed).

> **⚠️ Note:** On changing the multi-currency account product, the system automatically changes the product for the underlying sub-accounts only when the Default Attribute Option field in the sub-arrangement rules of the ‘From’ MCY account product is set to Resetting.

Consider there are two multi-currency account products – X and Y with the following setup in the Sub-Arrangement Rules condition for the respective products:

- Product X has the Allowed Product field in sub-arrangement rules condition set to sub-account product A.
- Product Y has the Allowed Product field in sub-arrangement rules condition set to sub-account product B.

An MCY account is created for the customer in the MCY account product X with underlying sub-accounts created in sub-account product A. When the bank user triggers the MULTI.CCY.ACCOUNT-CHANGE.PRODUCT-ARRANGEMENT activity in the MCY account, to change the MCY account product from X to Y, the system automatically triggers a Change Product activity in each of the underlying sub-accounts to change the product of the currency sub-accounts from product A to B as configured in the Sub-Arrangement Rules. This automatic product change in the sub-accounts take place only if the Default Attribute Option field in the Sub-Arrangement Rules of the MCY account product X is set to Resetting.

> **⚠️ Note:** It is not possible to change the product for an MCY account without automatically changing the product for the underlying sub-accounts in the MCY structure.

It is not possible to change the product of the sub account in a MCY structure directly. The user can trigger a change product of the MCY account to itself, during which the sub account product gets changed to the new product added in the sub-arrangement rule conditions.

During the life cycle of a multi-currency (MCY) account, the bank can change the product of the MCY account.

When the user changes the product of a MCY account in the TBC through the API, the TBC triggers the corresponding Change Product Activity (MULTI.CCY.ACCOUNT-CHANGE.PRODUCT-ARRANGEMENT) at the MCY account level. During a change product,

- The customer chooses a product from the list of products available.
- The eligibility of the customer for the new product chosen is evaluated by the TEP (Temenos Enterprise Pricing) or another external system.


#### 🔧 Working With

When the user initiates a change product at the multi-currency account, the sub-accounts also undergo a product change to the product specified in sub arrangement rules of the new MCY product. As a result of this, the entire MCY structure is upgraded or downgraded.


##### Illustration

The illustration below describes the upgrade of a regular MCY structure to a Gold MCY structure.

The sub-arrangement rule conditions of the regular MCY and Gold MCY products are as follows:

- The regular MCY account product has the Allowed Product as MCY Sub Account.
- The Gold MCY product has the Allowed Product as MCY Sub Account - Gold.

Consider an MCY arrangement with base currency as USD and sub accounts created in USD and EURO. This MCY account is created as a regular MCY account product that has Allowed Product set as MCY sub-account.

The user initiates the Change Product Arrangement Activity in the MCY account to change the product from Multi Currency Account to Multi Currency Account (Gold).

The user specifies the product to which the arrangement is to be changed in the Product field of the AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY record.

On authorising this activity, the MCY account product is changed to Multi Currency Account (Gold).

The USD and EUR currency sub-accounts under this MCY structure are also changed to the MCY Sub Account (Gold) product. This is as per the configuration in the Allowed Product field for the Multi Currency Account (Gold) product in the sub-arrangement rules condition.

The following activities are triggered in the given sequence to process the product change in the MCY account and its underlying sub-accounts:

- The user initiates the MULTI.CCY.ACCOUNT-CHANGE.PRODUCT-ARRANGEMENT activity in the multi-currency account. This activity triggers the secondary activity namely ACCOUNTS-CHANGE.PRODUCT-ARRANGEMENT in each of the underlying sub-accounts.

- At any point during the life cycle of a multi-currency account, the bank user can change the Allowed Product field . Any new sub-account created under the MCY structure after this change is created in the new product defined in the Allowed Product field. However, there is no automatic product change for the existing sub-accounts (sub-accounts created before the change in the Allowed Product field) under the MCY structure. To change the product for the existing sub-accounts, the user must initiate a Change Product in the MCY account to itself (that is, to the current MCY account product in which the MCY account is available). As a result of this, all the sub-accounts (including the existing sub-accounts) are automatically changed to the new sub-account product.
- During the product change of an MCY account, the system evaluates if the “To” sub account product is available in the currencies in which sub-account is already available in the MCY structure. If they are unavailable, the system raises a validation error.

In addition to the above-mentioned validations and features, during a Change Product like an upgrade or downgrade of the multi-currency structure in the TBC:

- The customer chooses a product from the list of products available.
- The eligibility of the customer for the new product chosen is evaluated by the TEP (Temenos Enterprise Pricing) or another external system.

### 4.2  Charges


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Financial institutions may impose charges for maintaining and servicing multi-currency accounts. The types of charges and the events when these are levied are listed below.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Active*, *Activity*, *Adj Amount, Adj Percent, Override Amt, Adj Reason, Expiry Date*, *Amount, Bill Type*, *Application Method*, *Charge*, *Def Account*, *Defer* ... +8 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With


#### 📖 Introduction

Financial institutions may impose charges for maintaining and servicing multi-currency accounts. The types of charges and the events when these are levied are listed below.

- Only fixed charges can be levied at the MCY arrangement level.
- Charges can be levied on occurrence of a specific event or activity at the MCY arrangement level.
- It is possible to schedule the charges at the MCY arrangement level.
- Both debit and credit type of charges can be applied. Regular charges and fees are applied as debit type charges, refunds and bonus are applied as credit type charges.
- The charges are triggered at MCY arrangement level and capitalised to the liquidation account given.

The charges levied on a multi-currency (MCY) account can be settled to:

- The base currency sub-account (under the MCY structure).
- Another account within the MCY structure.
- Another account (which is not under the MCY structure but within the Deposits TBC).


#### ⚙️ Configuration

In a multi-currency(MCY) arrangement structure, it is be possible to levy charges at the MCY arrangement level and collect them from the liquidation account specified.

To collect charges at the MCY level, the Charge Property Class must be part of MCY Account product. The Charge Property defined at MCY level need not necessarily be part of the charge liquidation account product for the charge to be raised and settled successfully. The Generate Charge Activity raises bill in Settlement account to levy the charge. The charge is capitalised to the liquidation account.

The AA.CHARGE.DETAILS of the charges are available at the MCY arrangement level. The AA.BILL.DETAILS are created at the liquidation account level. The bill details are available in the charge details record and is available in the Arrangement Overview of the MCY arrangement.

> **⚠️ Note:** It is recommended that the charge property used for MCY products is not used in other products like lending, deposits and accounts.

The charge property may not be defined in the liquidation account or its product. The charge property is defined only in the MCY arrangement but capitalised in the liquidation account. The system rebuilds the Activity and Balance Types for the charge as required in the Account product line when the MCY product group record is updated.

The features related to the Arrangement Overview screen are not applicable in the Deposits TBC.


##### Charge

The Charge Property Class can be used to define the charge condition for the MCY arrangement. The charge can be of debit or credit type. Only fixed charges can be applied at MCY arrangement. The following are the related fields.

- Type, Currency and Fixed Amount - These fields are used to define the fixed charge.
- Adj Amount, Adj Percent, Override Amt, Adj Reason, Expiry Date - These fields are used when the bank chooses to offer special pricing.

In the TBC, the special pricing for a multi-currency account can be defined and evaluated at TEP (Temenos Enterprise Pricing).


##### Activity Charges

The Activity Charges Property Class can be used to configure charges that should be triggered on occurrence of specific event or activity at the MCY arrangement. The following are the related fields.

- Activity – This field is used to indicate the event on occurrence of which the charge should be raised.
- Charge – This field is used to indicate the CHARGE property that is should be levied. A fixed or flat charge condition should be attached for this CHARGE Property at the MCY product level. The charge can be either a credit and debit type charge.
- Application Method – This field is used to indicate the charge application method. Only Capitalise option is allowed. The charge is capitalised at the liquidation account level.
- Payment Type – This field is used to indicate the AA.PAYMENT.TYPE for the charge. It is not a mandatory field. When this field is not populated, the system uses the default Charge payment method. It is used to link the activity charge payment type to the settlement condition. When specified, it is possible to map a specific settlement account to this payment type. Else the default settlement account is used.

> **⚠️ Note:** Cap and Inv type of Payment Types cannot be used in this payment type.


##### Scheduled Charges

The Payment Schedule Property Class can be used to configure charges that should be triggered on a specific frequency in the MCY arrangement. The following are the related fields.

- Type - This field is used to indicate the AA.PAYMENT.TYPE for the charge. It is used to link the scheduled charge’s payment type to the settlement condition. It enables users to map a specific settlement account to this payment type. Else the default settlement account is used. Cap and Inv type of Payment Types cannot be used in this payment type.
- Property – This field is used to indicate the CHARGE property that is should be levied. A fixed or flat charge condition should be attached for this CHARGE Property at the MCY product level. The charge can be either a credit and debit type charge.
- Method – This field is used to indicate the charge application method. Only Capitalise option is allowed. The charge is capitalised at the liquidation account level.
- Pay Frequency, Start, End, Num –These fields are used to define the payment frequency of the scheduled charge. Read Payment Schedule Property Class for more information.
- Amount, Bill Type – These fields can be used to input an actual amount, bill type for the scheduled charge.
- Defer – This field is used to defer the charge levied for administrative reasons.


##### Settlement

The settlement property class is used to define the settlement account for collecting the charges that are levied at the MCY arrangement level. The charges are set to capitalise in the Activity Charge and the Payment Schedule Condition. The Generate Charges Activity is used by the system to capitalise these charges to the liquidation account.

- Property Class, Property – These fields can be used to specify any other account other than default settlement account for the payout of charges.
- Payment Type – These fields can be used to specify any other account other than default settlement account for the payment of charges.
- Active – This field in the Payin and Payout settlement instruction is automatically set to Yes by the system so that the charges are capitalised successfully. When an account is defined in the settlement condition, the system evaluates if the accounting condition contains the allocation rules for the charge property class defined.

Else, the system raises an error.

> **⚠️ Note:** The system does not allow to accrue the charges or defer amortisation of charges configured at the MCY level and collected at the liquidation account level. The system raises an error if CHARGE is defined as AMORT.DEFER or ACCRUE in the Pc Accrue Amort field of Accounting condition at the liquidation account level.


#### 🔧 Working With

Financial institutions can impose charges at the multi-currency arrangement on occurrence of a specific activity (activity charge) or on a specific frequency (scheduled charge).

These charges can be debit charges collected from customer or credit charges that can be paid to the customer. Only a flat amount can be collected or paid as a charge. The Issue Bill activity is triggered on the settlement arrangement for the activity or scheduled charge to get processed. The defined charge will only be capitalised against the defined settlement account. The Generate Charges Activity is used by the system to capitalise these charges to the liquidation account mentioned in the Settlement condition.

The system updates the base currency sub-account as the default settlement account of the MCY arrangement. During MCY account creation, the base currency sub-account may be created automatically by the system or manually by the user subject to product configuration .

When the base currency sub-account is created:

- Automatically ( by the system) – The system defaults the base currency sub-account as the Def Account . This Def Account cannot be changed during MCY arrangement opening. The charges like new arrangement fees can be collected from the base currency sub account. Post creation of the MCY Account, the user can amend the default settlement account which could be any sub-account within the MCY structure or an AR (Retail Account) account outside MCY structure.
- Manually (by the user) – The system defaults the base currency as the default settlement account Def Account during base currency sub-account opening if the field is blank.

It is possible to specify a Payment Type specific settlement account for different type of charges. When an account is updated in Def Account or other settlement accounts, the system ensures that the accounting condition is available for the Charge Property Class in that account.

> **⚠️ Note:** When a charge is defined at time of arrangement opening, if automatic creation of sub-account is not defined, the settlement account should be updated by the user. Else, charges cannot be collected.

The charges levied on a multi-currency (MCY) account can be settled to:

- The base currency sub-account (under the MCY structure).
- Another account within the MCY structure.
- Another account (which is not under the MCY structure but within the Deposits TBC).


##### Illustrations

The following section illustrates how a scheduled or an activity charge can be set up during MCY creation, raised and settled from liquidation account.


###### Activity Charges

It is possible to collect an account opening fee as an activity charge at the time of MCY arrangement opening. As the base currency account has to be opened automatically, the charge is collected from the base currency sub-account. In the below example a MCY arrangement is created with a debit and credit charge defined during MCY account creation. The following are defined:

- A new arrangement activity charge of USD10 (debit charge)
- A bonus charge of USD 20 (credit charge) is defined during MCY account creation.
- Method is set as Capitalise.

These charges are capitalised to the base currency sub-account.

In the MCY arrangement, the charge and bill info details are shown below.

The debit and credit Bill Details Overview display the charge amount, corresponding settlement account ID and charge property name.

The charges are created at the MCY arrangement level and collected from the liquidation account level using the Generate Charges Activity as seen below:


###### Scheduled Charge

Consider a USD10 annual administrative fee scheduled in the MCY arrangement.

The settlement account gets automatically updated with base currency sub-account.

The Payment Schedule condition gets updated.

### 4.3  Combined Statement


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Arrangement Architecture (AA) supports a generation of combined statement frequency at the multi-currency (MCY) account level. When the combined frequency is set at the MCY account level, the statement generated for the frequency includes statements of all individual AR arrangements.*
> 
> **Applications:** `PRINTER.ID`, `REPORT.CONTROL`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Combined Statement*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With


#### 📖 Introduction

Arrangement Architecture (AA) supports a generation of combined statement frequency at the multi-currency (MCY) account level. When the combined frequency is set at the MCY account level, the statement generated for the frequency includes statements of all individual AR arrangements.

There are no specific differences to generation of combined statements in a multi-currency account using the TBC.

As per the defined frequency, the system hands off the combined statement information to a print carrier solution. These combined statements can be printed using the PRINTER.ID and REPORT.CONTROL configuration. When the printing solution is not configured, the statements are held in &HOLD& folder.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The Statement Property Class can be used to issue a combined statement at the multi-currency (MCY) account level. When the Combined Statement field is set to Yes at MCY account level, the combined statement is produced.


#### 🔧 Working With

The following section describes the process of generating combined statements at multi-currency (MCY) account level.

The MCY account can have a single combined statement of all the sub-accounts under the MCY account itself by setting the Combined Statement field as Yes in the Statement condition.

The MCY account acts as the lead account while the sub-accounts act as participant accounts in this combined statement. The combined statement is generated based on the frequency defined in the MCY account's statement condition.

As per the defined frequency, the system hands off the combined statement information to a print carrier solution. These combined statements can be printed using the PRINTER.ID and REPORT.CONTROL setup. When the printing solution is not configured, the statements are held in &HOLD& folder.


> **Related Applications:** `PRINTER.ID`, `REPORT.CONTROL`

### 4.4  Migration MCY AccountDetails


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *An MCY arrangement can be taken over from legacy system to Temenos' system through the Takeover Activity class. Post migration, the MCY account:*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Adjust Balance Type*, *Adjust Property*, *Base Ccy Product*, *Currency*, *Customer*, *MCY Orig Contract Date*, *MCY Product*, *MCY Sub Account Product* ... +2 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With


#### 📖 Introduction

An MCY arrangement can be taken over from legacy system to Temenos' system through the Takeover Activity class. Post migration, the MCY account:

- Retains its account number
- Is fully operational across our system
- Has its existing product conditions retained in our system
- Sub-account balances reflect as a memo balance at MCY arrangement level

When the user migrates a multi-currency account, through the provided API, the system triggers the corresponding Activity in the TBC to complete the migration process.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The Balance Maintenance Property Class and its configuration are not required for the takeover as there are no separate bills or balances that can be captured during a migration.

During the migration of data from the legacy system to Temenos' system, it is possible to improve the performance of the takeover process by updating certain AA tables through a background service. Read Customer Arrangement Offline Update for more information.


#### 🔧 Working With

The migration of a MCY arrangement can be performed using the MULTI.CCY.ACCOUNT-TAKEOVER-ARRANGEMENT activity. The MCY arrangement and rest of sub-accounts in the MCY account have to be taken over manually and separately by the user for the MCY arrangement migration to complete successfully. The parent and sub-accounts can be taken over using the Accounts Takeover activity.

The capture balance activity should be triggered manually and per account for the MCY parent and existing sub-accounts. All sub-account balances captured should reflect as memo balances at the MCY arrangement level.

The following are the steps for triggering a takeover activity for a multi-currency account:

1. The user defines the following fields using the MULTI.CCY.ACCOUNT-TAKEOVER-ARRANGEMENT activity: Customer MCY Product Currency MCY Orig Contract Date (MCY Arrangement Opening Date) Base Ccy Product field should always be blank in the Multi-Currency Rules Condition for the takeover activity to be triggered manually for each sub-account
2. The ACCOUNTS-TAKEOVER-ARRANGEMENT activity is used to capture the details of the sub-account(s) involved. The user captures the following: Customer MCY Sub Account Product Currency MCY Orig Contract Date (Sub-Account Opening Date) Master Arrangement ID
3. The user triggers the ACCOUNTS-CAPTURE.BALANCE-BALANCE.MAINTENANCE activity to capture the balances of the newly-created sub-account . The following fields must be specified: Adjust Property - BALANCE has to be specified Adjust Balance Type - CURBALANCE has to be specified New Balance Amount

After committing, the system updates the new sub-account balance accordingly. Other currency sub-accounts can also be taken-over similarly using the ACCOUNTS-TAKEOVER-ARRANGEMENT and the ACCOUNTS-CAPTURE.BALANCE-BALANCE.MAINTENANCE activities and specifying the corresponding currency.

In case the MCY account takeover is backdated and there is an activity or scheduled charge in the interim period, the user must update the settlement account manually for such charge to get levied successfully. In case of an activity charge and after take-over, balance capture and settlement definition, the user must trigger the activity manually as backdated for the activity charge to get raised and collected accordingly. In case of a scheduled charge, the user should also update the settlement account manually for the system to raise the scheduled charge automatically.

### 4.5  Misc


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Deposit Temenos Banking Capability (TBC) provides the functionality for multi-currency (MCY) accounts with the following key features:*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

The Deposit Temenos Banking Capability (TBC) provides the functionality for multi-currency (MCY) accounts with the following key features:

- Create a multi-currency account arrangement
- Create and link multiple sub-accounts with a single base currency account at any time
- Define base currency and allowed currencies
- Perform credit transactions for the MCY account
- Route funds to proper currency accounts based on the payment currency
- Supports single or multiple ownership for the MCY account
- Combined statement generation.

The functionality of MCY accounts in Deposit TBC is provided by the following features:

- Creation of a multi-currency account – Supports the opening of MCY accounts for a customer. Customers are maintained in the Party TBC, reference and market data are maintained in the Reference data and Market data TBCs, respectively.
- Sub-accounts in a multi-currency account – Supports creating sub-accounts under an MCY account. There can be more than one sub-account under a MCY account but there can be only one sub-account per currency. These sub-accounts are created on the customer’s request. The sub-accounts are created in the product defined in the Sub-Arrangement Rules definition.
- Sub-arrangement rules – Defines the information related to the customer, currency and product of the sub-accounts created under the MCY account using the Sub Arrangement Rules definition.
- Maintenance of a multi-currency account – Throughout the life of a MCY account, the customer or the bank can initiate changes in the account related information. These changes are handled through the provided APIs and the system publishes events to notify other systems for further processing.
- Transaction Processing in multi-currency accounts – Financial transactions in an MCY account can be initiated from any external payment system. The credit check for transactions in an MCY account is performed at the MCY account level. Based on the currency of the transaction, the transaction is routed to the corresponding sub-account at the Generic Accounting Interface (GAI) layer. The transaction is processed in the sub-account, based on the Activity Mapping setup. If there is no sub-account in the currency of the transaction, it is treated as an FCY transaction, posted to the base currency sub-account. As the credit check is at the MCY account level, it is possible that the debit transactions posted to the sub-account may result in a debit balance at the sub-account. In such situations, the system can be configured to automatically transfer the funds from another currency sub-account and clear the debit balance. When the transaction is posted successfully, the TBC emits an event, which can be consumed by an external GL system, for the accounting/balance updates to be completed.
- Charges in multi-currency accounts – Deposits TBC supports levying of charges on MCY accounts. The charges in an MCY account can be a scheduled charge or a charge triggered on the occurrence of a specific activity or when the rule is broken.
- Change Product – Banks can upgrade or downgrade an MCY structure, by performing a change product activity. When the product of a MCY account is changed, the sub-accounts also undergo a product change to the sub-account product specified in the sub-arrangement rules of the new MCY product.
- Combined Statement - Statement conditions can be configured for combined statements at the MCY level and handed off to the delivery system for a print carrier.
- Multi-currency account closure – Based on the customer’s request or the bank’s requirement, it is possible to close a specific currency sub- account or more than one sub-account or the multi-currency arrangement itself.
- Migration of multi-currency accounts - MCY accounts, along with their sub-accounts, can be migrated from any legacy system to TBC.

Features such as Eligibility, Delivery, Correspondence, and Activity messaging are not supported in the TBC. These are handled by external systems.

- Eligibility - The eligibility criteria for opening a multi-currency account can be handled in an external component, either Temenos’ solution, such as TEP (Temenos Enterprise Pricing), or a third-party solution, such as the bank’s onboarding solution.
- Alerts - Alerts can be configured in the Deposit TBC at the MCY account level or sub-account level, based on the business requirement. The alert messaging content is handed off as an event to the delivery system associated with the Deposit TBC in a preconfigured format.
- Accounting - Deposit TBC uses soft accounting to update the balances for the transactions in the MCY account within the TBC. The actual accounting entries themselves are handed off using the accounting events raised as part of every transaction which could be consumed by any external accounting system which handles/maintains the General Ledger (GL).

---


### 4.6  MultiCurrency Account Creation


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Financial institutions can create a Multi Currency Account (MCY) with sub-accounts in different currencies under the MCY account. The system auto-generates the account numbers for the MCY accounts and sub accounts opened in a MCY structure. This account number can be used by the banks and the custom...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Acc Bkno Prefix*, *Account Mask*, *Account No Length*, *Acct Checkdig Type*, *Allowed Currency*, *Allowed Prd Group*, *Allowed Product*, *Alt Acct Type* ... +18 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With


#### 📖 Introduction

Financial institutions can create a Multi Currency Account (MCY) with sub-accounts in different currencies under the MCY account. The system auto-generates the account numbers for the MCY accounts and sub accounts opened in a MCY structure. This account number can be used by the banks and the customer for all dealings. An account can have single or multiple owners.

When the user tries to create a multi-currency (MCY) account from the front end, the system is configured to trigger the corresponding activity in the TBC to complete the MCY account opening process. During this MCY account opening process:

- The eligibility of the customer for this MCY account product is evaluated by TEP (Temenos Enterprise Pricing) or another external system.
- Currently, the functionality pertaining to limits is not applicable for MCY accounts in TBC.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section orients the user on configuring multi-currency(MCY) account arrangements.


##### Designing Account Number

The user can validate the MCY account number format by the use of check digits or by the automatic inclusion of the CUSTOMER number and/or branch ID.

The COMPANY application defines the length and the check digit type used for a MCY account.

- Acc Bkno Prefix - Defines the bank code prefix which is a part of the local account number in countries like Belgium and Luxembourg and each bank receives a range or a unique identification numbers.
- Acct Checkdig Type - Identifies the check digit calculation method for the company being entered.

The following values are accepted:

- 1 - When the Local Currency starts with BE (that is, identifies Belgium).
- 2 - When the Local Currency starts with LU (that is, identifies Luxembourg).
- 3 - For 10 digit account numbers with a modulus 11 check.
- 4 - For 11 digit account numbers constructed with a 2-digit bank number prefix defined in Acc Bkno Prefix , followed by 7 identifying digits and a 2 digit mod 11 check digit. The prefix may contain leading zeros.
- 5 - For a standard check digit calculation with the account numbers zero filled to the Account Mask .
- 6 - For a 12-14, digit number with two check digits, the first 6 digits, and the second on the remaining digits. The check digits are calculated using mod 11.
- 99 - No check digit calculation, with the account number, padded with zero as per Account Mask.
- @routine name - Where a local subroutine performs the check digit calculation.
- Blank - In all other cases.

The MCY account number display can be controlled using the account mask feature. Account Mask - Identifies the mask that the user wants to apply to customer type accounts. It is a field in the COMPANY table and input in this field must contain at least four # characters to define the minimum length of the account number. It can be up to a maximum length of 20 characters with separators.

The first character can be R, which means that the account number is right adjusted and it can contain leading zeros.

- Mask = ##### - #####. No 1234 displayed as 1234
- Mask = ##### - #####. No 1234567 displayed as 12 - 34567
- Mask = R##### - #####. No. 1234 displayed as 00000 - 01234
- Mask = R##### - #####. No. 1234567 displayed as 00012 – 34567DD


##### Understanding INTERCO.PARAMETER

The following fields in INTERCO.PARAMETER govern the set-up of the branch ID of the bank in the MCY account number format:

- Branch Code Start - Indicates the digit in the MCY account number, at which the branch identification number starts.

- Branch Code Length - Indicates the length of the branch identification number in the MCY account number.

- Account No Length - Indicates the length of the customer MCY account. If the MCY account number length differs from this value, then it belongs to the initial company loaded namely master company.

- Company - Identifies the company whose details are entered in the Branch Code field.

- Fin Mnemonic - Indicates the company mnemonic for the company in the earlier field

- Branch Code - Indicates the branch codes that can be used in the customer MCY account for the company specified in the Company field.

A MCY account number can contain the customer number as part of the record ID. The following fields in the COMPANY table govern the set-up of customer ID as part of the MCY account number format:

- Customer Code Pos - Specifies the start position of the customer code within the MCY account number throughout the system.

- Cust Code Len - Defines the length of the customer number within the MCY account number(together with Customer Code Pos ).


##### Understanding Arrangement Number

The arrangement number is a unique identification number for the arrangement contract. The format of the ID is AAYYDDDXXXXX, where:

- AA - Arrangement Architecture module identifier

- YYDDD - Year and date of input in Julian date format

- XXXXX - A random string generated by the system

When an arrangement is linked to ACCOUNT , the account number and the arrangement ID can be used inter-changeably.


##### Alternate Account Number

It is possible to give alternate account numbers to MCY accounts. There can be account nick names indicated using Mnemonic field. The concept of alternate account number using Alt Id field is used when the legacy account numbers have to be linked to this account, previous IBAN account numbers. The Generate Iban field is used to generate the IBAN number automatically.

In practice, where our system has replaced an existing system, it allows the users to access customer accounts using the old account numbers. In order to allow this, ALT.ACCT.PARAMETER is set-up. This informs the system about the structure of the legacy system's account number (that is, how the legacy account number structure was defined). Once this is set up, it is possible to enter the old account number on the ACCOUNT record in the Alt Acct Type field.

- An index is kept in the ALTERNATE.ACCOUNT table.
- The ID in the external system account number and the single Globus Acct Number field contains the Temenos' system's equivalent.
- If the old account number is longer in length than the existing account number, it is possible to extend the maximum limit through the EB.OBJECT table.
- In the ALT.ACCT.PARAMETER application, alternative account formats can be specified, where the maximum length of fields is up to the number specified in the EB.OBJECT table
- In the Checkdigit Type field, a routine can be entered to validate the alternate account number.
- Multiple ALT.ACCT.PARAMETER records can be created, to allow multiple alternative account numbers.


#### 🔧 Working With

The Multi-Currency (MCY) Account Product Line available in AA allows the financial institutions to offer MCY account solutions to customers. This Product Line allows the customer to set up a base currency account and create multiple currency sub-accounts as per the allowed currency definition at any time.


##### Creating Multi-Currency Accounts

MCY accounts can be created from the Product Catalog by selecting an appropriate Product and triggering new Arrangement Activity.

The customers are defined at the time of the MCY account creation and can be added or removed anytime during the MCY account life cycle. All the customer(s) in the parent arrangement must be the customer(s) of the sub-arrangement(s) within the MCY account.

The MCY Product Line uses existing attributes enabled under Sub-Arrangement Rules Property Class related to the Allowed Customers, Currencies and Products, with the following changes/amendments:

- The Customer attribute is set to Parent Customers and Required Customer set to All.
- The Currency attribute supports all the three options namely, Parent Currency, Allowed List or Any and the user can define the list of Allowed Currency . When defined as Parent, it results in MCY account currency auto populated in the AR account arrangement when currency is not specified.

Allowed Prd Group and Allowed Product store the allowed Retail Account products that can be linked to the parent multi-currency arrangement.

The Base Ccy Product field stores the Retail Account product under which the base currency sub-account creates automatically after the MCY account creation.

Correspondence .

Document and image management is not applicable in multi-currency (MCY) accounts, opened in the TBC. The event that the system publishes for a MCY account opening, can be consumed by an external solution applicable for Document and Image management.


##### Single Customer View (SCV)

It enables the banks to view the complete customer information using the Single Customer View (SCV). The Products tab in the SCV displays a list of all the customer accounts including checking, savings, CD, IRA, loan, safe deposit box. The MCY accounts are listed under the Accounts tab. It enables the user to view the MCY accounts for a specific customer.

The features related to opening a new multi-currency account for a customer using the single customer view screen are not applicable in the TBC.

### 4.7  MultiCurrency Account Maintenance


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *In the life cycle of a multi-currency (MCY) account, the customer or bank initiates the changes in the account related information. The following are some of the MCY account maintenance activities:*
> 
> **Applications:** `PRINTER.ID`, `REPORT.CONTROL`
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With


#### 📖 Introduction

In the life cycle of a multi-currency (MCY) account, the customer or bank initiates the changes in the account related information. The following are some of the MCY account maintenance activities:

- Changing the customer
- Changing the account officer
- Changing the statement frequency
- Updating the limit
- Linking a card with charge to MCY arrangement

The features related to linking cards to a multi-currency (MCY) account are not applicable in the TBC.

When any of the other mentioned changes (that is, changing customer, officer or statement frequency) in a MCY account is requested from the front end, through an API, the system updates the respective details, using the corresponding activity in the underlying MCY account record in the TBC.

- During a change customer, the eligibility of the customer for that MCY account product is evaluated by TEP (Temenos Enterprise Pricing) or another external system.
- Currently, the functionality pertaining to limits is not applicable for MCY accounts in the TBC.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

In an account life cycle, the customer or bank initiates the changes in the MCY account related information. These changes are achieved by initiating relevant activities in the system. Thus, the user can change the attribute values (features) of the different Property Classes in the multi-currency(MCY) account, subjected to negotiation rules, tracking setup, and periodic rules.


#### 🔧 Working With

The following are the multi-currency(MCY) account maintenance activities:


##### Changing the Customer

The Change Customer Activity (MULTI.CCY.ACCOUNT-CHANGE-CUSTOMER) is used to change existing customers or add other customers to the MCY account. These customers are account owners and their eligibility rules are evaluated during the change activity.

The Update Customer Activity (MULTI.CCY.ACCOUNT-UPDATE-CUSTOMER) is used to change or update the other parties of the account. The role of the other party needs to be indicated. For example, another customer can be added as a Guarantor.

Any change of customer in MCY account applies automatically for all sub-accounts in MCY account structure.

- In the TBC, when a change of customer is processed, The eligibility of the customer for that multi-currency account product is evaluated by TEP (Temenos Enterprise Pricing) or another external system.


##### Changing the Account Officer

The Update Account Officer (MULTI.CCY.ACCOUNT-UPDATE-OFFICERS) details are used to change the account officer of the MCY account. This activity helps to include, change, or add account officers with specific roles and change the officers for a group of accounts.


##### Changing the Statement Frequency

It is possible to change the existing frequency (daily, monthly, quarterly, half yearly or yearly) at which the combined statement is being generated for a MCY account by editing the same with Update MCY Account Statement Activity (MULTI.CCY.ACCOUNT-UPDATE-STATEMENT) as shown below.

When a new currency arrangement (AR) is created against a MCY arrangement and if the MCY arrangement’s statement condition has a statement frequency number flagged to produce a combined statement, then the same frequency number in the underlying sub-account arrangements is used for producing the combined statement.

As per the defined frequency, the system hands off the combined statement information to a print carrier solution. These combined statements can be printed using the PRINTER.ID and REPORT.CONTROL configuration. When the printing solution is not configured, the statements are held in &HOLD& folder.


##### Updating the Limit

During the life cycle of a multi-currency account, it is possible to increase or decrease the limit sanctioned for the multi-currency account by using the Update Limit Activity (MULTI.CCY.ACCOUNT-UPDATE- ).

Currently, the functionality pertaining to limits is not applicable for multi-currency accounts in the TBC.


##### Linking a Card with Charge to MCY Account

The MULTI.CCY.ACCOUNT-ISSUE-CARD-ARRANGEMENT activity is used to issue a card and link the MCY arrangement. Any charges for the Issue Card Activity can be configured as an Activity Charge to MULTI.CCY.ACCOUNT-ISSUE-CARD-ARRANGEMENT Activity and applied to the MCY arrangement. This charge gets capitalised to the settlement account as per definition. The MULTI.CCY.ACCOUNT-ISSUE-CARD-ARRANGEMENT activity can be triggered directly from MCY Overview page under the Cards section.

The features related to linking cards to a multi-currency account are not applicable in the TBC.


> **Related Applications:** `PRINTER.ID`, `REPORT.CONTROL`
