### 4.8  SubAccounts


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The user can create sub-accounts under the MCY arrangement for each allowed currency. These sub-accounts are created in the account arrangements created in the Sub-Arrangement Rules of the MCY product.*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.ARRANGEMENT`, `AA.PRODUCT.DESIGNER`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Activity Link*, *Allowed Product*, *Base Ccy Product*, *Currency*, *Effective Date*, *Master Arrangement*, *Product*, *Product Only*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With


#### 📖 Introduction

The user can create sub-accounts under the MCY arrangement for each allowed currency. These sub-accounts are created in the account arrangements created in the Sub-Arrangement Rules of the MCY product.

There are no specific differences, related to the creation and update of sub-accounts under a multi-currency account.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The sub-accounts are account arrangements created in the product defined in the Allowed Product field of Sub-Arrangement Rules of the MCY product. The linkage between sub-arrangements and a parent arrangement within a multi-currency (MCY) account is supported using the Master Arrangement field of AAA. In addition, information related to the connection between the two arrangements is updated in the Activity Link type field .

Refer to Configuration of AR Accounts for more details on the configuration of Sub-Accounts.

Further, the arrangement account product for the sub-account should have the Product Only field set as ‘Mcy’ in the AA.PRODUCT.DESIGNER . This setup specifies that this product is for MCY sub-accounts only and it allows the bank to differentiate between the features of regular current, savings and MCY sub-accounts.


##### Automatic Creation of Base Currency Sub-Account

When the MCY arrangement is created, the system can be configured to create the base currency sub-account automatically. The automatic account creation can be configured by setting up the Base Ccy Product field in Sub-arrangement Rules condition of the MCY arrangement. The product should be a MCY only Product in AR product line. When the user gives this (Base Ccy Product) product in the Sub-arrangement of the MCY product configuration (or at MCY arrangement level), the base currency sub-account creates automatically in this product as part of MCY account creation.


#### 🔧 Working With

The user can create sub-accounts for each allowed currency in the MCY arrangement. On creation of the MCY arrangement, the system can be configured to create the base currency sub-account automatically or manually.


##### Automatic Creation of Sub-Accounts

The system recommends to create the base currency sub-account automatically by indicating the ‘MCY only’ account product in the Base Ccy Product of the Sub-arrangement rules.

The following fields auto populate in the new sub-account:

- Effective Date - Displays the date which is same as the opening date of MCY account arrangement
- Currency - Displays the base currency indicated in MCY account arrangement
- Product - Displays the sub-account opened in the Mcy-only product given in Sub-Arrangement Rules based on the Base Ccy Product field definition
- Master Arrangement - The system defaults this value as the MCY Account Arrangement ID
- Customer - The system defaults the customer and customer role information from MCY parent account

Following the MCY account creation, the system automatically creates the base currency sub-account as shown below.

As soon as the MCY account gets authorised, both MCY parent and base currency account move to Current status.

When a sub-account is created under the master arrangement, the system automatically updates the links between the sub-account and master account in AA.ARRANGEMENT .

The MCY arrangement holds the sub account details as shown below.

The sub-account holds the MCY arrangement details as shown below.


##### Creating a Sub-Account under MCY Account

It is possible to create a sub-account from MCY Overview page. If the base currency sub-account is not created automatically, the base currency sub-account should be manually created using the same option.

> **⚠️ Note:** Until the base currency sub-account is opened, the MCY account is in inactive (AUTHORISED) status.

> **⚠️ Note:** The MCY account and the sub-accounts should belong to the same company. The system raises an error when the user tries to open a sub-account in a company which is different from the MCY arrangement account’s company.


##### Maintenance of Sub-Accounts

The sub-accounts are maintained similar to AR accounts.

Read Introduction to AR Account Maintenance for more information.

The base currency sub-account can be created manually by triggering the corresponding API. Similarly, the sub-accounts in other currencies are opened by triggering the corresponding API.


> **Related Applications:** `AA.ARRANGEMENT`, `AA.PRODUCT.DESIGNER`

---


### 4.9  SubArrangementRules


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Sub-Arrangement Rules Property Class allows the user to define the conditions for the Sub-Arrangements (sub-accounts) created and linked with the multi-currency(MCY) account. Customer, currency and product of the currency arrangements created under the MCY account are restricted.*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.PRODUCT.DESIGNER`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Allowed Arr Per Ccy*, *Allowed Product*, *Allowed Product Group*, *Base Ccy Product*, *Currency*, *Customer*, *Product Only*, *Required Customer*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With


#### 📖 Introduction

The Sub-Arrangement Rules Property Class allows the user to define the conditions for the Sub-Arrangements (sub-accounts) created and linked with the multi-currency(MCY) account. Customer, currency and product of the currency arrangements created under the MCY account are restricted.

There are no specific differences related to defining conditions for creation of sub-accounts using sub-arrangement rules.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section describes the Sub-Arrangement rule conditions for multi-currency accounts.


##### Currency Sub-Accounts

As defined in Sub-Arrangement Rules Property Class , currency sub-accounts can be created with restrictions on:

- Customer – In Sub Arrangement Rules, the Customer attribute should be set as Parent Customer and the Required Customer attribute should be set as All in the MCY Product setup. All the customer(s) in the parent arrangement must be the customer(s) of the sub-arrangements in the MCY structure. When the sub-accounts are automatically opened by the system at the time of the MCY arrangement, the customer information in the sub-account is defaulted from the MCY arrangement. When the sub-account is opened manually, it is recommended that it should have same customer information as the MCY arrangement. Any change of customer in MCY account applies automatically for all sub-accounts in MCY account structure.
- Currency - Sub-accounts can be opened in any of the allowed currencies
- Allowed Product Group - This field specifies the Accounts product group under which the sub-account product should be created. The system evaluates this field at both the product proofing and the arrangement levels . It raises an error if more than one product group is defined for a MCY product.
- Allowed Arr Per Ccy – This field should be set to One for MCY Product line. No other values are allowed and this is a mandatory field.
- Allowed Product – This field specifies the Accounts product under which the sub-accounts can be created for the MCY arrangement. The allowed sub-account product should have the Product Only field in AA.PRODUCT.DESIGNER set to Mcy. The system evaluates this field at the product proofing and the arrangement levels. It raises an error if more than one sub-account product is defined for a MCY product.
- Base Ccy Product – This field indicates the product under which the base currency sub-account should be created automatically at the time of MCY arrangement creation. The Base Ccy Product , if defined, should be same as the Allowed Product defined in that condition. Else the system raises a proofing error.

> **⚠️ Note:** The sub-arrangement rules of an MCY product should not be set as a Product Only property.

Refer to Sub-Arrangement Rules Property Class condition for the use of each option for Customer, Currency and Product.

- The customer number defined at the sub-account level is evaluated against the records in Party TBC.
- The currency details of a sub-account are evaluated against the values defined in Reference and Market Data TBCs.


#### 🔧 Working With

The Sub-Arrangement Rules are used for defining the rules for currency sub-accounts.The following section describes the processing of these Sub-Arrangement rules.


##### Creating a Multi-Currency Sub-Account

During a sub-account creation, the sub-arrangement rules defined at product level are validated and if the validation fails, errors are generated. These validations are applied since the sub-arrangement rules are being defined for MCY accounts and sub-accounts are created under a MCY account as a child arrangement.

The Sub-Arrangement Rules control the below actions in the sub-account:

- Change of customer

- Change of product

- Change of currency


##### Creating a Sub-Account with Base Currency

The base currency sub-account is the first sub-account that must be created by the user. The system can automatically open a base currency sub-account at the time of MCY account creation using a configuration or the user can manually open it after MCY account creation.

The MCY arrangement has the status as AUTHORISED (inactive) till the base currency sub-account is created. If the user tries to create any other currency account directly before creating the base currency sub-account, the system raises an error.


> **Related Applications:** `AA.PRODUCT.DESIGNER`

### 4.10  Transaction Processing MCYA


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Transaction processing against a multi-currency(MCY) account is executed by Temenos Payments Hub. All payments are initiated and processed strictly through Payment Order.*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.PRODUCT.GROUP`, `AC.EVENTS`, `ACCOUNT`, `PAYMENT.ORDER.PRODUCT`, `PP.HEAVYWEIGHTPRODUCTCOND`, `TRANSACTION`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Account Type*, *Adjustment Order*, *Bal Conversion Mkt*, *Balance Conversion Market*, *Balance Conversion Mkt*, *Balance Treatment*, *Balance conversion Mkt*, *Chk Acct Restrict* ... +15 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With


#### 📖 Introduction

Transaction processing against a multi-currency(MCY) account is executed by Temenos Payments Hub. All payments are initiated and processed strictly through Payment Order.

For every transaction on a sub-account within the Multi-Currency (MCY) account structure the system updates a concentration memo balance per currency at the MCY arrangement account level.

The system maintains the memo balances per currency at MCY arrangement account level.

The credit check for transaction is always at the MCY arrangement level. During a debit transaction, when the balance to debit is more than the balance in the sub-account but well within the overall MCY balance, the system allows the transaction.

Such transactions can result in a debit balance or overdraft in the sub-account, then the system can be configured to automatically move the funds from one currency to another within the MCY structure during a service and COB.

The customer can also manually request for an internal position transfer from one currency sub-account to another under the same MCY structure.

The customer can request a payment from one sub-account to another sub-account using Payment Order, but the preferred Balance Conversion rates are not used for this transfer.

- In the TBC, the transactions in a multi-currency (MCY) account or its sub-accounts can be initiated by the customer or user at the payments system, which is outside the Deposits TBC. It is possible to settle the transaction amount with another account within TBC (which can also be a sub-account under the same MCY account) or forward a settlement request by publishing an event to an account or beneficiary outside the TBC. Hence, the payment order related details or restrictions stating that transactions should be strictly generated via a payment order are not applicable for the TBC.
- When a transaction is posted in a MCY account in the TBC from an external payments system, the request is passed through the GAI (Generic Accounting Interface) which routes it to the corresponding currency sub account. The transaction is processed in the sub account using the Activity Mapping configuration to trigger the corresponding debit or credit activity in the system. The TBC also emits an event, which can be consumed by an external General Ledger system for the balance updates or accounting to be completed.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The Multi-Currency(MCY) parent account is assigned with an account number and IBAN (currency dependent - carries the base currency of the structure) and is used as the account reference for any type of transactions initiated by the customer or user. Currency sub-accounts within the MCY account structure may be also assigned with an IBAN.

Whenever a MCY account is created, the system automatically updates the Multi Currency field stored in ACCOUNT application with the MCY parent account number.


##### Memo Balances at MCY Level

For any accounting entry posted to the sub account, the system should be configured to raise a memo balance at the MCY account level.

In the TBC, when there is any accounting entry posted to the sub account, the system emits an event, which can be consumed by an external General Ledger system to complete the balance updates or accounting.


###### MCY Account Condition

The attribute values in the Account condition should be:

- Multi-Currency - Yes
- External Posting - No
- Balance Treatment – Memo (thereby the Account Type in underlying ACCOUNT application is also updated as Memo);

Also, the system populates the Multi-Currency Parent as Yes in the underlying ACCOUNT application indicating that the account is an MCY arrangement account.

For example, when there is an internal position transfer from sub-account to another, the system evaluates for the balance in the sub-account automatically. Banks can levy a charge on the internal position transfer. To perform a credit check on the sub-account balance where the charge is capitalised, the transaction code used to book the charge should be classified as Internal.

> **⚠️ Note:** If the account condition of the MCY product does not have the above setup, the system raises a proofing error. These fields should be set as non-negotiable at the arrangement level.

The Balance Conversion Market attribute in the MCY arrangement indicates a special currency market for currency conversion during a transfers between the sub-accounts. If Balance Conversion Market is not updated, the system uses the regular exchange rate base on the Currency Market in the Account condition.

It is recommended to set Rebuild Balances as yes in AA.PRODUCT.GROUP for all the products including MCY products.

Also, it is recommended that the AC.BALANCE.TYPE for the memo balance of the MCY arrangement namely CUR INF should have Movement Suppress set as Yes and Entry Type set as SPECIAL.


###### Sub-Account

The attribute values in Account Condition should be:

- Multi-Currency - No
- External Posting - Yes
- Balance Treatment - Blank

These fields should be non-negotiable at the arrangement level.

When a sub-account is created under the MCY arrangement, the system automatically populates the Parent Account field of the sub account as the MCY arrangement account. This enables the system to cascade the balances to the MCY account.


##### Credit Check in MCY Structure

When a transaction is posted to the MCY arrangement, the credit check is performed at the MCY arrangement balance level. The MCY arrangement holds Memo Balances at MCY Level that enables the system to perform a credit check at the MCY arrangement level. The FX rates for converting the sub-account balances to base currency balance is determined based on the Balance Conversion Market and in its absence the regular currency conversion rates are used.

There is no additional configuration required as the credit check at the MCY arrangement level cannot be changed by the bank or the user. The Balance Availability condition an be used to choose the balance to be used during credit check. Component based credit check and activity-based credit check is not possible for MCY arrangements.

There is no credit check at the sub-account level. The Balance Availability Property Class is restricted in the sub-account product. That is, the system raises proofing errors if the Balance Availability condition is configured for a product with the Product Only field set as Mcy.

During a sub-account creation, the system defaults the Credit Chk Txn Type and Credit Chk Condition with Internal and Yes respectively. Thus, the system is automatically configured to perform a credit check at the MCY account level except the internal transaction types.

When a transaction is posted to the MCY arrangement, the system also evaluates for any debit/credit posting restrictions at the customer level, MCY level or sub-account level, if the payment order product used for processing the transaction has the Chk Acct Restrict field set as Both in the PAYMENT.ORDER.PRODUCT application.

The system automatically performs the credit check for the balance during an automatic or customer-requested position transfer between sub-accounts and does not require any configuration. It also evaluates the posting restrictions automatically.

For multi-currency (MCY) accounts in the TBC, the transactions in a MCY account or its sub-accounts can be initiated by the customer/user at the external payments system, which is outside the TBC. It is possible to settle the transaction amount with another account within TBC (which can also be a sub-account under the same MCY account) or forward a settlement request by publishing an event to an account or beneficiary outside the TBC. Hence, the payment order related details are not applicable for the TBC.

When a transaction is posted in a MCY account in the TBC from an external payments system, the request is passed through the GAI (Generic Accounting Interface) which routes it to the corresponding currency sub-account.

- The transaction is processed in the sub-account using the Activity Mapping configuration to trigger the corresponding debit or credit activity in the system.
- The TBC also emits an event, which can be consumed by an external General Ledger system for the balance updates or accounting to be completed.


##### Automatic Position Transfer

Whenever the user performs a debit transaction, where funds are moved from the MCY account to a customer account, the system performs a credit check at the MCA level.

As a result of this credit check at the MCA level, when the user debits an MCY arrangement (to transfer funds to another account), the system allows the transaction to be processed in a currency where the transaction amount is more than the sub-account balance. This can lead to a debit balance or overdraft in the sub account.

In such a scenario, the system can be configured to automatically move funds from the other currency sub-accounts to the sub-account holding the debit balance. Thus, an automatic internal position transfer from one currency to another takes place within the MCY structure.

To enable an automatic position transfer, the user must configure the following attributes in the Balance Availability product condition at the MCY account level:

- The Position Adjustment field has to be set to Yes
- The Adjustment Order field has to specify the order in which the funds must be automatically moved from the other currency sub-accounts to the sub-account holding the debit balance. The automatic position transfer takes place from the other currency sub-accounts that are under the same MCY structure as that of the sub-account holding the debit balance.

> **⚠️ Note:** If Position Adjustment is set as Yes, then Adjustment Order must be mandatorily set. Else, the system raises errors. In the Adjustment Order field, the currencies input are validated for duplication and an error is raised if duplicate values are found. The Position Adjustment and Adjustment Order attributes can be modified during the arrangement lifecycle. When the user performs a back value dated change to the value of the Position Adjustment and Adjustment Order fields, the system does not reverse-replay the automatic position transfers which were already processed from the back value date to the current date. The Position Adjustment field is an optional configuration and if the user does not input any value for this field, then the system defaults the value as No.

Only when the Position Adjustment attribute is set as Yes, the system monitors the MCY arrangement for a debit balance in the sub-account and updates a list file namely FXXX.AA.MCY.SWEEP.SERVICE.LIST for the automatic position transfer processing.

> **⚠️ Note:** The system updates the list file when an account goes into debit balance due to Account Debit Arrangement Activity. Therefore, ensure that the payment system has the debit transaction code mapped to a Debit Arrangement Activity Class. That is, this transaction code used in the activity mapping condition should be the same as the transaction code defined in the Debit Book Code field of PP.HEAVYWEIGHTPRODUCTCOND application.

The automatic position transfer is initiated by triggering the BNK/AA.MCY.SWEEP.SERVICE service either online or the service is run automatically during COB. When the service is run, the automatic position transfer is initiated for the items in the list file -FBNK.AA.MCY.SWEEP.SERVICE.LIST by the master activity MULTI.CCY.ACCOUNT-INTERNAL.TRANSFER-ARRANGEMENT. This activity, in turn, triggers the secondary activities - ACCOUNTS-CR.TRANSFER-ARRANGEMENT and ACCOUNTS-DR.TRANSFER-ARRANGEMENT on the sub-accounts based on movement.

The system evaluates the value in the Position Adjustment field when the AA.MCY.SWEEP.SERVICE is triggered and if the Position Adjustment field is changed from Yes to No, the automatic position transfer is not performed to clear the negative balance of accounts in the list file .

> **⚠️ Note:** The exchange rate for the conversions is determined using the Balance Conversion Market if given. If this is not configured, the currency market given in the Account product condition is used. Read Transaction Processing with MCY Accounts to know more on balance conversion markets. Manual reversal of the MULTI.CCY.ACCOUNT-INTERNAL.TRANSFER-ARRANGEMENT activity is not possible. In a scenario where the position transfer has to be reversed, the user must perform a contra transaction which nullifies the effect of the position transfer.

The following events must be configured in AC.EVENTS to perform the automatic position transfer.

- ACCOUNT-CR.MOVEMENT-PAY-INT
- ACCOUNT-DR.MOVEMENT-DUE-INT

Read AC.EVENTS for more details.

The payment order related details are not applicable for multi-currency (MCY) accounts in the TBC.

Any transaction in a MCY account or its sub-accounts can be initiated by the customer/user at the external payment system, which is outside the TBC.

In the TBC, when a sub-account of a MCY account goes into debit balance, the automatic position transfer is performed, only when the debit transaction code used by the payments system is mapped to the Debit Arrangement Activity Class.


##### Customer-Initiated Position Transfer

The customer can request for an internal position transfer from one currency to another within an MCY structure. This transfer does not trigger a regular payment order to transfer the funds instead it triggers an internal position transfer from one currency sub-account to another.

The customer can request a payment from one sub-account to another using Payment Order but the preferred balance conversion rates are not used for this transfer.

The user must click the Position Transfer icon in the Arrangement Overview page to process a customer-initiated position transfer.

On clicking this icon, a model version of the MULTI.CCY.ACCOUNT-U.INT.TRF-ARRANGEMENT activity opens with the following context specific fields:

- Debit Currency - The currency of the sub account from which the funds must be debited.
- Credit Currency - The currency of the sub account to which the funds must be credited.
- Debit Amount/Credit Amount - The amount to be transferred from the debit currency sub account to the credit currency sub account.

During implementation, the Debit Currency, Credit Currency and the Debit/Credit Amount fields can be exposed to the user agents interface with meaningful labels.

> **⚠️ Note:** The MULTI.CCY.ACCOUNT-U.INT.TRF-ARRANGEMENT activity is created as a linked activity from the MULTI.CCY.ACCOUNT-INTERNAL.TRANSFER-ARRANGEMENT activity to differentiate between automatic position transfers and customer-initiated position transfers.

Once the user commits and authorises the activity, the system processes the position transfer by cascading the captured details to the secondary activities (namely, ACCOUNTS-CR.TRANSFER-ARRANGEMENT and ACCOUNTS-DR.TRANSFER-ARRANGEMENT) which are triggered by the master activity (MULTI.CCY.ACCOUNT-U.INT.TRF-ARRANGEMENT). These activities process the customer-initiated position transfer.

> **⚠️ Note:** • The exchange rate for the conversions is determined using the Balance Conversion Market if given. If this is not configured, the currency market given in the Account product condition is used. Read Transaction Processing with MCY Accounts to know more on balance conversion markets. • Manual reversal of the MULTI.CCY.ACCOUNT-INTERNAL.TRANSFER-ARRANGEMENT activity is not possible. In a scenario where the position transfer is to be reversed, the user must perform a contra transaction which nullifies the effect of the position transfer. • The customer can request for a position transfer only for the current date. That is, the system does not allow the user to perform a back value dated or future dated customer-initiated position transfer.

The following events must be configured in AC.EVENTS to perform the customer requested position transfer.

- ACCOUNT-CR.MOVEMENT-PAY-INT
- ACCOUNT-DR.MOVEMENT-DUE-INT

Read AC.EVENTS for more details.

The payment order related details are not applicable for multi-currency (MCY) accounts or their sub-accounts in the TBC.

In the TBC, it is possible for the customer to request for movement of funds between the sub-accounts of a MCY account, by initiating a transaction at an external payments system, which is outside the TBC. In this case, the preferred balance conversion rates are not used for the funds transfer.


##### Pricing Adjustments for Transaction Processing Charges.

Whenever a transaction processing activity is triggered due to an automatic or customer-initiated position transfer, it is possible to levy and collect a charge from the customer. The activity charge condition should be set to capitalise the transaction processing charge whenever the automatic and customer-initiated position transfer activities - MULTI.CCY.ACCOUNT-INTERNAL.TRANSFER-ARRANGEMENT and MULTI.CCY.ACCOUNT-U.INT.TRF-ARRANGEMENT are processed.

A pricing adjustment or a discount on these transaction processing charges can also be offered to the customer by setting the pricing rules condition accordingly.

As an example, consider a charge amount of USD 20 is triggered on the occurrence of the automatic position transfer activity - MULTI.CCY.ACCOUNT-INTERNAL.TRANSFER-ARRANGEMENT.

The pricing rules condition can be configured to provide a pricing adjustment to the charge amount if the activity for automatic position transfer (MULTI.CCY.ACCOUNT-INTERNAL.TRANSFER-ARRANGEMENT) is triggered at least twice.

The pricing rules condition and the periodic attribute record used in the pricing rules evaluation are given below.

The rule evaluation is triggered on assessment. That is, when the activity charge is to get raised and capitalised and the pricing benefit is applied for that instance of assessment. Since the system triggers the MULTI.CCY.ACCOUNT-PRE.ASSESSMENT-PRICING.RULES before processing the automatic position transfer activity - MULTI.CCY.ACCOUNT-INTERNAL.TRANSFER-ARRANGEMENT, the user has to set the Value field in pricing rules condition as 1, even though the expectation is that the automatic position transfer activity should have been processed at least twice.

- When the user triggers the MULTI.CCY.ACCOUNT-INTERNAL.TRANSFER-ARRANGEMENT activity for the first time, either by triggering the service or during COB, the rule evaluation fails as the activity count is 0. Therefore, the pricing benefit is not applied and the entire charge amount of USD 20 is levied.
- When the MULTI.CCY.ACCOUNT-INTERNAL.TRANSFER-ARRANGEMENT is triggered for the second time, the rule evaluation is successful as the activity count is 1. Thus, the charge amount after discount (USD 20 – USD 15 = USD 5) is levied.

Read Pricing Rules for MCY accounts for more information.

For multi-currency accounts in the TBC, the features related to preferential pricing (that is, pricing adjustments or discounts based on certain conditions) can be defined and evaluated by TEP (Temenos Enterprise Pricing).


###### Back Valued Dated Transactions

When a back value dated debit transaction is processed, the system performs a credit check at the MCA level based on the account balance as on current date.

> **⚠️ Note:** For back value dated debit transactions, the interest accruals are updated based on the debit transaction, and the automatic position transfer is processed based on the current balance. If the automatic position transfer is triggered after the interest is capitalised, then the system also considers the capitalised interest while processing the automatic position transfer.

The system does not reverse-replay the automatic position transfers which were already processed from the back value date to the current date when:

- The user performs a back value dated debit transaction.
- The user performs a back value dated change in the values of the Position Adjustment and Adjustment Order fields. The system raises an override stating this.


#### 🔧 Working With

| Sub Accounts | Actual Balance in Acct | Exchange Rate | Balances in USD | Posting restriction |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| USD | 10,000 | 1 | 10,000 | None |
| EUR | 10,000 | 1.1703 | 11,703 | None |
| GBP | 5000 | 1.3748 | 6,874 | None |
| SGD | 1000 | 0.73478 | 734.78 | Debit restriction |
| MCY Arrangement – USD | Consolidated Total in USD | 29,311.78 | No posting restriction at the MCY level |  |


> **Related Applications:** `AA.PRODUCT.GROUP`, `AC.EVENTS`, `ACCOUNT`, `PAYMENT.ORDER.PRODUCT`, `PP.HEAVYWEIGHTPRODUCTCOND`, `TRANSACTION`

## Chapter 5: TBC - TBC_Deposits_Introduction


TBC - TBC_Deposits_Introduction module of Temenos Transact


### 5.1  TBC


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Temenos provides core banking solutions for multiple business streams on a single platform. The various banking business functionality which is supported in the Temenos legacy system, is decoupled from Transact and is becoming available as Temenos Banking Capabilities (TBCs).*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

Temenos provides core banking solutions for multiple business streams on a single platform. The various banking business functionality which is supported in the Temenos legacy system, is decoupled from Transact and is becoming available as Temenos Banking Capabilities (TBCs).

A TBC is one of the discretely packaged business capability, provided by Temenos, that can be deployed as a standalone functional capability. A TBC is an independently deployable piece of software, providing a solution for a specific banking business area. It is a self-contained banking capability that can be integrated with other TBCs through a loosely coupled event-based architecture.


##### Architecture

A TBC is built in a microservice architecture that puts each element of functionality into a separate service and scales by distributing these services across servers, replicating them as required, in contrast with Transact which is a monolithic application that puts all its functionality into a single process and, to scale, you need to replicate the entire monolith.

The TBCs are API driven and operate in a headless architecture. TBCs can interact with the other services, using an event-driven architecture.

TBCs may form part of a solution done in a distributed architecture that manage the functionalities pertaining to a particular banking service using REST APIs. TBCs are developed by decomposing Transact into multiple standalone systems. As an example, Deposits TBC is built by decoupling the components pertaining to Retail Accounts, Deposits and Multi-currency accounts. Therefore, the Deposits TBC acts as a centralised framework for a financial institution for servicing retail accounts/deposits/multi-currency accounts. It integrates with external supportive systems such as Party, Reference, and Market Data TBCs, for retrieving and updating details such as customer, currency, exchange rate, and so on.

The Deposits TBC generates events to update and integrate with other downstream systems such as other TBCs or third-party components. As an example, the events generated for creating or updating an account in Deposits TBC are emitted to external systems, such as Accounting, Statement, Limits, and so on. Each of the events have a well-defined schema in cloud events format and the event names follow the BIAN service domain standards for easy integration.


##### Key Components

TBCs are built on top of the Temenos Infrastructure (TI) framework, which contains the required Transact core modules, on top of which, the required products for the TBC can be built.

- API Framework – The API framework provides the endpoints for CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) operations.
- Data Composer – The data composer fetches the required external data from cache or source systems. It is a common library used within other run times.

- Business Events Store – The business events store is a microservice, which helps to store the data as a series of immutable events over time. Its primary functionality is to record all events that are generated in each of the TBCs. Additionally, it forwards the raised events to the respective TBC. In short, it is a critical component for the infrastructure that stores, orders, de-duplicates and publishes events from multiple services using streaming platforms.
- Configuration Service - A central configuration service that Temenos applications can make use of, to manage configurations through an API-based interface. This microservice supports distributed deployment and provides a stateless API interface. It has a dedicated data store or database to persist configurations uploaded through the API interface and contains the configuration for data composer/data registry as well as the adapter framework. As an example, the MDAL library or XACML library can access service registry configurations maintained in generic configuration service by passing configuration Group Id and the Configuration name.
- Adapter Framework – The adapter framework provides standard adapter functionalities, to interface with other systems which do not support event-based integration. That is, the adapter microservice transforms events into REST API calls by invoking APIs based on events, converts APIs to events, performs debulk and rebulk of requests.
- Distributed Cache - The distributed cache offers low latency as well as persistent access. It uses Redis by default but is fungible.
- Service Orchestrator – The service orchestrator ensures integrity over distributed transactions, by orchestrating events based on the sequence. It tracks the state of the orchestration and invokes participants as required. The participating services are not aware that they are being orchestrated as part of a sequence. In short, the service orchestrator is a saga pattern orchestrator for dependent business activities using command events and responses to trigger the next transaction steps.
- MDAL (Master Data Access Layer) - In a distributed architecture, the data or information required for the operation of a particular TBC, are accessed and acquired from external sources (such as Party TBC) using MDAL. It is used to access vital information required to complete business processing using REST API.


##### Dependencies in Deposits TBC

Throughout the lifecycle of an account/deposit/multi-currency account, the following dependencies need to be considered to utilise the features in Deposits TBC:

- Customer information -The customer information for an account/deposit/multi-currency account can be input from an external system, such as Party TBC. The system evaluates this customer information against the records found in the external system.
- Product -The account/deposit/multi-currency account product is selected from the list of products available.
- Currency The currency of the account/deposit/multi-currency account is evaluated against the list of currencies in which the product is available. It should be noted that the currency details can be evaluated from an external system like Reference Data TBC.
- Eligibility Criteria for the Product The eligibility conditions for an account/deposit/multi-currency account can be defined and evaluated in an external component, either a Temenos’ solution, such as Temenos Enterprise Pricing , or a third-party solution, such as the Bank’s onboarding or origination solution.
- The information related to company, holiday, IBAN and so on, are maintained in the Reference Data TBC. Additionally, details such as currency exchange rates, periodic interest rates, basic interest rates and so on, are maintained in Market Data TBC.

## Chapter 6: TBC - TBC_Lending_Introduction


TBC - TBC_Lending_Introduction module of Temenos Transact


### 6.1  TBC


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Temenos provides core banking solutions for multiple business streams on a single platform. The various banking business functionality which is supported in the Temenos legacy system, is decoupled from Transact and is becoming available as Temenos Banking Capabilities (TBCs).*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

Temenos provides core banking solutions for multiple business streams on a single platform. The various banking business functionality which is supported in the Temenos legacy system, is decoupled from Transact and is becoming available as Temenos Banking Capabilities (TBCs).

A TBC is one of the discretely packaged business capability, provided by Temenos, that can be deployed as a standalone functional capability. A TBC is a deployable piece of software, providing a solution for a specific banking business area. It is a self-contained banking capability that can be integrated with other TBCs through a loosely coupled event-based architecture.


##### Architecture

A TBC is built in a microservice architecture that puts each generic capability into a separate service and scales by distributing these services across servers, replicating them as required, in contrast with Transact which is a monolithic application that puts all its functionality into a single process and, to scale, you need to replicate the entire monolith.

The TBCs are API driven and operate in a headless architecture. TBCs can interact with the other services, using an event-driven architecture.

TBCs may form part of a solution done in a distributed architecture that manage the functionalities pertaining to a particular banking service using REST APIs. TBCs are developed by decomposing Transact into multiple standalone systems. As an example, Lending TBC is built by decoupling the components pertaining to Retail Lending. Therefore, the Lending TBC acts as a centralised framework for a financial institution for servicing retail loans. It integrates with external supportive systems such as Party, Reference, and Market Data TBCs, for retrieving and updating details such as customer, currency, exchange rate, and so on.

The Lending TBC generates events to update and integrate with other downstream systems such as other TBCs or third-party components. As an example, the events generated for creating or updating a loan in Lending TBC are emitted to external systems, such as Accounting, Statement, Limits, and so on. Each of the events have a well-defined schema in cloud events format and the event names follow the BIAN service domain standards for easy integration.


##### Key Components

TBCs are built on top of the Temenos Infrastructure (TI) framework, which contains the required Transact core modules, on top of which, the required products for the TBC can be built.

- API Framework – The API framework provides the endpoints for CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) operations.
- Data Composer – The data composer fetches the required external data from cache or source systems. It is a common library used within other run times.

- Business Events Store – The business events store is a microservice, which helps to store the data as a series of immutable events over time. Its primary functionality is to record all events that are generated in each of the TBCs. Additionally, it forwards the raised events to the respective TBC. In short, it is a critical component for the infrastructure that stores, orders, de-duplicates and publishes events from multiple services using streaming platforms.
- Configuration Service - A central configuration service that Temenos applications can make use of, to manage configurations through an API-based interface. This microservice supports distributed deployment and provides a stateless API interface. It has a dedicated data store or database to persist configurations uploaded through the API interface and contains the configuration for data composer/data registry as well as the adapter framework. As an example, the MDAL library or XACML library can access service registry configurations maintained in generic configuration service by passing configuration Group Id and the Configuration name.
- Adapter Framework – The adapter framework provides standard adapter functionalities, to interface with other systems which do not support event-based integration. That is, the adapter microservice transforms events into REST API calls by invoking APIs based on events, converts APIs to events, performs debulk and rebulk of requests.
- Distributed Cache - The distributed cache offers low latency as well as persistent access. It uses Redis by default but is fungible.
- Service Orchestrator – The service orchestrator ensures integrity over distributed transactions, by orchestrating events based on the sequence. It tracks the state of the orchestration and invokes participants as required. The participating services are not aware that they are being orchestrated as part of a sequence. In short, the service orchestrator is a saga pattern orchestrator for dependent business activities using command events and responses to trigger the next transaction steps.
- MDAL (Master Data Access Layer) - In a distributed architecture, the data/information required for the operation of a particular TBC, are accessed and acquired from external sources (such as Party TBC) using MDAL. It is used to access vital information required to complete business processing using REST API.


##### Dependencies in Lending TBC

Throughout the lifecycle of a loan, the following dependencies need to be considered to utilise the features in Lending TBC:

- Customer information - The customer information for a loan can be input from an external system, such as Party TBC. The system evaluates this customer information against the records found in the external system.
- Product - The loan product is selected from the list of products available.
- Currency The currency of the loan is evaluated against the list of currencies in which the product is available. It should be noted that the currency details can be evaluated from an external system like Reference Data TBC.
- Eligibility Criteria for the product The eligibility conditions for a loan can be defined and evaluated in an external component, either a Temenos’ solution, such as Temenos Enterprise Pricing , or a third-party solution, such as the Bank’s onboarding or origination solution.
- The information related to company, holiday, IBAN and so on, are maintained in the Reference Data TBC. Additionally, details such as currency exchange rates, periodic interest rates, basic interest rates and so on, are maintained in Market Data TBC.

### 7.1  Creating Cross Limits


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *In this section, the reference to limits and limit references concern only the cross limit structure, unless specifically stated.*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

In this section, the reference to limits and limit references concern only the cross limit structure, unless specifically stated.

A cross limit structure has three types of limit references:

- The PRODUCT limit references
- The CROSS limit references
- The SUB-PRODUCT limit references

The limit references that are used in a cross limit structure are different from those which are used in a normal limit structure.

> **⚠️ Note:** The three types of limit references or limits are specified in upper case in this document to distinguish their usage in a cross limit structure.

Cross limits provide a flexible limit structure with consolidation of limits at multiple levels, with the hierarchy of limits linked through the Record Parent field. It is possible to create more than one limit for a sub-product (with different sequence numbers) and attach them to the same PRODUCT or CROSS limit, which is not possible in case of normal limits.

More than one limit can be defined for a SUB-PRODUCT (under a PRODUCT or CROSS limit) to limit the exposure based on different conditions.

Under the

record 500101.1800.01, more than one limit can be defined for the SUB-PRODUCT 1860,

500101.1860.01 for customers 500101 and 500102 (both having liability customer 500101), and

500101.1860.02 for customers 500103 and 500104 (both having liability customer 500101).

This facility can also be used to define separate limits for a SUB-PRODUCT based on currency or company restrictions.

To limit the exposure in two different companies the following

(s) can be entered –

- 500101.1870.01 with restriction for use in first company and
- 500101.1870.02 with restriction for use in second company

Both companies have a Record Parent of 500101.1800.01.

When entering limits top to down, user must input only the PRODUCT or CROSS limits and Temenos Transact automatically creates or modifies the SUB-PRODUCT limits depending on the allowed products ( Product Allowed ) and customers, subject to some restrictions. SUB-PRODUCT limits can also be entered without entering the parent PRODUCT limits and Temenos Transact automatically creates the PRODUCT limits, which is transparent to the user.

### 7.2  Creating Customer Liability Structure


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *This functionality allows users to define a Customer Liability structure by using the functionality of a Customer Group.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Customer Number*, *Group Purpose*, *Key Type*, *Liability Customer*, *Liability No.*, *Limit Product*, *Limit Type*, *Risk Group Id*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With


#### 📖 Introduction

This functionality allows users to define a Customer Liability structure by using the functionality of a Customer Group.

This gives all the benefits that CUSTOMER.GROUP application offers, to the Liability Group as well. The bank can maintain Party Relationships, using a designated Liability Relation. Also, existing validations which allow customers to be part of only one risk group are applicable for Liability Group.

Limit Banking Capability supports creating customer group and its purpose and fetching its details through API. It also emits events for creating and updating the activities of customer group. Customer group is created with the Party and its relation details supplied directly in the API so Limit TBC does not support importing party relationship.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This functionality allows users to define a Customer Liability Structure using the CUSTOMER.GROUP application. To enable this functionality, user must select the ‘Liability’ option in the Group Purpose field in the CUSTOMER.GROUP application when creating a customer group. The user can also define the lead customer of the Customer Liability group by entering the respective customer number in the Liability Customer field in CUSTOMER.GROUP .

The Liability Customer field in the LIMIT application can now be used to specify the customer group ID, which has been defined with Group Type = ‘Liability’. This indicates that the given Limit structure is part of the Customer Liability Structure.

To create a Customer Liability structure, a new record must be defined in the CUST.GROUP.PURPOSE parametrisation table.

This allows users to create Customer Group records with Group Type = Liability. To define Limit records that are part of the Customer Liability structure, the Limit Type field must be blank and the Key Type field must be set to Txn Ref in Limit Products.

For example, the user can set a child Limit Product in the LIMIT.REFERENCE application as shown in the below screenshot.

The corresponding parent Limit Product is shown below.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section explains how to create a Customer Liability structure with an example.

The following image shows an example of Limit Product setup.

After parametrisation is done in the CUST.GROUP.PURPOSE table, the user can create a Customer Group in CUSTOMER.GROUP application with the Group Purpose field set to LIABILITY and a valid customer ID set in the Liability Customer field.

After parametrisation is done in the LIMIT.REFERENCE application, the user can create limit records in the LIMIT application with the above Customer Group ID set in both the Risk Group Id and Liability No. fields.

For example, the user can define the top-level Limit record (which constitutes the overall Limit Product cap) by setting both the Risk Group Id and Liability No. fields to CUSTLIB29, the Limit Product field to 5400 and leaving the Customer Number field blank.

The user can then define the lower-level Limit record (which constitutes the Limit Sub-Product cap) by setting both the Risk Group Id and Liability No. fields to CUSTLIB29, the Limit Product field to 5401 and leaving the Customer Number field blank.

After this, the user can also set Limit records for customers. For example, the user can define a Limit record, which constitutes the Limit Product cap for a given customer, by setting both the Risk Group Id and Liability No. fields to CUSTLIB29, the Limit Product field to 5400 and the Customer Number field to 148968.

Finally, the user can define the lowest level Limit record, which constitutes the Limit Sub-Product cap for a given customer, by setting both the Risk Group Id and Liability No. fields to CUSTLIB29, the Limit Product field to 5401 and the Customer Number field to 148968.

It is the lowest level of the structure that gets linked to a contract. The difference between this type of Limit structure and the utilisation/validation Limit structure is that the Limit check is performed from the bottom way up across all levels of the structure, not just the lowest one.

### 7.3  Creating Limit Products


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Limit Mnemonic*
> 
> **Sections:** ⚙️ Configuration


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section covers configuring limit products and linking them to underlying business.


##### Configuring Limit Products

The LIMIT.REFERENCE application links various limit products to the business application. The ID to this application is the product, defining the product hierarchy which is the second dimension to limits.

Each limit product ( LIMIT.REFERENCE within the system) can be defined as being part of a hierarchy and consists of a

- Global limit
- Product limit
- Sub-product limit

Global limits and their products must be defined in this application.

This application is also used for defining if the LIMIT.REFERENCE requires checking each time, or it is updated for information purposes only.

The Margin Level field represents the percentage ratio between the limit amount utilised by underlying transactions and the value of the collateral available for the limit.

Potential values associated with the Margin Event field are defined by setting up the EB.LOOKUP application with records prefixed with ID LI.MARGIN.EVENT * .


##### Limit Reference ID Change

The LIMIT.REFERENCE application supports alphanumeric key as its record ID. This alphanumeric key allows the creation of an unlimited number of limit product levels within the same structure.

The top-level holds a Validation Limit product, but its underlying Utilisation Limit products can go up to as many levels as the user needs, with a Utilisation Limit product being a parent of another Utilisation Limit product, regardless if it is a part of a shared structure or not.

For example, when creating a new Limit product, the user can enter any alphanumeric ID.

The Limit Mnemonic field supports up to 12 alphanumeric characters. It is defaulted to the LIMIT.REFERENCE record ID, if left blank when validating or committing the record.

User must follow the below steps to create the Limit product structure with alphanumeric ID.

1. First, the lowest level of the limit product structure must be created. Utilisation Limit product 5EDGHU765RE created for study loans. Utilisation Limit product 90SDF3IVS49X is created for car loans. Utilisation Limit product KD034JG0WRL4 for short term loans can be created as a parent for previously created study loans and car loans. Similarly, Utilisation Limit product 9DR56JV3OB81 is created for mortgage loans. Utilisation Limit product LSN435SDV02W is created for construction loans. Utilisation Limit product LF09362VKXTH for long term loans can be created as a parent for previously created mortgage loans and construction loans.
2. After all the Utilisation Limit products have been created, the top-level parent Validation Limit product can be created.
3. After all the Limit products are created and the lowest level products are parametrised accordingly in LIMIT.PARAMETER application, actual limit records can be created and the lowest level of the structure can be linked to contracts or accounts.


##### Linking Limit Products to Underlying Business

The limit products valid for a particular contract or account are defined in the LIMIT.PARAMETER application. As limit products are user-defined (on LIMIT.REFERENCE ), the process of linking contracts and accounts to these products also need to be user-defined. It is based upon any characteristic of the contract or account including the local reference fields (if required).

The parameter defines the limit products that are valid for a contract or account. If input is not made the limit product is defaulted. The following screenshot shows the limit parameter structure.

The following screenshot shows the LIMIT.PARAMETER section applicable to the MM.MONEY.MARKET (MM) application. If an MM contract has a Category of 21077, then the valid limit product ( Product No ) is 3020.

Two limit products are valid for loans:

- A secured loan
- An unsecured loan

The user must distinguish between the two when the loan is entered. If no distinction is made, then Temenos Transact applies a default of the first applicable product.

If the loan does not meet any of the above criteria, then the limit product corresponding to the ‘parent’ product is used. Temenos Transact insists that there is always a default specification for each application being used. It can appear anywhere on LIMIT.PARAMETER . All other specifications for the application are checked in the LIMIT.PARAMETER record. When a match is found, the checking stops.


##### Configuring Standalone Limit Products

Before creating standalone Limit records, the user must first create a Limit product.

5954 and 5955 are standalone Limit products.

- 5955 is for standalone Limits which hold bank’s exposure. So, the Third Party Exposure and (for demonstration purposes) the Suppress Accounting fields are set to No:
- 5954 is for standalone Limits that do not hold bank’s exposure. So, the Third Party Exposure and Suppress Accounting fields are set to Yes:

### 7.4  Intraday Limit


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *When a limit is granted, the functionality for setting up an intraday limit amount in the system is added to the available balance of a customer’s account.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Allow Intraday Limit*, *End Time*, *Start Time*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration


#### 📖 Introduction

When a limit is granted, the functionality for setting up an intraday limit amount in the system is added to the available balance of a customer’s account.

The intraday limit (IDL) is set on the level of the LIMIT record. For this, the IDL is allowed on the level of the limit product in the LIMIT.REFERENCE application.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The intraday limit is configured in the LIMIT.REFERENCE application using the following fields:

- Allow Intraday Limit – If this field is set to Yes, then an intraday limit can be setup on the limit. If this field is set to No or blank, then an intraday limit is not allowed.
- Start Time – This field defines the time of day when the intraday limit amount becomes available for use.
- End Time – This field defines the time of day when the intraday limit amount becomes unavailable.

### 7.5  Limit Sub-Allocation


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Sub-allocations are the transfer of limit amount to or from a limit.*
> 
> **Applications:** `LIMIT.PARAMETER`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Auto Restore Alloc*, *Effective Date*, *Max Sub Alloc*, *Temp Limit*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration


#### 📖 Introduction

Sub-allocations are the transfer of limit amount to or from a limit.

- A transfer from a limit is known as a ‘sub-allocation given’ and reduces the available value of the limit.
- A transfer to a limit is a ‘sub-allocation received’ and increases the available value of a limit.

The Effective Date field from the LIMIT.SUB.ALLOC application now accepts a future date. In such cases, funds from the source limit are booked instantly to ensure their availability when the sub-allocation becomes effective.

The Auto Restore Alloc field from the LIMIT.SUB.ALLOC application now has a value called Maximum. In case of either revolving or non-revolving limits, when the sub-allocation expires, funds returned to source limit is always capped with the target limit’s available amount. If the available amount is less than the sub-allocated amount, only what is left of the available amount is reverted.

Separate charges and interest rate conditions can be set up for the amount sub-allocated from the Reservation Limit to the Utilisation Limit. Besides the existing two limit tiers (one for limit amount, one for excess overdraft), the system has been enhanced to maintain an additional third interest tier for the temporarily sub-allocated funds. The ACCOUNT.DEBIT.LIMIT application has been enhanced with a field called Temp Limit , which keeps the sub-allocated amount. This field is used to derive the interest threshold in the AA arrangement for this amount.

Limit Banking Capability supports creation of limit sub-allocations through API and communicates with different business applications through events.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The user sets the Max Sub Alloc field in the LIMIT.PARAMETER application to define the maximum number of sub-allocations that can be either given or taken from an individual limit. The allowed values of this field range from 01 to 25. Any value outside this range result in an error.

> **⚠️ Note:** The system provides a sub-allocation ID and expiry date in the limit record only when this field is configured. If not configured, the system nets the sub-allocation values based on the date and currency.

When the limit sub-allocation is created, the following logics are used to calculate if the sub-allocation breaches the maximum number:

- From the perspective of the limit giving the sub-allocation, the system considers the total number of sub-allocations given by that limit.
- From the perspective of the limit receiving the sub-allocation, the system considers the total number of sub-allocations received by that limit.

Example for calculating max sub-allocations:

When a user initiates a sub-allocation from Limit A to Limit B, the system first checks the total number of sub-allocations assigned to Limit A. If this number is below twenty five, the system then checks Limit B. If both limits have fewer than twenty five sub-allocations, the system allows the creation of a new sub-allocation. However, if either limit has reached or exceeded twenty five sub-allocations, the system displays an error message indicating that the maximum number of sub-allocations has been reached.

Example for calculating max sub-allocation in hierarchy:

In multi-level sub-product limit structures, the top-level limit tracks the total count of all sub-allocations across subordinate sub-products. For instance, if a limit is created using sub-product 2310 and has two subordinate limits under sub-products 2311 and 2312, any sub-allocations given or received by these subordinate limits contribute to the sub-allocation count at the top level. If the sub-allocations at level 02 exceed the maximum allowed, the excess is also reflected in the count at level 01.


> **Related Applications:** `LIMIT.PARAMETER`

### 7.6  Limits TBC


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The term Credit Limit refers to the maximum amount of credit a financial institution extends to a customer. A lending institution extends a credit limit on a line of credit. Usually, the lenders set the credit limits based on information in the application of the person seeking credit, that is, borr...*
> 
> **Applications:** `ACCOUNT`, `CUSTOMER`, `LI.EXTERNAL.CONTRACT`, `LI.EXTERNAL.TRANSACTION`, `LIMIT`, `LIMIT.PARAMETER`, `LIMIT.REFERENCE`, `MS.EVENT` ... +1 more
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Application*, *Commodity*, *Country*, *Currency*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration


#### 📖 Introduction

Related topics:

- APIs
- Temenos Transact Services

The term Credit Limit refers to the maximum amount of credit a financial institution extends to a customer. A lending institution extends a credit limit on a line of credit. Usually, the lenders set the credit limits based on information in the application of the person seeking credit, that is, borrowers. Credit limit is one of the factors that affect the consumers' credit scores and can impact their ability to get credit in the future. A lender generally gives lower-credit limits to high-risk borrowers because they may not be able to repay the debt. Low-risk borrowers usually get higher credit limits, giving them higher flexibility to spend.

The limits are determined by banks, alternative lenders and credit card companies based on the information related to the borrower, such as

- Borrower's credit rating
- Personal income
- Loan repayment history and other factors

The line of credit is the maximum amount of money a lender allows a borrower to spend on a revolving or non-revolving credit limits.

The Limit (LI) module provides the credit limit or line of credit in Temenos Transact . All the business applications in Temenos Transact refer to the LI module for creation and maintenance of the line of credit facility applicable to the business scenario.

Temenos Transact supports the distributed architecture for several functionalities. The stand-alone systems are positioned as a distinct Temenos Transact subsystem providing different banking capabilities that can be simply hosted on the cloud platform based on the service required by the bank.

The Limit Banking Capability is one such subsystem that caters to customer credit risk management operations. It is designed to work as a stand-alone system interacting with the other subsystems in performing the credit risk management service. It communicates with the other banking capabilities through API in the distributed architecture.


##### Product Configuration

Credit limits are held by customer and product. Simple limits can be defined for a single customer and single product. However, more complex limits can also be configured with multiple levels.

Limits are held by the customer at two levels:

- Individual
- Liability group

Also, limits can be held by the product as 12 levels:

- 10 levels of sub-product
- Product
- Global

Thus, an individual trade can be updated as six limits.

In this example, bank provides an unsecured loan to ABC Ltd of 3 million USD. ABC Ltd is a part of the larger group, ABC International. Bank monitors the limits at both company and group levels. Unsecured loans are a sub-product within loans and the limits are monitored at both levels. Finally, the bank sets a limitation on all business with ABC Ltd and with ABC International, and these limits are held at the global-level.

Consequently, the unsecured loan has updated six limits. If any limit is exceeded, an override is raised during the input of loan.

- LIMIT application holds the credit limits.
- LIMIT.REFERENCE application holds sub-products, products and global definitions.
- CUSTOMER application holds the customers and customer liability definitions.
- LIMIT.PARAMETER application defines the various high-level parameters regarding the application. It links contracts and accounts to LIMIT.REFERENCE .

The main limit parameters are shown in the below flowchart.

Limits can also be set to monitor the exposure against currencies, countries and industries. These limits are monitored overnight. The LIMIT application uses the parameter and product tables to define the structure of limits.

This application defines the parameters that determine the way in which the limit system operates. LIMIT.PARAMETER record can have the ID as ‘SYSTEM’. The LIMIT.PARAMETER application controls the following:

- An indicator to specify if the foreign exchange contracts must be netted before limit comparison.
- A 'number of days' to define how many days prior to Limit Expiry Date and Review Date (can be fixed in the Review Frequency field) in the LIMIT application, the approach of these events must be reported.
- A date and cycle to indicate when the first revaluation occurs and at what frequency thereafter.
- A date and cycle to indicate when a central liability report (including those liability numbers which did not move) must be produced in the back-end process.
- A date and cycle to indicate when the commodity, country and currency reports must be produced.
- A ‘number of days’, administrative Extension Days, define the maximum number of days by which the expiry date of a limit can be ’administratively’ extended before a new expiry date must be assigned to the limit.
- The LIMIT application is defined according to the specific requirements of the bank. The most important feature of this application is that it allows the bank (for each financial application) to define the precise rules applicable to an environment. In this way, the limit verification process can be established by the bank according to a bank’s own set of rules without any program maintenance.

The product group definition that allows the bank to specify the different products, (in bank’s opinion) must be part of the commodity, country and currency exposure.

Creation of Other Record IDs:

The LIMIT.PARAMETER application allows the creation of other record IDs besides SYSTEM. These record IDs can have a valid legacy application (that is, ACCOUNT, LD, MM and FOREX) as ID. The purpose of these records is to move their parametersation, which was initially done in the SYSTEM record, to new individual records for each application to improve system performance.

For example, for the ACCOUNT application, the user can create a new record, which includes all the necessary parametrisation for this particular application.

In Limit TBC, the default configuration for LIMIT.PARAMETER is available in the SYSTEM record. The user can update the SYSTEM record with the limit product configuration applicable to external applications such as Lending TBC. The conditions determine the way in which limit products are used to create limits.

The following user actions are allowed in LIMIT.PARAMETER to configure the limit product used by the external contracts,

- The LI.EXTERNAL.CONTRACT , which is an application in the Limit TBC that stores the details of the external contracts, can be configured as a value in the Application field of the SYSTEM record or as a separate record in the LIMIT.PARAMETER application, to map the limit product used by the external contract or application.
- The contract details and limit product details stored in the LI.EXTERNAL.CONTRACT application are validated against the product configurations in the LIMIT.PARAMETER application.

The list of configurations in LIMIT.PARAMETER that is not supported in Limit TBC is given below:

- Product and product group definition for Currency , Commodity and Country .
- Excess limit check for DDA service.
- Default product definition for money market fiduciary deposits.
- Default account limit for overdraft balances.
- Default product definition for deposit contracts in money market and loans and deposits.
- Default product definition for money market fiduciary placements for information.
- Default product definition for nostro accounts.
- Definition for central liability ledger report, commodity exposure report, country exposure report and currency exposure report.
- Definition for processing the outstanding calculation of forex limit products.
- Setup to determine the accounting type for the balance types specified in collateral code.
- Setup to allow limit sharing group.
- Netting definition for foreign exchange contracts.
- Setup to allow sweeping of unutilized account balances to contingent account balances.
- Setup to define external contract application for correspondent bank limits.
- Setup to define whether auto defaulting of collateral right ID is in limit.

### 7.7  Neutral Revolving Limit Structure


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Neutral limits represent a dynamic limit structure that adapts its nature based on the underlying accounts or contracts it is linked to. Unlike conventional revolving or non-revolving limits, their status is derived from the lowest-level configuration in the limit hierarchy (such as a drawing or dis...*
> 
> **Applications:** `LIMIT.REFERENCE`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Limit Type*, *Reducing Limit*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With


#### 📖 Introduction

Neutral limits represent a dynamic limit structure that adapts its nature based on the underlying accounts or contracts it is linked to. Unlike conventional revolving or non-revolving limits, their status is derived from the lowest-level configuration in the limit hierarchy (such as a drawing or disbursement). This ensures that the limit structure is flexible and responsive to the specific needs of financial arrangements.

For example, consider an AA (Arrangement Architecture) product set-up with the same utilisation limit and is linked to both the facility product and its underlying drawing products.

The above diagram demonstrates a hierarchical limit structure where a facility is the parent entity encompassing multiple drawings. Each drawing represents a disbursement level tied to the facility. The limit structure operates under a neutral revolving limit configuration, where the revolving or non-revolving nature of limits propagates based on the linked contracts or accounts.

The facility limit governs the overall limit, while each drawing has its own drawing commitment outstanding and disbursement amounts. Additionally, non-contingent OS values are computed to ensure proper utilisation of the tracking. The above diagram indicates that the nature of these limits (revolving or non-revolving) depends on the lowest-level configuration of the structure. If the lowest-level (for example, a drawing) is set to ‘Neutral’, this status cascades up to all higher levels, ensuring consistency in how the limits are managed and utilised.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The ‘Neutral’ option in the Reducing Limit field (in the LIMIT.REFERENCE table) is used to configure the Neutral Revolving Limit Structure.

The values available for this field are:

- Yes – The limit product holds non-revolving (reducing) Limit records.
- No – The limit product holds revolving (non-reducing) Limit records.
- Cascade – The LIMIT records of the limit product inherit a revolving or non-revolving nature from its underlying child limit product, which is available for input only when the Limit Type field is set as Validation.
- Neutral – The LIMIT records of the limit product inherit a revolving or non-revolving nature from the contract or account they are linked to. This status is propagated from the lowest level of limit structure up to the highest level. If the lowest level is set as Neutral, the system accepts all the upper levels to be only Neutral.

For example, this can be an AA (Arrangement Architecture) product set-up with the same utilisation limit linked to both the facility product and its underlying drawing products.

The LIMIT.REFERENCE table (as part of the single-level facility linked to a limit) enables the creation of a neutral limit structure across all levels of the hierarchy.

- When a limit is defined as neutral and the linked contract nature is revolving, then the limit inherits a revolving nature.
- Similarly, if the limit is defined as neutral and the linked contract nature is non-revolving, then the limit inherits a non-revolving nature.

The following screenshot shows the Neutral option checked in the Reducing Limit field in the LIMIT.REFERENCE table.


#### 🔧 Working With

To create the below revolving neutral limit product structure,

The lowest level of the limit product structure is first created.

- Shared limit product 1111
- Shared limit product 1112
- Shared technical limit product 1120 with1111 and 1112 as child products
- Standalone limit product 1130

> **⚠️ Note:** The parent validation limit product can be created only after all the utilisation limit products are created.

The neutral status is particularly useful when the bank or the financial institution needs to dynamically determine the nature of the limits (revolving or non-revolving) without rigidly defining them at the product level. Below is the configuration for a neutral limit product structure.

Consider a scenario where limits are created using the neutral limit structure with the initial limit setup as follows:

- Credit Facilities (Validation Limit) is created with an Internal Amount of 1,000,000. This acts as the overall cap or validation limit for credit utilisation, ensuring the total usage under all connected facilities does not exceed this amount. Validation Limit is linked to the facility contract.
- Utilization Limit (Parent/Technical Shared) is created with an Internal Amount of 800,000. This is a technical or shared limit derived from the validation limit and allocated for further distribution on individual drawings level. Two revolving facility drawings are created, each with a commitment amount of 400,000 and are linked to the utilisation limit as shown below.

Consider one of the drawing contracts has utilised an amount of 100,000 USD, after which the limit hierarchy reflects the balances as shown below.

When the utilised amount is completely paid back to the facility drawing, the same is reflected in the limit structure which is restored, as the limit has inherited its revolving nature from the drawing contract.

Unlike revolving contracts, non-revolving facility and drawings are created and attached to the validation limits and utilisation limits using the same limit product hierarchy as shown in Example 1.

Consider one of the drawing contracts has utilised an amount of 100,000 USD, after which the limit hierarchy reflects the balances as shown below.

When the utilised amount is completely paid back to the facility drawing, it is not reflected in the limit structure, as the limit has inherited its non-revolving nature from the drawing contract.

> **⚠️ Note:** The actual limit records can be created and linked to contracts or accounts only after all the limit products are created.


> **Related Applications:** `LIMIT.REFERENCE`
