### 7.11  Update Approved


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Advised Amount*, *Amount*, *Default Advised*, *Default Max Total*, *Internal*, *Internal Amount*, *Key Type*, *Limit Type*
> 
> **Sections:** ⚙️ Configuration


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The Non-shared limit structure uses the alpha-numeric limit keys.


##### Configuring Limit Parameter for Alphanumeric Limit Key

To create LIMIT records with alphanumeric limit key, the SYSTEM record of the LIMIT.PARAMETER application must have Key Type field set to Txn Ref. Further, the Default Advised field must be set to Internal and Default Max Total field must be set to Advised.

If an existing user wants to adopt the alphanumeric limit key, then he has to set the Key Type field in the SYSTEM record to Txn Ref in the LIMIT.PARAMETER application. This still allows the user to use the existing LIMIT records that have the original key type or even create new ones with original key type but with the condition that an already defined Limit product is used, or new Limit products are created with Key Type set to Limit Key and Limit Type field is left blank (in the LIMIT.REFERENCE application).

- Key Type field in LIMIT.PARAMETER application becomes a no input field after record is committed and authorised.
- Key Type field in LIMIT.REFERENCE offers the flexibility to create Limit products that hold limits with either original or alphanumeric limit key. Parent and child products must have the same value of this field, mixed values are restricted in the same product structure.

If an existing user wants to use the original limit key structure, he has to set the Key Type field in SYSTEM record to Limit Key in the LIMIT.PARAMETER application, or leave it blank.


##### Configuring the Classification of a Limit Product

The LIMIT.REFERENCE application enables the classification of a Limit product via the Limit Type field and indicates whether a buffer limit can be extended to a given Limit product.

The Limit Type field allows the classification of a Limit product. It can be classified as follows:

- Validation – Limits in this reference follow the validation limit processing rules, that is, only Internal Amount can be entered and constitutes the parent of utilisation limits under it. Credit check is not performed for limits of this limit type.
- Utilisation – Limits in this reference follow the utilisation limit processing rules, that is, both Internal Amount and Advised Amount must be filled. Credit check is performed on these limits and can be linked to arrangements and contracts.
- Null – Limits in this reference are not part of a structure that holds validation and utilisation limits.

If a

with ID 1100 holds the validation level and

with IDs 1130 and 1180 holds the utilisation level, the following structure can be created:

- Reference 1100 with designated children 1130 and 1180.

- References 1130 and 1180.

The LIMIT application has two similar fields to classify the limit records for the limit types and for the creation and maintenance of buffer limits.


##### Configuring Reservation Limit

In order to create Reservation Limit records, first Reservation Limit products have to be created for them. For this, a limit product has to be created in the LIMIT.REFERENCE application, with the Limit Type field set as Reservation:

Funds reserved can consist either funds approved at the Validation Limit level but not granted to the customer, either funds approved at the Buffer Limit level and sub-allocated to the Validation Limit, either both.

When sub-allocating from the Buffer Limit to the Validation Limit with a future date, funds are reserved on the level of the Buffer Limit in order to ensure their availability when the sub-allocation becomes effective.

#### 📖 Introduction

The Static Data (SI) module handles the static reference data used by multiple Temenos modules, products and services.

Static Data can be deployed as a Temenos Transact module or installed as a Reference Data shared service, which can be referred by various Temenos services through IRIS APIs.

Using the Master Data Access Layer (MDAL), the modules in Temenos Transact can access static data. The details can be accessed directly if the static data is part of Temenos Transact, otherwise the appropriate IRIS API is invoked based on the configuration defined in the MDAL.

Read the Master Data Access Layer section for more information on MDAL.


##### Static Data APIs

Read Reference category available in Temenos API documentation to refer to the IRIS APIs used to create, update, delete and retrieve the Static Reference Data.


##### Product Configuration

There is no specific configuration for this module.

### 8.2  Static Data Information


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Static Data (SI) is a central system to handle the static data and service the requests received from various Temenos solutions. Various banking products expose the static data to front and back office users and customers through online channels.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Min Round Amount*, *Min Round Type and Cash Round Type*, *Rounding Type*, *Use Min Unit*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With


#### 📖 Introduction

Static Data (SI) is a central system to handle the static data and service the requests received from various Temenos solutions. Various banking products expose the static data to front and back office users and customers through online channels.

The table below lists the applications that are part of the Static Data module.

| Application Name | Description |
|---|---|
| CATEGORY | Displays the category codes used to classify the financial products or the type of business operations |
| TRANSACTION | Defines the main characteristics of the transaction codes associated to transactions |
| COUNTRY | Contains the static details of each country, referred using the ISO country code |
| COUNTRY.GROUP | Enables the logical grouping of countries for operational and reporting purpose |
| REGION | Defines the regions in a country or area (EU – Europe). It is used to separate regions in a country that follow different public holiday calendars. |
| HOLIDAY | Defines the public holidays for specific countries or regions, for specific calendar years. |
| DEPT.ACCT.OFFICER | Stores the department and account officer details in the bank |
| EB.ROUNDING.RULE | Defines different rounding rules that can be used in business transactions |
| INTEREST.BASIS | Stores the definition of the different interest basis that can be applied to the business transactions |
| ST.ORGANIZATION.STRUCTURE | Branch |
| ST.ORGANIZATION.CODE | Stores the definition of the organisation units along with their hierarchy details |
| ST.LINE.OF.BUSINESS | Defines the distinct business lines or cost centres within the bank organisation |
| ST.BRANCH | Contains the branch names, if the branch level is defined in the organisation hierarchy |


#### ⚙️ Configuration

There is no specific configuration for this feature.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section presents the applications that are part of the Static Data module.


##### CATEGORY

Category codes (or product codes) are used to classify financial transactions according to the type of business operation or product. Temenos Transact has the following three types of pre-defined category code ranges:

- Accounts

- Contracts

- Profit and Loss

The CATEGORY application defines and maintains the category codes.

Read the Category section under System Tables for more information.


##### COUNTRY

The COUNTRY application contains the static details of each individual country, for example, the name of the country and local currency.

ISO country codes are used as the standard identifiers for this application, for example, DE for Germany and IT for Italy. Dummy country codes are used for entities that do not have an official country code but only have a currency code, for example EU for the European Currency unit. In such cases, the CURRENCY application must be set up before creating the COUNTRY application.

Read the Country section under System Tables for more information.


##### COUNTRY.GROUP

The COUNTRY.GROUP application allows countries to be grouped together to determine the residence or non-residence, when applying charges.

Charges and commissions can be different depending on whether the customer is a resident or a non-resident in the EU. So, the user can setup a country group, which contains a list of all the countries that constitute the EU. This group ID is used instead of entering all the EU member country codes in each charge record.


##### REGION

The REGION application (optional application) is used to segregate a region within a country, where public holidays or non-working days differ from other parts of the country. This enables a separate HOLIDAY application to be defined for the region. The screenshot below displays the list of different holiday regions.


##### HOLIDAY

The HOLIDAY application indicates the public holidays and non-working days for each country or region. The COUNTRY and REGION applications are used to set up the HOLIDAY application.

Temenos Transact (almost on all days) accommodates branch processing and different weekend working across country regions. Every day is specified as working, except for key holidays and weekends are defined by specifying the days in each month.

Read the Holiday section under System Tables for more information.


##### INTEREST.BASIS

Interest basis refers to the methods of calculating interest. It can be set as a default value at the transaction level or allow users to select it manually.

Temenos Transact supports various interest basis as shown in the below table.

| Key | Days/Numerator | Description of Use |
|---|---|---|
| A | 360/360 | Indicates the method used, when each month has 30 days for the numerator and 360 as the denominator. It is sub-divided into methods A1, A2 and A3. |
| B | 366/360 | Indicates the method used when the exact number of days is considered in respect of the numerator and the denominator is 360. |
| C | 366/366 | Indicates the method used when the exact number of days is considered in respect of the numerator and 365 for the denominator in a non-leap year and 366 in a leap year. |
| C2 | 366/366 365/365 | Similar to key C. Read the Interest day basis documentation for any deviation. |
| D | 360/366 | Indicates the method used when each month has 30 days for the numerator and 365 for the denominator in a non-leap year and 366 in a leap year. |
| E | 366/365 | Indicates the method used when the exact number of days is considered in respect of the numerator and the denominator is 365. |
| E1 | 365/365 | This method is used when the 29th day in February (in case of a leap year) is ignored and is considered a non-leap year. The total number of days in the year represented in the denominator is 365. |
| F | 360/365 | Indicates the method used when each month has 30 days for the numerator and 365 days for the denominator. It is sub-divided into methods F1 and F2. |
| F1 | 360/365 | Similar to key F. Read the Interest day basis documentation for any deviation from F. |
| F2 | 360/365 | Similar to key F1. Read the Interest day basis documentation for any deviation from F1. |
| G | 366/364 | Indicates the method used when the exact number of days is considered in respect of the numerator and the denominator is 364. |
| H | 360/356 | Indicates the Hirja method. This is similar to 360/360, but the day calculations use the 360 year (30 days per month) only and the denominator is 356 instead of 360. |
| S | Note 1 | Special (special interest basis). |
| W | 252/252 | Indicates the method used when interest is calculated based on the exact number of working days in a month. The total number of days in the year represented in the denominator is 252. |
| W1 | 21/252 | Indicates the method used when interest is calculated based on the number of working days in a month to be always 21 days. The total number of days in the year is represented in the denominator 252. |
| A4 | 30/360 | This method is similar to other 30/360 methods. It also caters to February month-end, where each month is considered to have 30 days for the numerator while the denominator will be 360 for both leap and non-leap years. |

- Key S is the special interest basis, which allows the interest amount to be entered manually. The amount entered is then checked against the nominal rate to avoid errors and it is checked against the threshold for the interest amount.
- Conventions are when actual dates are used. The convention in Temenos Transact is that the number of days in the year is calculated based on whether the year is a leap year or not. If the start date is in a leap year and the end date is in the following year, then the number of days is calculated as 366 for the days in the leap year, and 365 for the days in the following year.

Read the Interest Day Basis section under System Tables for more information.


##### TRANSACTION

The transaction table contains information about all the transaction codes used in Temenos Transact. A range of transaction codes assigned to various Temenos business module to facilitate their recognition and identification within Temenos Transact. The transaction codes identify important processing conditions, which are defaulted by the respective business application, if not defined at the transaction level.

The EB.ROUNDING.RULE application is used to define different rounding rules to be used in business transactions.

The application allows a rounding rule to be set at application level instead of the currency level. This rounding rule supersedes the one defined at the currency level. The rounding rule ID in the application record is the key to using EB.ROUNDING.RULE . Any transaction from an application that has a defined rounding rule, uses the rounding rule set up, irrespective of the currency of the transaction.

The following settings overrule the rounding definition at the currency level:

- Rounding Type : Ignores the definition in the Min Round Type and Cash Round Type fields in the CURRENCY application.
- Use Min Unit : Indicates whether the Min Round Amount defined in the currency is used. Else, the rest of the rounding definition is used from the Currency record.

The DEPT.ACCT.OFFICER (DAO) application is used to identify each department and account officer in the bank using a code.

An account officer code is assigned to each record in the CUSTOMER application, and it can be overridden at transaction level when necessary. This enables to produce accurate Management Information Reports (MIS reports) at the account officer level.

Similarly, a department code or an account officer code is assigned to each user, which. is recorded in the USER profile and allows a user to be easily identified in the Temenos Transact System. Almost all Temenos Transact applications default the department code from the department code specified in the USER application.

If more than four numeric characters are required for the DAO key, then the user must update the ACCOUNT.OFFICER record in the EB.OBJECT application with the new length.

Branch. Many business functions like product pricing refer this organisation structure.

The ST.ORGANIZATION.CODE table defines the organisation codes for each level defined in ST.ORGANIZATION.STRUCTURE . This table defines each element in the organisation along with its hierarchy details - Parent and Level.

After the ST.ORGANIZATION.CODE records (defined for the branch level) are authorised, the branch records are populated in the ST.BRANCH table.

The line of business is used to distinctly identify different cost centres for the bank and align them later to a particular branch, depending on its construction and requirement. This is defined in the ST.LINE.OF.BUSINESS application, as shown below.

## Appendix B: Consolidated Field Reference


This appendix consolidates all field description tables from across the documentation, grouped by sub-module. This provides a single reference for all field definitions.


### TBC - Accounts_Capability (Accounts_Capability)


**Misc**

| Values in the Data Item field | Description |
|---|---|
| CONTROL TOTAL | Displays the total number of items in the request. If this is provided in the message, it is checked against the number of actual entries in the message. |
| SIGN | When the sign is not supplied in the request, the value in the header is used by default. |
| CURRENCY | When the currency is not supplied in the request, the value in the header is used by default. |
| LOCAL REF | Supplied at the header level and stored in the AC.INWARD.ENTRY record, which stores the header of the CSMBATCH message. |
| EXT.BATCH.REF | The batch reference provided in the batch message (if any) is not only populated in the batch entry in AC.INWARD.ENTRY , but also in the individual ones. For CSM and CSMBULK, this is populated in the accounting entries raised on the contra account and on the accounts specified in the request message; it will be stored in STMT.ENTRY / CATEG.ENTRY / RE.CONSOL.SPEC.ENTRY , in the ADD.DETAIL.VALUE field associated with the ADD.DETAIL.NAME field, which has the value “EXT.BATCH.REF”. |

**Misc**

| Values in the Contra Entry field | Description |
|---|---|
| ENTRY | The balancing entry is raised for each entry indicated in the request. |
| CURRENCY.NET | Balance by currency, netting debit and credit entries, irrespective of the value date. If the entries that are part of an online posting message are netting for each currency to zero, a balancing entry is not raised. |
| CURRENCY | Balance by currency and sign, irrespective of the value date. A consolidated entry is created for all debit/credit entries, per each currency. |
| CCY.VAL.NET | Balance by value date and currency, irrespective of sign netting debits and credits. If the entries that are part of an online posting message are netting to zero per currency and per value date, a balancing entry is not raised. |
| CURRENCY.VAL.NET | Balance by currency, sign and value date. A consolidated entry is created for all debit/ credit entries, per each currency, sign and value date. |
| LOCAL | To raise balancing entries in the local currency irrespective of request currency. Balancing happens by value date, processing date, accounting date, and netting the debit and credit entries irrespective of sign. |
| CCY.PROC.NET | To allow balancing using currency, processing date, and netting debit and credit entries irrespective of sign. |

| Business Event | Description |
|---|---|

| settlementService.checkFunds.fundNotAvailable | Event for a cover request when sufficient funds are not available in the account |

| S.No. | Parameters | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | AC.ENTRY.PARAM | The processing rules related to Generic Accounting Interface (GAI) messages are described in the AC.ENTRY.PARAM application. Nonfinancial option in the Attribute field indicates the non-financial clearing messages and its respective responses updated in the AC.INWARD.ENTRY.NONFIN table. If this attribute is not set, all messages continue to update in existing way, that is, in the AC.INWARD.ENTRY table. |

**Balances and Availability**

| Date | Description |
|---|---|
| Booking Date | Date on which the transaction is booked. |
| Value Date | Date from which the entry is included for calculation of interest. |
| Exposure Date | Date on which a credit entry is included in the cleared balance of an account. |

**Balances and Availability**

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Open Actual Bal | This is the actual non-cleared or ledger balance of the account on the start of a day (SOD). |
| Open Cleared Bal | This is the cleared balance of an account on SOD, which includes the value of all entries (except any credit and reversal debit entries with exposure dates in the future). A future exposure date entry is updated on the particular day’s SOD. |
| Online Actual Bal | This is the actual balance of the account during the day and the value is same as the Open Actual Bal with authorised entries from SOD. Account balances are held in the EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES table. For an arrangement account, CURBALANCE holds the online actual balance. CURBALANCE - indicates the current or live value of property balance and indicates the account property name of a product in the model bank system. |
| Online Cleared Bal | This is the cleared balance of the account during the day. The value is same as the Open Cleared Bal with authorised entries from SOD (except any credit or reversal debit entries with exposure dates in the future). The Exposure Date Splitting feature helps to split a single amount to clear in separate periods. |
| Working Balance | This is the cleared balance of an account considering the unauthorised debits (but ignoring unauthorised credits and future authorised credits). This is the current balance of an account, which is used for checks done by the LIMITS system. During SOD, Working Balance is same as Open Cleared Bal and Online Cleared Bal If the cleared balance is USD 1000 and unauthorised debit is USD 100, then working balance is USD 900. |
| Available Bal | This helps to identify if any movements or transactions can generate a deficit of cash in client accounts, and anticipate the impact of a new transaction on pre-existing client commitments. |
| Open Available Bal | This is the SOD balance that consists of all authorised debits with value date before or same as the current date, along with all authorised credits with an exposure date before or same as the current date (excluding contract entries, such as the principal draw down of current loan value). |

**Balances and Availability**

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Av Auth Db Mvmt | Authorised Debit Movements |
| Av Nau Db Mvmt | Unauthorised Debit Movements |
| Av Auth Cr Mvmt | Authorised Credit Movements |
| Av Nau Cr Mvmt | Unauthorised Credit Movements |

**Misc**

| S.NO | Parameters | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Account | The Account property class is used by all the products which are account based. This property class primarily controls the description of the account. The ACCOUNT property allows the user to define and control balance treatment, posting restriction, linked account number (for memo accounts), currency market, date convention related setup for the account. Although the account names are account specific, generic titles can be defaulted from the product and can be replaced or given additional detail at the arrangement level. Each product defined and processed in AA can have a single ACCOUNT Property defined. |
| 2 | Activity Charges | The Activity Charges property class defines the charges that have to be applied when a particular activity is triggered on the arrangement. The charges so applied can be made due, capitalised or deferred. The user can enable auto settle the charges made due from unallocated credit balance by setting this to Yes. In accounts, charges are enabled for dormancy, settle payoff and ageing. This property class is also extensively used for all AA related modules, charges are set for various other activities. |
| 3 | Activity Restriction | The Activity Restriction property class is used to specify a restriction on a particular transaction. The restriction rules including the relevant periodic attributes and activities are defined in the product condition. These rules are then used to define activity based or property based restrictions. A rule if broken can be set to result in an override or error. A charge can be attached for this and can be set to be made due, capitalised or deferred. For the AR module, activity restriction is extensively used for restricting transactions by number, type, and so on. This is also extensively used in other modules to restrict the user from doing various user activity based on the life cycle status of contracts. |
| 4 | Balance Availability | The Balance Availability property class allows the user to control the following features pertaining to AR module: Notice amount and period, which needs to be given by a customer for withdrawing money from his account. Default Credit Check and Available Balance update related set up. Activity class or Activity specific credit check, and NSF related fees pertaining to it Tolerance Amount or Tolerance Currency - To indicate the grace amount, which is the allowed overdraft before the bank imposes NSF or OD fees. Overdraft Grace Period - To waive the NSF fee levied on the account, if the customer clears the debit balance within the stipulated grace period. |
| 5 | Dormancy | The Dormancy property class allows the user to control the parameterisation of inactive or dormant accounts and movement of the same into various buckets at the arrangement or product level. The same can be controlled based on period, and some exceptions or rules also can be added for evaluation and movement. The user can include or exclude certain activity or activity class for the evaluation. It is possible to, Configure different Dormancy status based on the period of inactivity Specify different charges and charging frequency for each Dormancy status Apply some exception rule filtering at an individual arrangement level (for example, account is in debit balance) and such rules can either be an API or a rule created using the Rules Engine Specify notices and notice frequency for each Dormancy status Specify Activities or Activity Classes or Activity Initiation Types which are qualified to keep an account active. Auto Reset can be enabled based on status or on Activity Type. |
| 6 | Facility | The Facility is a service component for financial products designed using arrangement architecture. The Facility property class controls the list of available services for an arrangement account. When an external activity (financial or non-financial) is triggered and the corresponding service group is mapped to an activity through Activity Mapping and EB.EVENTS . And the same came allowed or restricted or charged corresponding error message is raised to stop the activity. |
| 7 | Inheritance | The Inheritance property class is used for BN pool structure for inheriting the product conditions set at Parent level arrangement to the Child level arrangement accounts. The product conditions that are set for inheritance are attached to Property records with type as Inheritance Only. The properties to be inherited can be controlled both at source and target level. |
| 8 | Interest | The Interest property class is used for all interest definition and processing in AA. A product defined and processed in AA can have multiple interest properties defined (for example, principal interest, penalty interest, commission, etc. Interest rates can be defined as fixed , floating , periodic or linked rate (referring an INTEREST property from other arrangement), routine based calculation. Tiered interest can also be defined. Further it is possible to define a negative rate, minimum interest amount and waive the interest. Interest adjustment can be done in run time, and adjustment related detail or values can be captured in adjustment related fields. |
| 9 | Limit | The Limit property class primarily controls the use of LIMIT module by the product. We can set up single or shared limit. We can define the LIMIT.REFERENCE applicable for a specific product such that the system defaults the same in an arrangement. For a new limit, at the arrangement level, the LIMIT.SERIAL has to be given as NEW. The AR module can have self-contained secondary limit without having actual limit attached to it. Overdraft status or notice for AR module is handled inside the Limit Property class. Further Limits can be set to use the LIMIT module (AL and AD) or it can be managed only within the arrangement architecture framework. |
| 10 | Payment Schedule | The Payment Schedule property class is used by all products which have amounts billed (that is,made due) or capitalised or Pay. A Payment Schedule can be comprised of one or more payment definitions with conditions such as payment Type and Method, arrangement properties, dates and amounts. The AA.PAYMENT.TYPE application is used to define the standard payment types such as constant, linear, actual and fixed equal and so on, that can be used by a product. This payment type is then attached to each payment schedule definition. The start and end date can be specified, the user can specify the repayment of arrangement to commence after ‘n’ months from the arrangement date or ‘n’ months before the maturity or ‘n’ months after the change product or reset and rollover has happened. |
| 11 | Periodic Charges | The Periodic Charges property class acts as a container to group different charge properties and calculate a periodic charge amount. The Payment Schedule property class drives this property class. A periodic charge property can be attached in payment schedule and on schedule date periodic charge amount is calculated. At the arrangement level adjustment can be done by the user on whole periodic charge. |
| 12 | Statement | The Statement property class is used to define the legacy ACCT.STATEMENT feature at the AA level. Statements may be produced daily (every working day), every 1-9 weeks, twice a month (on the 15th and the last day of the month) or every 1-12 months on any day of the month. Up to nine statement cycles may be specified for each account, and each statement cycle is independent. In addition to this, special interim statements can be enabled. This property class also controls whether or not advices are to be produced when interest and charges are applied, and whether detailed interest statements (interest scale) should be produced. Within a statement cycle, it is possible to define multiple frequencies with a combination of weekly and monthly, such that statements are produced on the dates specified by both frequencies, but only contain details of entries since the last statement in that cycle. |

**Misc**

| S.No | Product Name | Product Attributes |

**Misc**

| S.NO | Parameters | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Account | The Account property class is used by all the products which are account based. This property class primarily controls the description of the account. The ACCOUNT property allows the user to define and control balance treatment, posting restriction, linked account number (for memo accounts), currency market, date convention related setup for the account. Although the account names are account specific, generic titles can be defaulted from the product and can be replaced or given additional detail at the arrangement level. Each product defined and processed in AA can have a single ACCOUNT Property defined. |
| 2 | Activity Charges | The Activity Charges property class defines the charges that have to be applied when a particular activity is triggered on the arrangement. The charges so applied can be made due, capitalised or deferred. The user can enable auto settle the charges made due from unallocated credit balance by setting this to Yes. In accounts, charges are enabled for dormancy, settle payoff and ageing. This property class is also extensively used for all AA related modules, charges are set for various other activities. |
| 3 | Activity Restriction | The Activity Restriction property class is used to specify a restriction on a particular transaction. The restriction rules including the relevant periodic attributes and activities are defined in the product condition. These rules are then used to define activity based or property based restrictions. A rule if broken can be set to result in an override or error. A charge can be attached for this and can be set to be made due, capitalised or deferred. For the AR module, activity restriction is extensively used for restricting transactions by number, type, and so on. This is also extensively used in other modules to restrict the user from doing various user activity based on the life cycle status of contracts. |
| 4 | Balance Availability | The Balance Availability property class allows the user to control the following features pertaining to AR module: Notice amount and period, which needs to be given by a customer for withdrawing money from his account. Default Credit Check and Available Balance update related set up. Activity class or Activity specific credit check, and NSF related fees pertaining to it Tolerance Amount or Tolerance Currency - To indicate the grace amount, which is the allowed overdraft before the bank imposes NSF or OD fees. Overdraft Grace Period - To waive the NSF fee levied on the account, if the customer clears the debit balance within the stipulated grace period. |
| 5 | Dormancy | The Dormancy property class allows the user to control the parameterisation of inactive or dormant accounts and movement of the same into various buckets at the arrangement or product level. The same can be controlled based on period, and some exceptions or rules also can be added for evaluation and movement. The user can include or exclude certain activity or activity class for the evaluation. It is possible to, Configure different Dormancy status based on the period of inactivity Specify different charges and charging frequency for each Dormancy status Apply some exception rule filtering at an individual arrangement level (for example, account is in debit balance) and such rules can either be an API or a rule created using the Rules Engine Specify notices and notice frequency for each Dormancy status Specify Activities or Activity Classes or Activity Initiation Types which are qualified to keep an account active. Auto Reset can be enabled based on status or on Activity Type. |
| 6 | Facility | The Facility is a service component for financial products designed using arrangement architecture. The Facility property class controls the list of available services for an arrangement account. When an external activity (financial or non-financial) is triggered and the corresponding service group is mapped to an activity through Activity Mapping and EB.EVENTS . And the same came allowed or restricted or charged corresponding error message is raised to stop the activity. |
| 7 | Inheritance | The Inheritance property class is used for BN pool structure for inheriting the product conditions set at Parent level arrangement to the Child level arrangement accounts. The product conditions that are set for inheritance are attached to Property records with type as Inheritance Only. The properties to be inherited can be controlled both at source and target level. |
| 8 | Interest | The Interest property class is used for all interest definition and processing in AA. A product defined and processed in AA can have multiple interest properties defined (for example, principal interest, penalty interest, commission, etc. Interest rates can be defined as fixed , floating , periodic or linked rate (referring an INTEREST property from other arrangement), routine based calculation. Tiered interest can also be defined. Further it is possible to define a negative rate, minimum interest amount and waive the interest. Interest adjustment can be done in run time, and adjustment related detail or values can be captured in adjustment related fields. |
| 9 | Limit | The Limit property class primarily controls the use of LIMIT module by the product. We can set up single or shared limit. We can define the LIMIT.REFERENCE applicable for a specific product such that the system defaults the same in an arrangement. For a new limit, at the arrangement level, the LIMIT.SERIAL has to be given as NEW. The AR module can have self-contained secondary limit without having actual limit attached to it. Overdraft status or notice for AR module is handled inside the Limit Property class. Further Limits can be set to use the LIMIT module (AL and AD) or it can be managed only within the arrangement architecture framework. |
| 10 | Payment Schedule | The Payment Schedule property class is used by all products which have amounts billed (that is,made due) or capitalised or Pay. A Payment Schedule can be comprised of one or more payment definitions with conditions such as payment Type and Method, arrangement properties, dates and amounts. The AA.PAYMENT.TYPE application is used to define the standard payment types such as constant, linear, actual and fixed equal and so on, that can be used by a product. This payment type is then attached to each payment schedule definition. The start and end date can be specified, the user can specify the repayment of arrangement to commence after ‘n’ months from the arrangement date or ‘n’ months before the maturity or ‘n’ months after the change product or reset and rollover has happened. |
| 11 | Periodic Charges | The Periodic Charges property class acts as a container to group different charge properties and calculate a periodic charge amount. The Payment Schedule property class drives this property class. A periodic charge property can be attached in payment schedule and on schedule date periodic charge amount is calculated. At the arrangement level adjustment can be done by the user on whole periodic charge. |
| 12 | Statement | The Statement property class is used to define the legacy ACCT.STATEMENT feature at the AA level. Statements may be produced daily (every working day), every 1-9 weeks, twice a month (on the 15th and the last day of the month) or every 1-12 months on any day of the month. Up to nine statement cycles may be specified for each account, and each statement cycle is independent. In addition to this, special interim statements can be enabled. This property class also controls whether or not advices are to be produced when interest and charges are applied, and whether detailed interest statements (interest scale) should be produced. Within a statement cycle, it is possible to define multiple frequencies with a combination of weekly and monthly, such that statements are produced on the dates specified by both frequencies, but only contain details of entries since the last statement in that cycle. |

**Static Data Information**

| Application Name | Description |
|---|---|
| CATEGORY | Displays the category codes used to classify the financial products or the type of business operations |
| TRANSACTION | Defines the main characteristics of the transaction codes associated to transactions |
| COUNTRY | Contains the static details of each country, referred using the ISO country code |
| COUNTRY.GROUP | Enables the logical grouping of countries for operational and reporting purpose |
| REGION | Defines the regions in a country or area (EU – Europe). It is used to separate regions in a country that follow different public holiday calendars. |
| HOLIDAY | Defines the public holidays for specific countries or regions, for specific calendar years. |
| DEPT.ACCT.OFFICER | Stores the department and account officer details in the bank |
| EB.ROUNDING.RULE | Defines different rounding rules that can be used in business transactions |
| INTEREST.BASIS | Stores the definition of the different interest basis that can be applied to the business transactions |
| ST.ORGANIZATION.STRUCTURE | Branch |
| ST.ORGANIZATION.CODE | Stores the definition of the organisation units along with their hierarchy details |
| ST.LINE.OF.BUSINESS | Defines the distinct business lines or cost centres within the bank organisation |
| ST.BRANCH | Contains the branch names, if the branch level is defined in the organisation hierarchy |

**Static Data Information**

| Key | Days/Numerator | Description of Use |
|---|---|---|
| A | 360/360 | Indicates the method used, when each month has 30 days for the numerator and 360 as the denominator. It is sub-divided into methods A1, A2 and A3. |
| B | 366/360 | Indicates the method used when the exact number of days is considered in respect of the numerator and the denominator is 360. |
| C | 366/366 | Indicates the method used when the exact number of days is considered in respect of the numerator and 365 for the denominator in a non-leap year and 366 in a leap year. |
| C2 | 366/366 365/365 | Similar to key C. Read the Interest day basis documentation for any deviation. |
| D | 360/366 | Indicates the method used when each month has 30 days for the numerator and 365 for the denominator in a non-leap year and 366 in a leap year. |
| E | 366/365 | Indicates the method used when the exact number of days is considered in respect of the numerator and the denominator is 365. |
| E1 | 365/365 | This method is used when the 29th day in February (in case of a leap year) is ignored and is considered a non-leap year. The total number of days in the year represented in the denominator is 365. |
| F | 360/365 | Indicates the method used when each month has 30 days for the numerator and 365 days for the denominator. It is sub-divided into methods F1 and F2. |
| F1 | 360/365 | Similar to key F. Read the Interest day basis documentation for any deviation from F. |
| F2 | 360/365 | Similar to key F1. Read the Interest day basis documentation for any deviation from F1. |
| G | 366/364 | Indicates the method used when the exact number of days is considered in respect of the numerator and the denominator is 364. |
| H | 360/356 | Indicates the Hirja method. This is similar to 360/360, but the day calculations use the 360 year (30 days per month) only and the denominator is 356 instead of 360. |
| S | Note 1 | Special (special interest basis). |
| W | 252/252 | Indicates the method used when interest is calculated based on the exact number of working days in a month. The total number of days in the year represented in the denominator is 252. |
| W1 | 21/252 | Indicates the method used when interest is calculated based on the number of working days in a month to be always 21 days. The total number of days in the year is represented in the denominator 252. |
| A4 | 30/360 | This method is similar to other 30/360 methods. It also caters to February month-end, where each month is considered to have 30 days for the numerator while the denominator will be 360 for both leap and non-leap years. |
